text:
Knack Packaging Ltd - Q2 FY27 Results

Key Highlights -
- Q2 FY27 revenue grew 52.5% YoY to ₹294.8 Cr. EBITDA increased 29.9% to ₹49.8 Cr, while PAT grew 21.2% to ₹25 Cr.
- EBITDA margin declined to 16.35% from 19.25% last year due to a sharp increase in polypropylene prices and higher freight costs.
- H1 FY27 revenue grew 47.2% to ₹569.1 Cr. EBITDA increased 41.5% to ₹108.9 Cr, while PAT rose 34.5% to ₹55.6 Cr.
- Growth was driven by higher export volumes, increased business from existing customers, new international accounts and capacity ramp-up.
- The company serves more than 2,040 customers across 75 countries and has 13,974 SKUs.
- Management expects margins to improve from Q3 FY27 as customer price revisions take effect, although complete recovery will depend on raw material prices and the extent of cost pass-through.

Financial Performance -
Q2 FY27:
- Revenue: ₹294.8 Cr, up 52.5% YoY.
- EBITDA: ₹49.8 Cr, up 29.9% YoY.
- EBITDA margin: 16.35% versus 19.25% last year.
- PAT: ₹25 Cr, up 21.2% YoY.
- PAT margin: 8.22% versus 10.34% last year.

H1 FY27:
- Revenue: ₹569.1 Cr, up 47.2% YoY.
- EBITDA: ₹108.9 Cr, up 41.5% YoY.
- EBITDA margin: 19.14% versus 19.91% last year.
- PAT: ₹55.6 Cr, up 34.5% YoY.
- PAT margin: 9.76% versus 10.68% last year.

The Mexico JV contributed a loss of ₹6.1 Cr in H1, including ₹2.6 Cr in Q2, which affected consolidated profitability.

Business Performance and Demand -
- Exports remain a major growth driver, with the company selling across 75 countries and six continents.
- Growth is coming from existing global FMCG, pet food and agricultural customers, along with new international accounts.
- The company works across more than 25 industries, including food, pet nutrition, fertilisers, rice, grains, pulses, cement and seeds.
- Management highlighted increasing demand for premium printed laminated woven polypropylene bags and pinch-bottom bags.
- Customers are gradually shifting from regular woven bags to higher-value laminated and pinch-bottom bags. This increases value addition without requiring the same level of additional fabric-manufacturing capacity.
- Management also sees an opportunity to replace paper packaging with polypropylene woven bags, particularly where paper prices and availability are challenging.

New International Order -
- In October 2026, Knack announced a three-year contract renewal with an international pet food and animal nutrition customer.
- The contract is worth approximately ₹150 Cr annually.
- The customer currently operates across more than 100 countries, while Knack serves only a portion of its markets.
- Management sees scope to increase volumes by adding more countries and products, including opportunities to replace the customer's existing paper packaging.

Capacity and Utilisation -
- Existing manufacturing capacity was approximately 42,000 tonnes annually, with management indicating that it was operating at around 39,000–40,000 tonnes.
- Overall plant utilisation was approximately 90–91%, limiting the scope for substantial volume growth until additional capacity ramps up.
- Q2 production was 11,252 tonnes, up approximately 13–14% YoY and 3% sequentially.
- A new facility with approximately 5,040 tonnes of additional capacity was added in August. Management expects it to reach around 50% utilisation during Q3, supporting higher production and sales.
- Total installed capacity is expected to increase to approximately 69,000–72,000 tonnes after the next expansion phase, targeted by October 2027.
- Management is also exploring ways to increase production before the full expansion is completed.

Pinch-Bottom Bags -
- Pinch-bottom bags contributed around 21% of revenue, compared with approximately 17–18% previously, according to management.
- The two recently added machines were operating at approximately 60–70% utilisation and are still ramping up.
- The rice season is expected to support demand and utilisation in Q3 and Q4.
- The company plans to convert more existing customers from regular laminated woven bags to pinch-bottom bags, which offer higher value addition.
- Management indicated that the expanded facility could eventually have around 32,000 tonnes of pinch-bottom bag capacity, with an initial target of approximately 25,000–30,000 tonnes as the business scales.
- Two additional pinch-bottom machines are expected to arrive around October 2027, given the long machinery delivery timelines.

Margins and Raw Material Costs -
- Polypropylene prices increased sharply during Q2, with management describing price movements of around 25–30% over a short period.
- The company was unable to pass on the entire increase immediately because customer pricing and order delivery operate with a time lag.
- Around 45–50% of customers operate under contracts with monthly or quarterly price revisions. Since production and delivery take approximately 1–1.5 months, the effective pass-through can take around 3–4.5 months.
- The impact of higher raw material prices reduced gross margin by approximately 7 percentage points, according to management's response during the call.
- Management expects a better Q3, supported by pricing revisions, seasonal demand and the shift towards pinch-bottom bags.
- However, management acknowledged that it may not recover the entire margin decline in one quarter and that the extent of recovery depends on market conditions and negotiations with customers.
- Investors should track absolute EBITDA per kg as well as percentage margins, because raw material inflation can increase reported revenue without a corresponding increase in manufacturing contribution.

Mexico Joint Venture -
- The Scion Knack JV in Mexico is in the ramp-up phase and continues to affect consolidated earnings.
- Management indicated installed capacity of around 400 tonnes per month.
- Monthly sales were approximately 80 tonnes in the previous quarter, with management indicating a potential move towards 100–120 tonnes.
- Management expects the JV to approach breakeven around Q3 FY27, with approximately 120–130 tonnes per month described as the breakeven level.
- The improvement in Mexico is important because the JV's current losses are reducing consolidated PAT without yet contributing meaningfully to group earnings.

Cash Flow and Balance Sheet -
- The debt-to-equity ratio improved to 0.26x from 0.68x a year earlier.
- The working capital cycle was 75 days compared with 76 days in Q2 FY26.
- Management explained that higher inventory requirements and increased export receivables affected operating cash flow, as export collections generally take longer than domestic collections.
- Higher tax payments and deferred tax effects also influenced the reported cash flow.
- Cash conversion needs to be monitored alongside revenue and profit growth, particularly as export volumes and capacity expand.

Our View -
Knack Packaging has delivered strong growth in revenue and EBITDA, supported by export demand, deeper customer relationships and increasing volumes. Its presence across several industries and long-standing customer relationships provide a base for further growth.

The main concern this quarter is margin pressure. Polypropylene prices rose faster than the company could revise customer prices, resulting in a decline in EBITDA margin despite strong revenue growth. Management expects improvement from Q3, but a complete recovery is not guaranteed in one quarter.

The shift towards pinch-bottom bags is an important part of the growth strategy. It allows Knack to move customers towards higher-value products, improve product mix and generate better contribution from its existing manufacturing base. However, customer conversion takes time, and the new machines are still ramping up.

The capacity expansion provides room for future growth, but execution and utilisation will matter. The Mexico JV is another important monitorable, as reaching breakeven would reduce the drag on consolidated profitability.

Overall, demand and customer additions look encouraging. The key question is whether the company can convert this growth into sustainable EBITDA per kg, stronger margins and better cash generation while managing the next phase of capacity expansion.

Key Monitorables -
1. Recovery in EBITDA margin from Q3 FY27 as customer price revisions take effect.
2. EBITDA per kg and gross contribution as polypropylene prices fluctuate.
3. Utilisation and ramp-up of the new 5,040-tonne capacity.
4. Growth in pinch-bottom bags and the pace of customer conversion.
5. Execution of the three-year international contract worth approximately ₹150 Cr annually.
6. Progress towards the planned capacity of 69,000–72,000 tonnes by October 2027.
7. Mexico JV volumes and progress towards monthly breakeven sales of approximately 120–130 tonnes.
8. Operating cash flow, export receivables and working capital requirements.
9. Whether higher revenue translates into sustainable profit growth rather than being driven mainly by higher raw material prices.

text:
ICYMI O/N — THURSDAY 29 OCTOBER

MACRO:

Nasdaq 100 futures fell 1.1% and S&P futures 0.3% following Microsoft, Alphabet and Samsung results. The Kospi was down 1.2% after Wednesday’s sharp rally. (BBG)

Wall Street rewarded Microsoft and Oracle on Wednesday for showing that they could fund their enormous AI ambitions without endlessly tapping investors. Alphabet, by contrast, was punished for burning through cash, while Google Search's slower growth fanned fears that competition was hurting the business that bankrolls its AI expansion. (RTRS)

Bessent said another Fed hike would not necessarily be a mistake given strong growth, while urging an open mind about the energy shock proving temporary. He reiterated his and Trump’s confidence in Warsh. (BBG)

Bessent played down AI-credit fears, saying neoclouds are a small part of the ecosystem and financing is still occurring. He pointed to Meta’s equity funding and said Treasury is monitoring developments. (BBG)

Timiraos argues Warsh’s view that rates are reaching the AI boom could imply fewer hikes, while broader economic strength points the other way. TD and BofA criticised his explanation for waiting until December as insufficiently clear. (WSJ)

Global bond issuance has reached an annual record $6.61tn, up 15%. Cloud and data-centre borrowers raised almost $368bn—over six times the prior-year amount—and accounted for about one-third of the increase. (BBG)

'Bitcoin Traders Expect Swings on $11 Billion Options Expiry' Bloomberg article notes around $11bn of Bitcoin options expire October 30, approximately one-third of Deribit open contracts. Tesseract estimates 70% of expiring gamma lies between $75,000 and $82,000; dealer-positioning direction remains uncertain. (BBG)

WSJ counts 43 announced US government equity and warrant deals involving around $30bn since Trump returned, spanning chips, minerals and quantum computing. Many also include loans or supply commitments. (WSJ)

Trump deferred immediate robotics and industrial-machinery tariffs despite finding national-security risks. Commerce and USTR will negotiate with trading partners and report within 180 days. (RTRS)

Japan’s two-year government bond auction drew firm demand, as elevated yields attracted investors ahead of a Bank of Japan policy decision on Friday, where rates are widely expected to remain unchanged. (BBG)

T. Rowe Price favours longer JGBs, AllianzGI is adding intermediate and long maturities, and BNP Paribas AM has increased super-long exposure, citing valuations, returning domestic demand and greater policy confidence. (BBG)

Five-year CDS widened across all 40 major Japanese companies tracked by Bloomberg in October, with a median 12bp increase—the largest deterioration since September 2022. October corporate issuance reached a record roughly ¥2.5tn. (BBG)

China’s STAR 50 fell as much as 4.6% despite strong chip results. Moore Threads dropped 13% on nearly 1,800% revenue growth, while Biwin lost 14% despite over 500% profit growth. (BBG)

China's Huafa repaid some investors in an overdue trust product, a Bloomberg source said. Its 2027 offshore yuan bonds traded near 60 cents after losing around 38% this week; its property arm delayed results to October 31. (BBG)

Chinese copper buyers are rushing to secure supply in a tightening market, sending the Yangshan premium to a record high of more than $200 a ton. (BBG)

Macquarie expects copper surpluses over the next few years and says prices have outrun fundamentals. Trafigura estimates data centres add 350,000 tonnes of demand this year, while high prices squeeze other consumption. (FT)

Around 90% of LME/Comex copper warehouse stocks are now in the US versus 20% two years ago. Macquarie warns removing the tariff threat could prompt rapid liquidation. (FT)

UBS estimates 150–170m tonnes of iron-ore supply is cash-negative below $90/t, although closure costs delay cuts. Producers representing 15–20m tonnes have already reduced or signalled lower output. (BBG)

Narrowing the Hong Kong dollar’s trading band against the US greenback may enhance stability and reassure the public if such a move were ever implemented, according to John Greenwood, the economist dubbed the father of the city’s currency peg. (BBG)

CICC’s chief economist urged greater yuan flexibility and more direct currency-pair trading. He argues sustainable RMB funding demand depends on China’s manufacturing and supply chains rather than cheap carry alone. (BBG)

A voting member on the Bank of Korea's board warned that the recent pace of the won's moves warranted close monitoring, signalling caution over the currency even as the export-reliant economy benefits from booming demand for AI chips. (RTRS)

Markets have virtually fully priced another RBA hike next week. AMP sees December tightening as a high risk rather than its baseline; HSBC identifies February as another window, depending on the growth slowdown. (WSJ)

RBNZ Governor Breman said the probability of a December increase was high. Markets priced an 85% chance of a 25bp hike on December 9 after Wednesday’s unexpected hold at 2.75%. (BBG)

BoC Governor Macklem warned in a Bloomberg interview that US fiscal policy was unsustainable and raising borrowing costs internationally. Heavy government borrowing and AI-related debt issuance could lift Canada’s neutral rate, although the BoC has not changed its estimate. (BBG)

Macklem expects energy costs to pass increasingly into non-energy inflation next year. He defended the BoC’s new forecasting framework and denied the model change itself caused Wednesday’s hike. (BBG)

UK Chancellor Healey played down rejoining the EU, saying the priority was a better deal at next month’s summit. He acknowledged Brexit had damaged growth but said Britain must make the best of being outside. (FT)

The IFS estimates £35bn of tax rises or welfare cuts in the UK would be needed by 2030–31 to avoid real cuts to some services while sustaining health spending and defence goals. (FT)

Spain's Vox is preparing to demand reversed immigration policy as its price for supporting a conservative Spanish government after November 29. Polling at 18–19%, it could hold the balance if the PP misses a majority. (FT)

The South African Reserve Bank and financial institutions are preparing a backup plan in case legislation needed for the switch to a new rand benchmark interest rate isn’t passed by the end of the year. (BBG)

Dedicated LatAm equity funds have fallen to 226 from over 660 in 2015. Only two IPOs above $500m have listed across Brazil and Mexico combined in five years, Bloomberg’s analysis found. (BBG)

Venezuelan oil executives warned shortages of engineers and skilled tradespeople threaten production growth from roughly 1m b/d. PDVSA engineers’ base pay of around $200 monthly makes returning from abroad unattractive. (FT)

Vietnam will retain full ownership of EVN and PetroVietnam through 2030 while reducing Vietcombank and BIDV holdings to at least 65%, preserving stakes in other strategic enterprises. (BBG)

IRAN:

The US remains engaged in negotiations over a temporary peace deal, Semafor reports, without providing further details. (Semafor)

Vance sent security chief Mohsen Rezaei a letter exploring renewed peace talks, WSJ reports. Subsequent discussions concerned a negotiating framework rather than a detailed peace proposal. (WSJ)

A US official said Vance’s letter stressed that talks to avert further strikes must address Iran’s nuclear programme. The delivery date was not disclosed. (Axios)

Trump acknowledged approving Vance’s contact but denied directing renewed peace negotiations, saying it concerned medical supplies. His public account differed from the purpose described by WSJ’s sources. (BBG)

The US is positioned to resume Iran operations after the midterms, but Trump has made no final decision, a defence official told NewsNation. (NewsNation)

Trump said electricity shortages were hampering Iranian drone production. (Trump remarks)

Israeli security experts told FT the inconclusive election leaves Netanyahu able to order Iran strikes as caretaker PM, with few institutional constraints, although US support would likely be needed. (FT)

Persian Gulf oil exports fell to at least 15.7m b/d in the week through October 26 from over 24m b/d through October 18, Kpler data show. The recovery above prewar flows has proved difficult to sustain. (WSJ)

Goldman estimates disruption fears have added roughly $27/bbl to Brent, while JPMorgan’s model puts fair value at $94. Depleted inventories and costly, vulnerable shipping continue supporting prices. (WSJ)

GEOPOLITICAL:

Rosatom said Russia was discussing US cooperation on small nuclear plants for AI data centres. No agreement, project location or financing was announced. (RIA/Sputnik via NAMPA)

Ushakov said Russia and the US were discussing possible sanctions relief for the Russian Direct Investment Fund, but he did not know the outcome. (Interfax)

The Pentagon watchdog declined senators’ request to investigate Ukraine’s Starlink/Starshield disruptions, treating the questions as contractual and referring them elsewhere in the Pentagon. It could reconsider if new information emerges. (AP)

North Korea fired approximately ten short-range ballistic missiles from Wonsan towards the East Sea, South Korea’s military said. Some social reports had put the number at twelve. (Yonhap)

North Korea conducted test loudspeaker broadcasts towards the South Thursday morning, with border residents reporting hearing them. (Yonhap)

China and Japan are considering a Xi–Takaichi handshake at next month’s APEC, FT reports. No meeting is confirmed, but it could offer an opening after the Taiwan dispute. (FT)

EQUITIES:

Marvell is in advanced Lumentum acquisition talks, with an announcement possible next week. No agreement is final; Lumentum’s roughly $83bn market value is not an agreed purchase price, and payment terms are undisclosed. (BBG)

Microsoft Corp. posted increasing growth in its cloud business and kept its capital expenditures in check, satisfying investors amid a drumbeat of concern that spending on artificial intelligence won’t pay off. (BBG)

Azure revenue grew 48% to $33.17bn. Q2 Azure growth guidance of 49–50% beat 47.6% consensus, while total revenue guidance of $96–97.1bn topped $95.6bn expected. (RTRS)

Microsoft’s Q1 capex was $45.2bn versus roughly $50bn planned because third-party capacity slipped. Calendar-2026 capex is now around $170bn (prev. 175bn, citing third-party delays again), with spending above $50bn in Q2 and acceleration in fiscal H2. Microsoft expects positive FY27 free cash flow and will access funding markets when attractive. (RTRS, Call excerpts)

Alphabet’s shares fell about 10% in early trading, setting the stock up for its biggest-ever market value wipeout, after the company disclosed that its artificial intelligence search product was eating into its core advertising business, missing on revenue estimates. Te (BBG)

Alphabet retained $195–205bn calendar-2026 capex guidance and expects another significant increase in 2027. (RTRS)

Samsung Electronics 005930.KS posted a 15-fold jump in quarterly chip profit on Thursday, powered by the AI boom, but its shares tumbled as investors balked at a lack of fresh shareholder-return plans and an outlook that lagged rival SK Hynix's.

Samsung plans to hike spending more than 60% this year after selling out of high-end chips for 2027, yet its stock fell after the company failed to outline plans to share ballooning profits. (BBG)

Samsung says 2027 HBM capacity is sold out with pricing negotiated, and expects the broader memory shortage to persist through 2028. (Chosun Biz)

Samsung says ₩55–75tn remains within estimated 2026 shareholder returns, including buybacks and cancellations. Final amounts and execution await January; the lack of detailed plans disappointed investors. (Samsung, FT)

Banks shelved a planned $5–7bn refinancing for the Anthropic-linked Hubbard, Texas data centre amid the grid review. Underlying loans are already funded; lenders retain exposure longer, with bond issuance potentially staggered into next year. (BBG)

Nscale is pursuing a roughly $30bn IPO valuation despite pushback. Bloomberg highlights $103bn of contracts against just 55MW delivered as of August and potential development capacity of 10GW. (BBG)

UniSuper’s CIO said a $2tn Anthropic valuation could be a stretch. Other Australian CIOs also expressed concern about valuations and the volume of incoming AI equity issuance. (BBG)

DeepSeek and Moonshot allegedly relied heavily on GPT-6 Astra outputs to train recent models, The Information reports. The companies did not comment. (RTRS — The Information)

Tencent is prioritising enterprise agents to improve monetisation, its cloud chief said. WorkBuddy reached 32m monthly users by autumn after an internal shift towards business customers. (BBG)

ServiceNow Inc. shares plunged after the company gave an outlook for quarterly subscription sales that met analysts’ estimates, but failed to quell Wall Street’s anxieties that artificial intelligence will disrupt the software maker. (BBG)

Fortinet beat expectations for the quarter and also gave guidance above analyst expectations for Q4. (Investing)

Equinix, one of the world’s biggest data-center companies, said mounting barriers to bringing new projects online will make existing capacity more valuable and potentially strengthen its grip on the market — including pricing. (BBG)

KLA Corp forecast quarterly revenue above estimates on Thursday, banking on ​strong demand for its chipmaking tools as semiconductor manufacturers ramp ‌up production of high-end processors for AI. However, shares fell nearly 9% in extended trading, with some analysts saying the market had expected a ​higher guidance. (RTRS)

Apple’s 2026 NAND bill could reach $25bn versus $6bn last year for approximately the same volume, TechInsights estimates. Hyperscalers now buy around twice Apple’s share, reversing two years ago’s relationship. (WSJ)

Operators report strong initial iPhone Duo sales and sold-out allocations despite typhoon disruption. DIGITIMES cautions initial shipments were limited. (DIGITIMES)

Ford lifted annual EBIT’s lower bound $500m to $10.5–11bn after 49¢ adjusted EPS beat 41¢ expected. Commodity headwinds approach $2.5bn and Model e revenue fell 31%. Ford expects 2027 EBIT roughly flat with this year’s up-to-$11bn forecast, facing around $2bn of inflation headwinds. (BBG/WSJ)

Carvana Co. reported better-than-expected results on a key profit measure even as high fuel prices and interest rates pressure the business. (BBG)

FedEx raised adjusted EPS guidance to $18–18.60 from $16.90–18.10 and revenue growth to around 12% from 11%. Quarterly EPS of $3.74 beat $3.34 expected, though cost forecasts also increased. (WSJ, BBG)

T-Mobile US Inc. added more total customer accounts in the third quarter than analysts had expected, showing its slate of offers and loyalty incentives are resonating with customers. (BBG)

Deutsche Telekom AG’s plans to combine with its American arm T-Mobile US Inc. have hit a snag, people familiar with the matter said, casting doubt on what would be the largest-ever public merger. (BBG)

EBay recorded higher quarterly sales as customers flock to the e-commerce platform to buy items like trading cards, sports memorabilia and coins, according to its chief executive officer. (WSJ)

Honeywell Aerospace reported higher profit and sales in its first quarter as a standalone company, driven by continued demand across the commercial air travel and defense industries. (WSJ)

Chipotle Mexican Grill Inc. sales rose faster than expected in the third quarter, as more frequent menu launches and revamped loyalty offers help sustain a recovery that had been threatened by a food-illness scare. (BBG)

Korea Zinc is discussing semiconductor-grade sulphuric-acid supply with Micron, Intel and GlobalFoundries from its proposed US smelter. Testing and pricing talks continue; no supply contracts are signed. (ZDNet Korea)

Hyundai cut annual sales guidance to 4m from 4.16m and margin to 5.5–6.5% from 6.3–7.3%. Net profit missed, although operating profit beat; planned investment falls 10% to ₩16tn. (WSJ, BBG)

Toyota September sales fell 2.9% to 921,847 and production 4.5%. China fell 20%, its eighth monthly decline, while North America grew 8.6%. (BBG)

Geely reported RMB4.84bn Q3 net income, but shares reversed gains as investors focused on European hybrid-import restrictions. Exports were about 40% of quarterly sales. (BBG)

BYD short interest fell to a seven-month low of 6.3% of Hong Kong free float. Analysts expect around 55% Q3 profit growth off a weak base but continue cutting 2027 estimates. (BBG)

STMicroelectronics NV forecast fourth-quarter revenue growth as a recovery in chip demand continues after a prolonged slump. (BBG)

🚨 BALTIMORE REJECTS NEW HOME FOR CONFEDERATE STATUES — NEARLY NINE YEARS AFTER REMOVAL, CITY STILL HAS NO PUBLIC RELOCATION PLAN

BALTIMORE, MD — Baltimore has reportedly rejected a proposed new home for its four Confederate monuments, leaving their long-term future unresolved under Mayor Brandon Scott.

The statues were removed in August 2017 and returned to Baltimore earlier this year following an exhibition in Los Angeles. Their storage location remains undisclosed, along with the associated costs.

▪️ NINE YEARS WITHOUT RESOLUTION: Former Mayor Catherine Pugh ordered the monuments removed following the deadly Charlottesville demonstrations. No permanent location has been announced.

▪️ RELOCATION OFFER: Maryland historical preservation records document an earlier offer by the Sons of Confederate Veterans to purchase the monuments in connection with a scholarship for Baltimore students studying history.

▪️ SCOTT’S POSITION: Mayor Brandon Scott has publicly supported melting down and repurposing the monuments rather than restoring them to their original public locations.

▪️ HISTORICAL PRESERVATION DISPUTE: The Maryland Historical Trust previously concluded that Baltimore lacked legal authority to remove three of the monuments without the state’s approval under a preservation agreement.

▪️ TAXPAYER QUESTIONS: City officials have declined to disclose the precise storage location or detailed security and preservation costs. The public has not been given a comprehensive long-term plan.

The monuments commemorate Confederate figures and causes associated with slavery and segregation. Their historical significance does not require restoring them to places of honor, but their treatment remains a public-property and preservation issue.

THE ACCOUNTABILITY QUESTION: Baltimore can reject relocation proposals, but that leaves officials responsible for explaining the alternative.

What is the city’s actual plan, how much is continued storage costing taxpayers, and when will residents receive a final decision?

text:
In 1993, Jeffrey Dahmer sat down for an interview with Inside Edition from inside a maximum-security prison. 

He was 33 years old, had been sentenced to hundreds of years in prison, and had already confessed to murdering 17 young men and boys.

But what he admitted during that interview was particularly chilling.

When asked whether he still experienced the urges that had driven him to kill, Dahmer didn’t pretend they had disappeared.

“I wish I could say that it just left me completely, but no, there are times when I still do have the old compulsions.”

Think about that for a moment. He was behind bars, separated from the world, and facing the consequences of his crimes, yet he admitted that those compulsions had not completely gone away.

The interview offered a disturbing glimpse into how he described his own mind. He spoke about his growing obsession with keeping his victims close to him and how the behaviour had escalated over time. He also acknowledged that he had repeatedly tried to fight his thoughts before eventually giving in to them.

Less than two years after that interview, Dahmer was dead.

On 28 November 1994, while serving his sentence at Columbia Correctional Institution in Wisconsin, he was attacked by fellow inmate Christopher Scarver. Dahmer suffered fatal head injuries after being beaten with a metal bar. He was 34 years old.

The man who had terrorised so many families was killed inside the prison where he was supposed to spend the rest of his life.

His story remains one of the most disturbing criminal cases in American history, not simply because of the brutality of his crimes, but because of what his own words revealed about his continuing compulsions while incarcerated.

Sometimes, the most unsettling part of a true-crime case is hearing the perpetrator explain, in his own words, what was happening inside his mind.

text:
A personal assistant emerged from a simple messaging hack

Jamie Cuffe, Ben Lerer, Lucas Atkins, Bridgit Mendler, Jeff Miller, Peter Steinberger and Aaron Frank on TBPN with John Coogan and Jordi Hays. Jamie Cuffe founded Pace, an AI operations partner for insurers, after building a data-integration company acquired by Retool. Ben Lerer founded Thrillist and co-founded Lerer Hippeau. Lucas Atkins is CTO of Arcee AI, which moved from customizing models to pretraining its own. Bridgit Mendler co-founded Northwood Space, Jeff Miller leads marketing at Anduril, Peter Steinberger created Moltbot after selling his software company, and Aaron Frank founded Final, later sold to Goldman Sachs, before joining Lightspeed.

Steinberger described Moltbot as a personal-assistant experiment that connects models, messaging and local tools. He said the open-source project is unfinished, has unresolved security risks and may need a foundation to support its community. Coogan and Hays argued that personal agents could expand inference demand and change how people use apps. The guests described AI operations for insurers, proprietary models, satellite ground infrastructure, AI drone racing and lessons from building media companies. Frank said agentic commerce still lacks trusted identity and efficient payment rails, while stablecoins' clearest use is extending access to US dollars globally.

Minute by minute

1. Moltbot's name change was swift (9:02)
John Coogan said Peter Steinberger renamed Claude Bot to Moltbot after Anthropic raised a trademark concern. Jordi Hays said the similar-sounding names could confuse users and that Anthropic had to protect its mark. Coogan warned viewers about crypto accounts using the old handle.

2. Personal agents could lift inference demand (15:27)
Coogan saw Moltbot as a glimpse of consumer AI agents that can handle computer tasks, not just answer questions, and said assistants could make flight booking and other tasks practical. Hays argued that broader access to these tools could increase token use, while noting that major platforms may build the experience into their own products.

3. Personal agents need secure access (33:31)
The hosts warned that Moltbot has sharp edges and urged users to follow its security documentation. They debated whether users will self-host assistants or wait for large platforms to offer them, noting that local access can let an agent work across data and apps that cloud services may not reach.

4. Chip fabrication may be a bottleneck (45:03)
Coogan relayed Ben Thompson's argument that TSMC's planned capacity may lag hyperscaler demand, while fabs take years to build. He and Tyler debated whether energy or chip production is the tighter constraint. Coogan estimated that a larger share of fabrication capacity than energy supply is currently allocated to AI.

5. Meta expands infrastructure and paid features (50:23)
The hosts discussed Meta's $6,000,000,000 multi-year Corning agreement for fiber-optic cable and expanded manufacturing capacity in North Carolina. They also covered planned subscriptions for Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp, including expanded AI features and Meta's Manus agents.

6. Ramp favors direct-response branding (1:00:29)
Coogan and Hays liked Ramp's Super Bowl ad for making the accounting problem, product and brand easy to understand. They argued that repeating the Ramp name and logo could build recognition, and noted the ad's recurring character, Brian, the overburdened accountant.

7. AI safety mixes misuse and control (1:09:41)
The hosts noted that Claude could draft Slack messages, visualize ideas in Figma and show Asana timelines, making integrations a competitive battleground. Tyler said Dario Amodei's essay focused on misuse by bad actors and government oversight, while Coogan emphasized that AI risks also depend on human networks and social conditions.

8. Pace automates insurance back offices (1:19:00)
Jamie Cuffe said Pace raised $10,000,000 from Sequoia and is live with insurers including Prudential and brokers such as Newfront. Its agents handle new-business submissions, policy servicing and claims by converting existing procedures into agent instructions and working with legacy systems. Cuffe said customers can build additional agents on the platform after Pace helps launch the first ones.

9. Media growth can erode focus (1:33:28)
Ben Lerer said Thrillist started as a profitable niche media company, but raising money and pursuing rapid growth diluted its focus. He said combining media with commerce did not work as investors hoped and advised TBPN to prioritize its audience over a venture-scale target. As an investor, he warned against chasing hot deals without regard to price or likely returns.

10. Small models are getting larger (2:03:34)
Lucas Atkins said Arcee AI moved from customizing open models to pretraining its own, and that models below 50,000,000,000 parameters now count as small. He said reinforcement learning can help a 100,000,000-parameter model perform like models that had 5,000,000,000 or 6,000,000,000 parameters. Customers often look to smaller self-hosted models when production costs, compliance or data privacy become concerns.

11. Northwood owns the ground stack (2:17:28)
Bridgit Mendler said Northwood Space raised $100,000,000 and produced eight portal units in four weeks. The units reached their destination by commercial airliner and were operating within 12 hours. She said the company handles the ground-side stack from satellite contact through hardware, networking, software and APIs. Northwood plans to bring more production in-house and target 12 units per month for one product line.

12. Anduril turns drone racing into recruiting (2:33:08)
Jeff Miller said Anduril is developing an AI drone-racing league where teams use identical hardware and compete through software. The plan includes virtual and physical qualifiers, an event in Columbus, a $500,000 prize pool and the possibility of jobs at Anduril. Teams are capped at eight people. Miller also discussed making Anduril merchandise more accessible and using product-development stories in marketing.

13. Moltbot began as a personal assistant (2:57:41)
Peter Steinberger said he returned to coding after burnout and built Moltbot by connecting WhatsApp, models and local tools. An agent handling a voice message convinced him of its potential. He said Opus was his favorite for conversational personality, while Codex was a reliable coding worker. Steinberger sees apps becoming APIs for personalized assistants, but said prompt injection remains unsolved and the project needs maintainers.

14. Agentic commerce needs trusted rails (3:35:26)
Aaron Frank said agentic commerce lacks an efficient payment model and a way for merchants to verify agents, creating fraud and attribution problems. He said he had not yet bought anything through an agent. Frank argued that stablecoins' clearest use is extending access to US dollars globally, and put their total value at about $300,000,000,000, up from roughly $200,000,000,000 the prior year.

The link in the reply plays each point from its second.

I've been to all of these states and I wouldn't live in any of them... - Oklahoma, Mississippi, and West Virginia rank as the most affordable states to live in the United States, driven by low housing costs and everyday living expenses well below the national average.

Top Most Affordable States (2026 Cost-of-Living Index)

The national average is set at a baseline of 100. States with scores below 100 are more affordable than the rest of the country.
Oklahoma – Index score: ~83.0 to 84.7 (Housing costs are roughly 31% to 33% below the national average)
Mississippi – Index score: ~85.3 (Lowest or near-lowest housing prices and rent in the nation)
West Virginia – Index score: ~88.0 (Features some of the most affordable median home prices in the country, tracking around $225,500)
Alabama – Index score: ~88.1 (Low property tax rates and budget-friendly daily essentials)
Kansas – Index score: ~88.4 (Lower-than-average grocery, utility, and housing expenses)
Missouri – Index score: ~88.4 (Housing costs run about 20% below the national average)
Iowa – Index score: ~89.7 (High housing affordability relative to local median household income)
Arkansas – Index score: ~90.3 (Low overall cost of living with very affordable rural and suburban real estate)
Tennessee – Index score: ~90.4 (Combines lower-than-average everyday expenses with no state income tax on earned wages, though major areas like Nashville have seen price growth)
You can review complete state-by-state breakdowns and metrics via the US News Affordability Rankings and the North American Van Lines Cost of Living Guide.

Key Factors Driving Affordability

• Housing Market: Housing is the largest component of personal budgets, and these states offer median home values and rent prices significantly lower than coastal hubs like California, New York, or Hawaii.
• Regional Clustering: The most budget-friendly states are heavily concentrated across the South and the Midwest, where land and construction costs remain lower.
• Taxes and Utilities: Several of these states feature low property tax rates or no traditional state income tax, though some offset this with higher sales or utility taxes depending on the season.

Poor states are affordable.

text:
Prince’s 3121 Expanded Edition Arrives Across All Major Music Streaming Services

Sender: Legacy Recordings / The Prince Estate
Date: October 29, 2026
Time: 11:22 AM CET

Originally released in 2006, 3121 found Prince delivering an irresistible mix of funk, soul, rock, and pop across tracks like “Black Sweat,” “Te Amo Corazón,” “Fury” and “Beautiful, Loved and Blessed.” Now, 3121 expands beyond the original album. This expanded edition combines the original 12 tracks with 10 additional tracks, including previously unreleased material. Rediscover 3121 and go beyond the original album with this expansive look at one of Prince’s most celebrated eras. The full digital package arrives on all major streaming services on December 11, 2026, with the preview track “Time of Ur Life” already available across platforms.

Apple Music:
Apple Music already has “Time of Ur Life” available for streaming, alongside the original 12-track 3121 album. The full expanded edition will arrive for streaming and download on the December 11 release date. Apple’s lossless and spatial audio options will apply where available, giving listeners a high-fidelity experience of both the classic tracks and the newly added vault material, including the acoustic versions and previously unreleased songs. The platform is expected to include the set in “New Music” and artist-focused collections tied to Prince’s ongoing catalog expansions.

Amazon Music:
Amazon Music prominently features the expanded edition through its merch and album pages. The 2CD + Blu-ray physical set is available for pre-order (ASIN B0HNR74GNW), and the service will carry the complete 22-track digital version upon release. Users can already stream the original 3121 and the new preview single “Time of Ur Life.” Amazon Music Unlimited subscribers will receive the full expanded album in high quality, with the platform highlighting the bonus cuts and related merch.

Spotify:
Spotify will host the complete 3121 Expanded Edition as a dedicated album on December 11, 2026. The original 12-track version remains available, and “Time of Ur Life” is streaming now as an early release. Expect the full set—including acoustic versions of “The Word,” “Love,” and “Te Amo Corazón,” plus unreleased tracks such as “The Streets of Panama,” “Elixer,” “Glass Cutter,” and “Girls In the Band”—to appear in Prince’s catalog with updated artwork and credits. Spotify’s editorial playlists are anticipated to feature the new material prominently.

YouTube Music:
YouTube Music (and the broader YouTube platform) will offer the full 22-track expanded edition on release day. The service already carries the original album, official videos for “Fury,” “Te Amo Corazón,” and “Black Sweat,” and the preview track “Time of Ur Life.” The new bonus tracks will join the catalog, and related concert footage from the Las Vegas residency may appear in video content.

Tidal and Deezer:
Tidal and Deezer will both carry the complete 3121 Expanded Edition on December 11, 2026. These services already stream the original 12-track album and the early preview single “Time of Ur Life.” Listeners can expect high-resolution options on Tidal and standard streaming on Deezer, with the full bonus track list (including “Another Girl,” “Ur’e Such A Tease,” and the acoustic versions) integrated into Prince’s discography.

Other Platforms:
The expanded edition will also appear on Pandora, iHeartRadio, and additional digital service providers worldwide on the same date. Physical buyers of the 2CD or 3LP sets receive a free digital/MP3 version in many regions, further expanding access. With the full package combining the original album’s chart-topping mix of funk, soul, and rock with previously unreleased and alternate tracks, December 11 marks a major moment for fans seeking a deeper look at one of Prince’s most celebrated mid-2000s eras across every major streaming service.

text:
BRISTOL MYERS SQUIBB $BMY Q3’26 — REVENUE +7%, GROWTH PORTFOLIO +12%, BUT EARNINGS FALL 17%.
Bristol Myers Squibb delivered stronger revenue growth, supported by newer medicines and continued strength in Eliquis.
But adjusted earnings declined, margins contracted and management lowered its full-year EPS outlook.
THE NUMBERS
🔹 Revenue: $13.07B (Est. ~$12.72B) 🟢; +7% YoY
🔹 Adjusted EPS: $1.35 (Est. ~$1.09) 🟢; −17% YoY
🔹 Reported EPS: $1.05; −3% YoY
🔹 GAAP Net Income: ~$2.2B
🔹 Adjusted Net Income: ~$2.8B
🔹 Adjusted Gross Margin: 68.4%; −450 bps
🔹 GAAP Gross Margin: 68.3%; −360 bps
🔹 Growth Portfolio: $7.66B; +12% YoY
🔹 Legacy Portfolio: $5.42B; +1% YoY
FY2026 GUIDANCE — REVENUE RAISED, EPS LOWERED
🔹 Revenue: $49.75B–$50.25B (Prior: $49B–$50B) 🟢
🔹 Revenue Midpoint: $50B; raised $500M
🔹 Adjusted EPS: $6.35–$6.55 (Prior: $6.75–$7.00) 🔴
🔹 Adjusted Gross Margin: 69%–70%; maintained
🔹 Eliquis Revenue Growth: +20% to +25%; maintained
The EPS reduction primarily reflects higher acquired R&D and licensing charges rather than a comparable deterioration in underlying operating expectations.
KEY DRUG PERFORMANCE
🔹 Eliquis: $4.69B; +25% YoY
🔹 Opdivo: $2.37B; −6%
🔹 Opdivo Qvantig: $334M; more than tripled
🔹 Reblozyl: $750M; +22%
🔹 Breyanzi: $526M; +46%
🔹 Camzyos: $420M; +42%
🔹 Opdualag: $367M; +23%
🔹 Revlimid: $303M; −47%
🔹 Pomalyst/Imnovid: $130M; −81%
WHAT'S CHANGING
1. NEWER MEDICINES ARE GAINING MOMENTUM
Growth Portfolio revenue increased 12% to $7.66B, representing approximately 59% of total sales.
Breyanzi, Camzyos, Reblozyl and Opdualag continue expanding, while Opdivo Qvantig is contributing to the oncology franchise.
However, the original Opdivo formulation declined 6%, demonstrating how growth within the portfolio can partly reflect transitions between formulations.
2. ELIQUIS REMAINS BOTH A STRENGTH AND A RISK
Eliquis revenue increased 25% to $4.69B.
That represents approximately 36% of total quarterly revenue.
But upcoming patent expirations and generic competition create a significant future revenue-replacement challenge.
Meanwhile, Revlimid and Pomalyst continue experiencing substantial declines as generic competition expands.
The question is whether newer medicines can grow quickly enough to offset future erosion in the legacy portfolio.
3. MARGINS AND EARNINGS NEED ATTENTION
Adjusted gross margin declined 450 basis points to 68.4%.
Management attributed the pressure primarily to product mix and a one-time contract termination charge.
Acquired R&D charges increased to approximately $1.6B, contributing to lower adjusted EPS.
These investments may support future growth, but their financial returns remain uncertain.
4. THE PIPELINE IS BECOMING MORE IMPORTANT
Bristol Myers continues advancing treatments across oncology, hematology, neuroscience and cardiovascular medicine.
Recent developments include:
🔹 Zenbexus: Regulatory approval for multiple myeloma.
🔹 Iza-bren: Positive Phase 3 results in breast and lung cancer.
🔹 RYZ101: Positive Phase 3 results in neuroendocrine tumours.
🔹 Milvexian: Upcoming late-stage cardiovascular trial results.
The pipeline offers several potential growth opportunities, but clinical success must translate into approvals, commercial adoption and profitable revenue.
MY TAKE
What interests me most is the contrast between Bristol Myers' improving revenue

MERCK $MRK  Q3’26 — REVENUE BEATS, GUIDANCE RAISED, BUT KEYTRUDA'S 2028 PATENT CLIFF REMAINS THE BIG QUESTION.
Merck delivered stronger-than-expected Q3 results, supported by oncology, vaccines and growing contributions from newer medicines.
But beneath the earnings beat, profitability declined and the company still faces a major challenge: reducing its dependence on Keytruda before 2028.
THE NUMBERS
🔹 Revenue: $18.09B (Est. ~$17.35B) 🟢; +5% YoY
🔹 Adjusted EPS: $2.49 (Est. ~$2.09) 🟢; −3% YoY
🔹 Reported EPS: $2.04; −12% YoY
🔹 GAAP net income: $5.07B; −12% YoY
🔹 Adjusted gross margin: 81.4% (vs. 81.9% LY)
🔹 Pharmaceutical sales: $16.27B; +4% YoY
🔹 Animal Health: $1.68B; +4% YoY
FY2026 GUIDANCE — RAISED
🔹 Revenue: $66.8B–$67.3B (Prior: $66.3B–$67.3B)
🔹 Adjusted EPS: $2.77–$2.82 (Prior: $2.66–$2.76)
🔹 Adjusted gross margin: ~81%; maintained
The improved outlook is encouraging, although the EPS guidance includes substantial acquisition-related R&D charges and benefits from a lower expected tax rate.
KEY DRUG PERFORMANCE
🔹 Keytruda + Keytruda Qlex: $8.60B; +6% YoY
🔹 Keytruda Qlex: $830M
🔹 Gardasil/Gardasil 9: $2.00B; +14%
🔹 Winrevair: $694M; +93%
🔹 Januvia/Janumet: $380M; −39%
Keytruda remains Merck's largest revenue contributor, accounting for approximately 48% of quarterly sales.
Winrevair is emerging as an important growth driver, while Gardasil recovered and Januvia continues to face generic competition.
WHAT'S CHANGING
1. THE REVENUE BEAT NEEDS CONTEXT
Merck reported 5% revenue growth, but approximately $550M of pharmaceutical sales benefited from purchasing timing.
That represents roughly 3% of quarterly revenue.
It doesn't eliminate the underlying growth story, but it means investors should be careful about extrapolating the headline revenue beat.
2. KEYTRUDA REMAINS BOTH THE STRENGTH AND THE RISK
Keytruda generated $8.6B in quarterly revenue, demonstrating its continued importance to Merck.
The launch of Keytruda Qlex offers another way to support the franchise through a subcutaneous formulation.
However, the approaching 2028 U.S. patent expiry remains a significant challenge.
The question isn't whether Keytruda is performing well today. It's how much of that revenue and profitability Merck can protect once biosimilar competition arrives.
3. THE PIPELINE IS BECOMING MORE IMPORTANT
Merck continues to advance several potentially significant treatments.
🔹 Sac-TMT: Positive Phase 3 data in endometrial cancer, with an FDA priority review underway.
🔹 Cancer vaccine: Positive Phase 3 melanoma results from its collaboration with Moderna.
🔹 Winrevair: Strong commercial growth in pulmonary arterial hypertension.
These developments strengthen the long-term pipeline, but clinical success doesn't automatically translate into commercial success.
Regulatory approvals, market adoption, pricing and profitability will determine their eventual contribution.
MY TAKE
What interests me most is the contrast between Merck's current earnings strength and its longer-term revenue replacement challenge.
The company is still generating substantial revenue from Keytruda, while Winrevair and other newer products are beginning to contribute more meaningfully.
But adjusted EPS declined despite revenue growth, and the headline sales beat benefited from purchasing timing.
I also wouldn't overlook the scale of Merck's recent investment in its pipeline. Acquisitions and licensing agreements can create long-term value, but investors need to assess the returns against the capital committed.
For me, Merck's investment thesis increasingly depends on whether its next generation of medicines can grow quickly enough to offset future Keytruda competition.
WHAT MATTERS NEXT
Can Winrevair, Keytruda Qlex and Merck's expanding oncology pipeline generate enough profitable growth to reduce the impact of Keytruda's 2028 patent expiry?
The earnings beat is encouraging. But Merck's long-term value will depend on how successfully it builds the business beyond Keytruda.

First Mid Bancshares, a community bank across the Midwest, grew profit through acquisitions while its existing loan book shrank. Profit per share excluding one-offs rose 30% from a year ago to $1.26 after February's Two Rivers merger, and troubled loans fell by $46 million. • Q4 quarterly dividend plan: $𝟎.𝟐𝟔 (+4% from a year ago, unchanged from Q3)

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: 🟢 Bullish

The story got better because Chief Executive Matthew Smith found a clean way past the $10 billion asset mark and cleaned up low-yielding bonds. Buying Evergreen Bancshares adds enough profit to cover the debit card fee caps that kick in above $10 billion, and an October bond sale trades a one-time loss for higher interest income. One caution: total loans fell $86 million from last quarter, and rising deposit rates outpaced loan yields.

The question now is whether higher bond yields and new lending can offset rising deposit costs before Evergreen closes. Either the October bond reinvestment lifts the lending margin, or commercial loan payoffs and money market rates keep squeezing net interest income. Fourth-quarter loan balances and deposit costs will tell.

Chief executive Matthew Smith announced a deal to buy Evergreen Bancshares, saying it is "better positioning us to move past the $10 billion asset threshold".

• Evergreen assets: $932 million, with $712 million in gross loans and $727 million in deposits
• Expected profit per share boost in 2028: about 5%, or 7% before the debit card fee cap
• Tangible book value dilution at close: about 0.5%, earned back in roughly six months

The deal matters because banks often lose profit if they cross $10 billion slowly through normal lending. Buying Evergreen adds 10 branches around St. Louis and Indianapolis and brings enough profit at once to cover the new regulatory costs.

What to watch: the merger registration filing and the closing timeline. A delay in regulatory approval would push back the 2028 profit boost.

🟢 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐛𝐥𝐞𝐦 𝐋𝐨𝐚𝐧𝐬 𝐒𝐡𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐤 𝐀𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐄𝐚𝐫𝐥𝐢𝐞𝐫 𝐅𝐚𝐫𝐦 𝐃𝐨𝐰𝐧𝐠𝐫𝐚𝐝𝐞𝐬
Over the first half of 2026, lower crop cash flows pushed more farm borrowers into troubled loan categories. First Mid divides watched credits into special mention loans, which show early strain, and substandard loans, which carry higher risk.

In the third quarter, total criticized loans fell by $45.9 million because borrowers paid down debt, refinanced elsewhere, or earned rating upgrades. Special mention balances dropped $37.6 million to $101.5 million, and substandard loans fell $8.3 million to $131.6 million. Because loan balances shrank and net loan losses were $0.2 million, the lender released $0.3 million from its credit loss reserves.

What to watch: non-performing loans, which are credits no longer paying interest and edged up $1.8 million to $43.1 million this quarter. Another rise after fall crop harvests would show that farm stress is still spreading.

🟢 𝐔𝐩𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐌𝐨𝐧𝐞𝐲 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐞𝐭 𝐀𝐜𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐓𝐨𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐃𝐞𝐩𝐨𝐬𝐢𝐭𝐬
First Mid needs local customer deposits so it does not have to rely on wholesale borrowing. Total deposits rose $44.2 million from last quarter to $7.62 billion. Stripping out the $1.04 billion acquired with Two Rivers Bank & Trust at close in February, deposits from businesses owned a year ago grew 4.6% from a year ago by our math, compared with 21.1% headline growth.

Money market accounts drove the quarterly gain, rising $198.8 million to $1.57 billion. The bank credited its "deposit product refresh in early 2026" and ongoing marketing for bringing in those balances while checking and savings accounts shrank.

What to watch: non-interest-bearing checking accounts next quarter. Those free deposits slipped $21.2 million to $1.47 billion in the third quarter, and further outflows would force the bank to rely even more on higher-rate money market accounts.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐃𝐞𝐩𝐨𝐬𝐢𝐭 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐞𝐭𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐒𝐪𝐮𝐞𝐞𝐳𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐋𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧
A bank's primary engine is its net interest margin (NIM), the gap between what it earns on loans and bonds and what it pays for deposits and borrowings. On a tax-equivalent basis, First Mid's NIM shrank by 0.03 percentage points from last quarter to 3.76%, pushing net interest income down $0.3 million to $79.4 million.

New and renewed loans came on the books at 6.25% and 6.50%, which lifted the average yield on earning assets by 0.06 percentage points to 5.51%. However, market rate moves and rival offers pushed the average cost of interest-bearing deposits up 0.18 percentage points to 2.16%. Overall funding costs rose 0.10 percentage points to 1.85%, outpacing the loan yield gains.

What to watch: the average cost of interest-bearing deposits in the fourth quarter. If deposit costs keep rising faster than loan yields, net interest income will fall again even after the October bond reinvestment.

🔴🔴 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐜𝐢𝐚𝐥 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐭𝐲 𝐏𝐚𝐲𝐨𝐟𝐟𝐬 𝐒𝐡𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐤 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐋𝐨𝐚𝐧 𝐁𝐨𝐨𝐤
First Mid closed the Two Rivers acquisition in February, which lifted headline loans 17.6% from a year ago to $6.85 billion. Stripping out the $871.4 million of loans acquired at close, underlying loans grew 2.6% from a year ago by our math. From last quarter, total loans fell by $85.8 million, following a $9.9 million drop in the second quarter.

Smith said lending faced pressure from "higher payoff activity from customer collateral sales", including a multi-location business that sold property and paid off its debt. Commercial real estate loans dropped $107.3 million from last quarter to $2.82 billion, and commercial business loans fell $33.3 million. Shrinking loan balances cut into interest income and leave the bank with more cash sitting in lower-yielding accounts.

What to watch: period-end total loans in the fourth quarter. Another sequential drop before the Evergreen merger closes would show that customer payoffs are still outrunning new lending.

🔴 𝐇𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐟𝐟 𝐁𝐨𝐧𝐮𝐬𝐞𝐬 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐄𝐱𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐬𝐞 𝐑𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨
Reported operating expenses fell $5.7 million from last quarter to $65.0 million because one-time Two Rivers merger bills dropped from $7.1 million to $0.4 million. Excluding those merger bills and other one-offs, operating costs rose $0.8 million to $60.3 million, and the efficiency ratio — operating costs as a share of revenue — worsened by 1.74 percentage points to 56.13%.

Salaries and employee benefits drove the increase, rising $1.0 million from last quarter to $39.4 million. By our math, staff costs rose by 1.51 percentage points of adjusted revenue to 36.7%, which First Mid attributed to "additional variable compensation for overperformance compared to plan".

What to watch: the efficiency ratio in the fourth quarter. A reading above 56% would show that higher staff pay is eating into the cost savings promised from the Two Rivers merger.

👓 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐬

𝐎𝐜𝐭𝐨𝐛𝐞𝐫 𝐁𝐨𝐧𝐝 𝐒𝐚𝐥𝐞 𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐝𝐞𝐬 𝐋𝐨𝐬𝐬 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐘𝐢𝐞𝐥𝐝
On October 26, after the third quarter ended, First Mid sold investment securities yielding 1.51% for $175.8 million in cash. The sale creates a $14.8 million pre-tax loss that will hit fourth-quarter reported earnings. The Illinois bank plans to reinvest the cash at higher market rates and expects the extra interest income to earn back the loss in less than two years.

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐍𝐨𝐧-𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟐𝟕.𝟐 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Fee revenue fell 5.6% from last quarter on seasonal dips in insurance commissions and wealth management, though it rose 18.8% from a year ago. Fee businesses — wealth management, insurance, farm services and card fees — produced 26% of total revenue. The bank also agreed to buy Winship Farm Management, adding 8,600 acres over three years.

First Mid paid off $10.0 million of subordinated debt — long-term borrowings that sit below regular debt — using cash on hand during the quarter. That follows a $27.5 million paydown in the second quarter and leaves the balance down 71.4% from a year ago, trimming quarterly interest expense on those notes from $0.9 million to $0.5 million.

𝐓𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐢𝐛𝐥𝐞 𝐛𝐨𝐨𝐤 𝐯𝐚𝐥𝐮𝐞 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟑𝟏.𝟎𝟗  ⇒ stable
Net worth per share, excluding goodwill and other intangible assets from past mergers, slipped $0.06 or 0.2% from last quarter but remains up 10.2% from a year ago. A $32.3 million rise in unrealized bond losses cut $1.21 per share in the quarter, which quarterly earnings almost offset.

𝐐𝟒 𝐑𝐞𝐠𝐮𝐥𝐚𝐫 𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐥𝐲 𝐃𝐢𝐯𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐝: $𝟎.𝟐𝟔 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞  ⇒ stable
New. The board declared a quarterly cash payout of $0.26 per share for the fourth quarter, payable December 1. That matches the third-quarter rate after a $0.01 increase in August and is up 4.0% from a year ago.

❓ 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐞𝐱𝐚𝐜𝐭 𝐩𝐮𝐫𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐬𝐞 𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐦𝐬 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐄𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐠𝐫𝐞𝐞𝐧 𝐁𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞𝐬?
