text:
Study Notes - (Pulpit Version Explained) 

Psalms 131:1-3
EXPOSITION
This psalm has been said to be "like a string era Christian ’Lyre Innocentium’" (Bishop Alexander). It breathes the profoundest humility and submission to God’s will (Psa_131:1, Psa_131:2). At the same time, it encourages the faithful to maintain a lively "hope" in God’s sustaining grace (Psa_131:3). The ascription of the psalm to David is quite in accordance, both with the language and the contents.
Psa_131:1
Lord, my heart is not haughty; or, "not lifted up". Not unduly elated by the prosperity that thou hast bestowed on me. Nor mine eyes lofty (comp. Psa_101:5), "Pride," as Hengstenberg says, "has its seat in the heart, and betrays itself especially in the eyes." Neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me; literally, too wonderful (comp. Psa_139:6, "Such knowledge is too wonderful for me: it is high: I cannot attain unto it"). The speculative debates of so-called "wise men" concerning the deep things of God’s moral government are probably glanced at (see Job_42:3).
Psa_131:2
Surely I have behaved and quieted myself; rather, I have stilled and quieted my soul. I have brought my soul into a state of peacefulness and content. As a child that is weaned of his mother. The weaned child is quiet and content; the suckling always impatient and restless. My soul is even as a weaned child. Another repetition for the sake of emphasis (see Psa_130:5, Psa_130:6).
Psa_131:3
Let Israel hope in the Lord from henceforth and forever (comp. Psa_130:7). Israel is exhorted to have like confidence and trust in God as the psalmist.
HOMILETICS
Psa_131:1-3
Lowliness of mind.
This psalm may have been written by David so far as its subject-matter is concerned. For that lowliness of mind of which it treats is quite as compatible with a high as with a humble position in life. Royalty may be very meek, and obscurity may be very proud. All moral qualities are independent of situations; they are a question of character, not of circumstance. Of the greatest One that ever bore our likeness it is said, "Thy King cometh … meek" (Mat_21:5). But we have here—
I. A COMMON TEMPTATION. There are souls that do not aspire to be or do what is beyond them in any direction; but they are probably the exception rather than the rule. In all departments of activity men and women long for that which is out of their reach. The sailor is looking forward eagerly to a captaincy, or to be commodore or admiral The soldier will not be satisfied until he is gazetted colonel of his regiment. The politician hungers for an office which is much higher up than the one he holds. And thus it is in every sphere. It is right, indeed, that every one should seek and strive to putout all his powers, instead of allowing them to slumber in silence and inactivity. We are bound to be our best and do our utmost in a world that is crying for help and for redemption. But our temptation is to long and to labor for that which is beyond our capacity, for which we were not created and endowed, which would exalt us, but which we should not adorn. The student wants to master that which is "too wonderful for him," actually "unattainable" (Psa_139:6). The servant of Christ wants to fill a post in the Church for which he is not mentally and morally qualified. The traveler thirsts to reach a latitude which is outside the range of practicable pursuit, everywhere, in all classes and conditions, men are sighing and striving for that which they will never reach, or will only reach when they have exhausted their strength and cannot enjoy what they have gained.
II. THE LESSON OF EXPERIENCE. Experience is continually teaching us the folly of seeking to move in a sphere which is beyond us. It is constantly resulting in defeat, in disappointment, in mortification. The position sought is not won, and there is the deep discontentment of having toiled in vain; or it is gained, and is found to be full of difficulty that was not anticipated, and, instead of yielding the expected pleasure, it is productive of dissatisfaction and complaint, and it ends in serious, perhaps disastrous, failure. They are wise men who, witnessing this in other people, or beginning to discover it in their own case, reach the psalmist’s conclusion; this is—
III. THE PRACTICAL CONCLUSION OF THE WISE. To be contented with the sphere which God has assigned us, and to do our best therein. The psalmist has learnt the lesson. He has had to compose a disquieted spirit, and he has done so; he was restless and passionate, like an unweaned child clamoring for its mother’s breast. But he has "quieted himself," he has calmed his spirit; he has withdrawn from a false position; he has settled down permanently to the only true one. His heart is not lifted up; his eyes do not look enviously and hungrily to the heights beyond him; he does not dwell in anxious, wearisome thought on matters which are best left alone; he concentrates his sympathies and his energies on that which demands his attention, and which is productive of good to himself and those around him; he is perfectly contented to be just what God has made him, to go where his Master sends him, to do what is placed in his hands to do. He is so far from thinking himself essential to the prosperity of the Church and the redemption of the world, that he hopefully, and even confidently, leaves that in the care of the Supreme (Psa_131:3).
HOMILIES BY S. CONWAY
Psa_131:1-3
The soul’s most blessed condition.
That which the psalmist here affirms of himself is undoubtedly the spiritual condition which is nearest to heaven that here on earth we can know.
I. HE TELLS US WHAT IT IS NOT.
1. Pride of heart is absent from it. "My heart is not haughty." We may say this to our fellow-men, and deceive them by a show of humility; but it is quite another thing to affirm this, as is here done, before the Lord, "to whom all hearts are open, and from whom no secrets are hid" Happy are we if before him we can say this. For pride is destructive of all real happiness: it is continually meeting with rebuffs; nothing people like so much as to take down the man who is haughty of heart. To humiliate him is the keenest delight. If the devil has planted pride in all men’s hearts, as he has, God has so ordered the world that every man’s hand shall be against such pride.
2. It is free from ambition. "Nor mine eyes lofty." The man’s eyes are not forever fixed on and hankering after something higher up in the world than it has yet reached. Blessed is the man who is content with the lot God hath ordered for him, and is solicitous only to be found faithful there.
3. And from presumption. "Neither do I exercise myself," etc. (Psa_131:1). But how many there are who are forever doing that which the psalmist here disclaims! David’s brothers accused him of this, though wrongly, and blamed him for leaving his sheep to come to the battle-field. But though David was innocent of such fault, many are guilty of it. They want to know all mysteries, to be able to explain all that they see around them in God’s providence, and all that they meet with in the Scriptures: they want to undertake work which is beyond them, whilst that which is within their power they refuse. They could sweep a crossing, but they want to rule a kingdom; they could manage the one talent, but because they have not the five, the one they have they bury, to their infinite shame and loss.
II. HE TELLS US WHAT IT IS. To have one’s soul "as a child that is weaned from its mother." Therefore:
1. It is separation from what it once loved. It is a terrible time for the child when this separation has to be made: the metaphor is as touching and beautiful as it is powerfully expressive. And the soul knows how it once loved the world, not so much, perhaps, the evil things of the world as those that were not evil; but it has come to give them all up, and to be content with what the Lord orders for him. Yet morels it separated from the sinful ways of the world. Once it loved them, but that time is past.
2. And it is not only separated from them, but has ceased to desire them. The child is happy and at rest, though no longer allowed that in which it once so delighted. The very desire is gone.
3. And this is not through any disappointment, chagrin, or disgust with the world. Some men rush from the world in anger because of the way it has treated them. But this is not the motive here: such are wrenched from the world rather than weaned from it.
4. Nor either is it the relinquishment which comes from satiety with the world’s pleasures;—from having had so much that the soul has come to care no more for it, its sweets clog and nauseate rather than give pleasure.
5. Nor from want of capacity to enjoy what the world has to offer. But it is a willing abandonment of that which once it delighted in—the world’s pleasures, profits, honors, comforts, as well as its more questionable belongings.
III. HOW WAS THIS BROUGHT ABOUT?
1. It was not self-produced. No child ever weaned itself.
2. It has been the Lord’s work. By his Holy Spirit and his providence he has wrought this wondrous change. Hence we have come to find that what once delighted us so much fails to do so now. The world has become embittered to our taste. Our God has separated us from what we loved and clung to; there was no chance of our voluntarily giving it up, and so God took it away. And he has given us what is better far than that which we have lost (cf. Psa_63:1-11.). Higher, purer joys are ours. Also he has blessed our own endeavors after self-denial and renunciation; he has "worked in us to will and to do,’ etc.
3. And the result is most blessed. The calm quiet and stillness of the soul; its freedom from fret; its heavenly peace.
IV. WHAT THIS EXPERIENCE LEADS TO. A delight in God, and a conviction of his love and faithfulness, which make him call upon all his countrymen to hope in the Lord. When the soul has this experience, it cannot but commend the Lord to others. It must bear its testimony.—S.C.
HOMILIES BY R. TUCK
Psa_131:1
The sense of what is acceptable with God.
This psalm expresses the meek humility of the pardoned and restored sinner. But taken as expressing the sentiment of the restored nation, it suggests the mood of cherished feeling that keeps us in right relations with God. It is not a mood of submission, or even of submissive obedience only. It is a mood of willing submission, of delighted obedience; of submission that has ceased to be a strain, and has become the free, natural, joyous expression of the self. The "heart is not haughty;" so there is no resistance to what is felt to be the duty.
I. SUBMISSION THAT IS STILL A STRAIN CAN ONLY BE PARTIALLY ACCEPTABLE WITH GOD. And very much that is called submission is really only submission in the making. Indeed, if we speak with absolute precision, we must say that submission wholly free from strain can never be the experience of men while they are under human conditions and limitations. We have no instance of perfect submission save that of the Divine Man, the Lord Jesus Christ; and even in his case we have to notice that strain and struggle continued up to Gethsemane, and that absolute entireness of obedience was won only on Calvary, where even the very life was surrendered. We can, therefore, while we are on earth, never gain more than a qualified Divine acceptance. There is peace, and promise, and power, and joy in the measure of acceptance we can gain; but it is always an inspiration, not a satisfaction. Very many good people never get above or beyond this apprehension of Christian life; "they submit because they must." They never can rise to get duty glorified. Indeed, there are many who try to persuade themselves that their submission cannot really be submission unless they feel the strain of it. But it is with this grace as with the digestive process—it is only healthy when we know nothing about it.
II. SUBMISSION THAT HAS CEASED TO BE A STRAIN IS FULLY ACCEPTABLE TO GOD. The will may persistently force attitudes and acts of submission. Then man is but a dual being. The goodness is forced. The man may submit with a reserve. He is willing to go so far. The man is wholly willing to submit sometimes and in some things. It is clear that none of these cases can be fully acceptable to God. When a man’s heart is in the submission, then the man’s will is rightly swayed, and a man’s conduct is in harmonious order. The man is a unity in his submission; strain of resistance is gone, and the full Divine smile can rest upon him.—R.T.
Psa_131:1
On knowing our spheres.
Prayer-book Version, "I do not exercise myself in great matters: which are too high for me." The poet disclaims three distinct kinds of pride; secret conceit of heart; the ostentation of the man of lofty bearing; and the presumptuous self-importance which intrudes. One of the things that can only be learned through the experiences of life is what we can do, and what we may do. Putting wise limits upon our undertakings and our spheres is one of the most important and anxious things that we have to do. And one of the chief modern sins is attempting too much, and not being willing to keep ourselves strictly within the limits of what we can do really well. The young man thinks he can do anything and everything; and it may often be the consequence that he does nothing really well.
I. OUR SPHERES ARE DISCOVERED FOR US BY DIVINE PROVIDENCE. Nothing is more remarkable in a man’s life than the way in which he is led round to the occupying of spheres of which he had never dreamed, and to the undertaking of work for which he had never recognized a fitness. It may occasionally be the case that what a man has to do in life is shown him early, and he runs in the appointed rut from the beginning to the end of his days; but in the majority of cases, even if a hint of the future is early given, the way round to its realization is a set of surprising experiences; and often the life-work unfolds suddenly and unexpectedly, in the time of a man’s maturity. The good man sees in this the leading of Divine providence.
II. OUR SPHERES ARE DISCOVERED FOR US BY OUR AFFINITIES. There are things we have to do, and things we like to do. And, in the long run, life comes round to fit to our likings. We can do well what we enjoy doing, and we gradually drift into the spheres to which we are fitted by bias and inclination. Ideally life would be perfect if every man was placed according to his affinities. Towards the ideal perfection humanity is moving, though its progress is greatly hindered and confused by human self-will, and the exigencies of civilization.
III. OUR SPHERES ARE DISCOVERED BY OUR ATTITUDES OF OBEDIENCE. This is taking the higher, the Divine view of life. When a man fully realizes life as service to God, he rests assured that his Divine Master appoints his sphere and provides his work; and his Master will be absolutely sure to provide sphere and work for every servant who jealously keeps the attitude of obedience.—R.T.
Psa_131:2
Restraint of natural ambitions.
"Instead of fretting after what is too great for him, he quiets his ambition, and his spirit lies calm and gentle, like a child in its mother’s arms, that, after the first trouble of weaning is over, is soothed and lulled by the maternal caress." The image is strikingly simple and true, of natural desire stayed and of a subdued quietness of rest rather than delight. Perowne quotes the following as a mother’s experience: "The weaned child has for the first time become conscious of grief. The piteous longing for the sweet nourishment of his life, the broken sob of disappointment, mark the trouble of his innocent heart: it is not so much the bodily suffering; he has felt that pain before, and cried while it lasted; but now his joy and comfort are taken away, and he knows not why. When his head is once more laid on his mother’s bosom, then he trusts and loves and rests; but he has learned the first lesson of humility, he is cast down, and clings with fond helplessness to his one friend."
I. NATURAL AMBITIONS ARE NOT WRONG IN THEMSELVES. They do but express a man’s individuality and energy. They are but the sign of the intelligence that can fix an aim and a purpose for a life. It describes a helpless, hopeless man to say, "He has no ambition." Such a man wants nothing, tries for nothing, and gets nothing. Religious people often condemn ambition as an essential evil. All we need say is that it may be, but it need not be.
II. NATURAL AMBITIONS BECOME WRONG WHEN THEY ARE SELF-CENTERED. A man is a being in relations. There is a measure of health in every scheme he has for the benefit of another. A man is a dependent being, and his first consideration has to be the approval of him on whom he depends. Ambition to secure purely selfish ends is sin against our relationship, and against our dependence. Ambition that is self-centered is only too likely to inspire unscrupulous means.
III. NATURAL AMBITIONS NEED RESTRAINT WHEN GOD’S WILL IS KNOWN. It is not that God’s will is either antagonistic to, or out of harmony with, our natural ambitions; it is that they are either exaggerated, or have become masterful. If we could read life aright, we should always find that God’s will for our life is in strictest harmony with our own real and well-qualified ambitions. And precisely what the revelation of God’s will does for us is help us in getting our ambitions into proper limitation and control. God does not want the service of men out of whom all heart and energy have been taken. It is not any crushing out of our individuality that honors God: restraint within wise limits means the retention of all good and right ambitions.—R.T.
Psa_131:3
Man’s personal experience may be the basis of his hope in God.
"Let Israel hope in the Lord;" let him, because he has such abundant reason for so doing, in the experience that he has had of the Lord’s gracious working. This is the refrain of several of these "songs of degrees," which, we have seen, are essentially "songs of uplifting," or calls to put trust and hope in God.
I. MAN’S PERSONAL EXPERIENCE IS SELDOM, IF EVER, PRECISELY REPEATED. Froude suggests that experience is like the stern-lights of a ship, which show the way that has been taken. And he hints that experience is of practically little use for the guidance of the way that has to be taken. But this is a very partial view. It would not culture a man in the dependence and trust, which are the key-notes of his nobility, if his life were a mere succession of precise repetitions, so that he might know precisely how to act in each recurring case, and the lessons of experience were a mere routine; a fixed measure to be applied to every instance. Life with emergencies and surprises is alone a healthy life for a moral being in whom character is to be trained. It was a misanthrope who said, "The thing which hath been is, and there is nothing new under the sun." And every man will be prepared to say, on looking over his life, that nothing ever happened in his life which was a precisely imitative experience; nothing that proved to be exactly what he expected it to be. Then it may be hastily said that experience is a delusion, and cannot really help us. What we have to see is that it cannot, and never was intended to, help us as a yard-measure does. How, then, does it help?
II. MAN’S PERSONAL EXPERIENCE ESTABLISHES PRINCIPLES AND BRINGS KNOWLEDGE OF WHICH MAN CAN MAKE PRACTICAL USE. Israel restored from exile had a new set of experiences, but his knowledge of God’s adaptations of grace to all previous experiences established confidence in him. It was easy to argue that God, having made adjustments to their need in forty-nine cases, was not likely to be baffled by the fiftieth. And we can always get that persuasion out of a life-experience. And we can plainly see the force of this principle—all human experiences, though apparently unlike each other, go into classes. We can always find something in past experience which belongs to the same class as our present experience; and then, if we can fully apprehend the Divine intervention in some case that belongs to the class, we can confidently say to our soul, "Soul, hope thou still in God."—R.T.
HOMILIES BY C. SHORT
Psa_131:1-3
Humility.
"Lord, my heart is not haughty," etc. "The psalmist has learned from adversity the lesson of submission, and counsels the nation to fit itself in like manner for winning the blessings which are still in store." The authorship is uncertain; but it was probably written after the Exile. The writer had learned—
I. HUMILITY.
1. Humility is exemplified in a lowly estimate of ourselves be/ore God and man. Before God as well as before man.
2. In not aiming at things which are beyond our powers of attainment. Some men’s ambition is greater than their ability. And yet none of us uses his ability to the utmost. We ought to learn how much God will help us to do.
II. SUBMISSION TO THE WILL OF GOD.
1. This implies the recognition of God’s will as good. Not only as supreme, but as good. Only thus shall we be able to say from the heart, "Thy will be done."
2. The overruling of all discontent with the changes of circumstances. As a child that has been weaned at length learns to rest on its mother’s bosom.
III. HUMILITY AND SUBMISSION ARE CONNECTED WITH PATIENT WAITING AND HOPE.
1. God rewards the patient and humble. "Giveth grace," etc; "but knoweth the proud afar of."
2. All the deeper knowledge of God, springing from humble patience, leads on to a greater hope in him. The deepest experiences lead to the highest hope in God.—S.

To @gadi_eisenkot and @netanyahu Respectively, To
 Members of the Knesset, @Knesset99 

My name is Dr. Whimsy Anderson. I am a medical anthropologist and the creator of the Anderson Oasis Pilot program for Gaza. The work I am presenting here is offered free of charge and as a gift to the State of Israel.

The rise of Arab Israeli citizens as a sizable and growing voting bloc is a security threat if that population remains alienated from the state. It is a threat that can be avoided through deliberate integration and inclusion. Policies that treat fellow citizens as secondary or rely on divide-and-conquer increase the risk of lasting fracture. Integration that improves daily lives, builds skills, and creates visible stakes in the state reduces that risk and strengthens cohesion.

No Israeli should be viewed as second-class or an afterthought. Otherness generates animosity, and animosity fuels violence. If we do not begin to treat one another with respect and a genuine desire for unity, the danger of deeper division—and ultimately civil conflict—rises. The solution is a state that actively works for the well-being of all its citizens.

I am currently developing four pilot programs designed for adoption and implementation by existing Israeli systems and operators. I would like to submit them for review by the Knesset and by the organizations best positioned to facilitate their delivery. The programs and their first-year planning costs are:

Hebrew Camp (ages 8–14, 100 children): Day-one health screening (medical, dental, vision, hearing, nutrition) and educational placement testing. Daily remedial Hebrew and mathematics, communal meals, counselor contact, and field trips focused on Israeli history, Bedouin contributions to the state, and civic belonging. Children bring modest gifts home to parents upon meeting attendance and behavior standards. High-risk children move directly to licensed boarding. Estimated cost: 935,000 NIS.

Paid youth-to-work (ages 15–17, 40 participants): Screening, legal light summer employment, evening remedial Hebrew and math, and inclusion activities. Estimated cost: 560,000 NIS.
Adult at-risk work-and-housing (18+, 25 participants): Screening, legal work, site housing, and ulpan under clear rules. Estimated cost: 605,000 NIS.
Young couples and families (15 households): Screening, temporary housing, paid work, and ulpan; children enter the youth tracks. Estimated cost: 655,000 NIS.
Combined first-year gross cost of all four pilots: approximately 2.76 million NIS.

Comparable programs in the United States and Europe have produced measurable reductions in youth violence and delinquency. In a randomized controlled trial of Chicago’s One Summer Plus program, disadvantaged high-school youth offered eight weeks of paid summer employment experienced a 43 percent reduction in violent-crime arrests over the following 16 months compared with a control group. Evaluations of Boston’s summer youth employment program found reductions of approximately 35 percent in violent-crime arraignments in the 17 months after participation. Demonstration projects with Boys & Girls Clubs reported drops in juvenile arrest rates of 16 percent after one year and 31 percent after three years in participating areas. European meta-analyses of early psychosocial and family-support interventions for young children show average reductions in later delinquent behavior on the order of 19 percent, with stronger effects the earlier the intervention begins.

All cohorts in the proposed pilots are voluntary, hosted by existing operators, and measured against matched peers on police contact and NEET rates. On conservative assumptions, illustrative 5-year justice-related savings range from 4.5–10.8 million NIS, with further gains by year 10. The framework is Benign Dominance Theory: when the state takes active, practical steps to ensure basic well-being and pathways forward, citizens are more likely to thrive and become loyal. This requires responsible education and ensuring that no household is left without adequate needs met. Changing the environments that produce otherness reduces the security threat posed by alienation.

I will be sending the Knesset the complete paper on these four pilots in the hope that a way can be found to work them into the budget. I will also contact the relevant organizations, including Desert Stars, to inform them of what I plan to build going forward. You may reach out to me at any time. This work is offered without charge as a contribution to the strength and cohesion of the state.

Respectfully,

Dr. Whimsy Anderson
Medical Anthropologist
Creator, Anderson Oasis Pilot Program for Gaza

text:
"Through this writing, I want to show you that you must prepare yourselves for a Great Purification.  

All the ravages to your spirit, your body, your heart and your soul will be consumed by the fire of love. Just like iron that is whitened by the fire so that it may be exempt of all impurities, you also will be whitened by the purifying fire so that you may be exempt of all impurities. All that is within you will be before you, for you will be inside yourselves.  

Read the following: 

• Feelings of rancor, envy, anger, frustration, pride, greed, fear, jealousy, hatred, superiority, hypocrisy, indifference, perversity, selfishness, malevolence, and others, that have been detrimental to your soul and your neighbor’s soul, and that have gone against The Love, will not be able to remain hidden within you, you will know what they have produced and you will bear the weight of them. 
• Your slightest thoughts against me, The Love, against your neighbor, and against yourselves, such as thoughts of impurity, covetousness, destruction, vengeance, gluttony, judgement, infidelity, trickery, laziness, lust, and how many others that you have nourished, will be shown to you. 
• All your words, even those that were only pronounced internally, that you have uttered against me, The Love, against your neighbor and against yourselves, such as your comments, your judgements, your black humor, your lies, oh! your blasphemous words, your insults, your insolence, your mockery, your hurtful comparisons, your opinions, your slander, your criticism, your betrayals, your stupidities, your poor discernment, and others, you will be able to hide none of this, you will not be able to admit that you are innocent before these facts. 
• All your gestures against me, The Love, against your neighbor and against yourselves, such as murders, rapes, incest, forbidden sales, illegal purchases, fraud, pedophilia, abusive sexual pleasures, physical violence, gluttony, laziness, adultery, domination, tampering, plotting, illegal confinement, revolts, protests, refusal of love, disobedience, alcohol abuse, abuse of medications, drug abuse, idolatry, scandals, immoral parades, lack of sharing, gestures against nature, gestures against any animal species, and how many others, everything about you will be exposed: you will discover your interior that caused you to commit evil. 
• The reasons that pushed you into committing evil, by refusing to distance yourselves from them, and for which you refused to give love to me, The Love, to your neighbor, and to yourselves, will be shown to you, such as the bad influences of television, bad magazines, bad movies, diabolical music, wild and languorous dances, unhealthy games, clandestine locations, places of debauchery, occult sciences, the contraband of forbidden products, spells — and you know there are others, and I do too —, you will know all this since it will no longer be possible to hide your baseness. 
• Your lack of charity towards your neighbor which was the cause of their sufferings, you will see it. 
• Knowing that you have contributed to baseness such as racism, atheism, exclusion, lack of compassion, revolt, betrayal, plotting, etc., will be reasons for you to hide to avoid seeing that you have lacked love towards your neighbor. 
• Your cold, arrogant, petty, snobbish, hateful looks, as well as others, you will face them. 
• You will be before all those who will have suffered because of you, such as your husband or wife, your children, your parents, your brothers, your sisters, your loved ones, your friends, your professors, your companions, your directors, your employers, aborted children, active members of my Church, members of the clergy, your brothers and sisters of all races, of all languages, of all religions, of all nations; yes, you will feel shame, for I will place them before you; this will happen through the power of my presence since I carry them within me. 
• You will become aware of all animosity towards me, The Love, and towards your neighbor. 
• You will be faced with the prejudices perpetrated against your neighbor because of your bad conduct. 
• You who have wanted to know pleasure to the detriment of the love for your neighbor, I will show you how many times you have made suffer those who prayed for you, while you ridiculed them. 
• You who speak against the Church of Rome and against all Churches which are part of it — the number is much greater than you think for wherever my Presence is, there is the Church —, you will know the consequences of your words and your rejections regarding my Churches, which are an ensemble of my royal Edifice. 
• You who speak against my consecrated, you will learn that you are members of my Church just like them, and you will see all you have done against my Mystical Body, which is me, them, and you. Because you have wanted to bring it down to your level by listing its human faults, without thinking of yourselves who are part of it, you will suffer because of this, for you will see that the Mystical Body is composed of men and women who have given their lives to give God love. Those men and women left everything behind to follow rough paths to bring help to others. They instructed the children of God without keeping track of their time, they took care of God’s children without thinking about their own pains, they brought help to the most destitute without seeking personal gain. 
• You, my consecrated, you alone will be before all the words that you will have uttered, and before all the gestures that you will have made against me, The Love, against your neighbor and against yourselves; you will see all the consequences of your actions, all will be revealed to you. Because you will have been the cause of much pain, you will experience terrible emotions, and greater still, for the offences committed against your priesthood, you will answer to me, the Christ Priest, and each active member who composes the Mystical Church. Any consequence due to your infidelity will be exposed; you will know all the souls which were lost due to your negligence. 
• You, the baptized of my Church, you will discover your lack of fidelity to my sacrament: the Baptism. Because you have refused this sacrament to your little children while you yourselves have received the purifying graces that erased the original sin, you will be before the loving benefits of this sacrament and you will feel a great void before all they missed because of you. You will become conscious of all the pain that you have inflicted upon their soul and your soul, who suffered atrocities because they were not protected against the bites of the Demon. 
• All the baptized of my Church, all children of all religions, and all the children of no religion but who believe in goodness, will be before their faith, and faced with their belief, they will be their own judges before all they neglected to do for the love of God, who is Goodness, for the love of one’s neighbor, and for the love of themselves. 
• You who have been baptized and who have refused to come nourish yourselves with portance of the Eucharist. Because you will have chosen to not receive me within yourselves, you will feel like inferior beings before those who will have received my Presence. 
• You who will have received me in a state of venial sin, you will know the shame of not having gone to Confession as soon as possible. Your interior will show you your indifference towards not wanting to please me. 
• You who will have received me in a state of mortal sin, you will be before your own gestures which are so black, and you will discover my love for you, I who climbed Calvary. I will show you my loving gesture and your impure gestures will make you feel a strong pain, like a vice squeezing your heart, which is cold before my wounds that opened every time you would receive me within yourselves. 
• You who will have touched my pure Body with your dirty hands, you will feel the uncleanliness of your hands, which will smell like sulphur. You will know that I let myself be taken out of love, when I was giving myself while forgetting my pure Being; this will show you your negligence towards me, the perfect Being of the Son of God the Father. 
• You who will not have been mindful of my Presence within you when I had just given myself to you in the Eucharist, you will recognize yourselves as children not very worthy of the Presence of God. You will feel an inner loneliness, you will know what you have done to me, the Presence. 
• You who will have neglected to come adore me, you will see your shortcoming, and you will feel uncomfortable before The Love, the King of kings; you will feel unworthy of so much love. 
• You who did not see the necessity of bending your knees or bowing your heads to adore me at the moment of the elevation of my Body and of my Blood, because you saw in it nothing more than   certain form of worship, you will be ashamed before your lack of regard towards me, the King of kings; I will show you what you were unable to see: my countless graces that I reserve only for my subjects. 
• You who will have profaned my sacred place and all that is enclosed within it, you will see yourselves deprived of all action. You will want to flee, for you will feel exposed. Because you will have violated my enclosure, your limbs will be immobilized and you will know that it is because of what you will have done. You, the renegades, you will be deprived of all regard for yourselves, for you will not have respected all that is sacred, and your entire being will be in pain, for you will feel what I, I felt when you committed that sacrilege against my place of love. 
• Beware, you who have practised: black masses, sacrifices, spells, satanic idolatry, etc., and also to you who took part in them, you will be before The Love whom you have betrayed. Because you have practised black masses by making sacrifices with the purpose of making souls perish, of harming God’s children, of obtaining through force what would satisfy your thirst for power, by sacrificing humans and by shedding the blood of God’s creatures, you have marked yourselves with the sign of the Beast. How you will suffer, you, the traitors! Why have you chosen so much suffering! You have only wanted to live in your being without thinking that I am the Life within you. You have condemned yourselves to eternal death; you will be what you will have wanted to be: vile beings for eternity. You will see all you have done against me; all your actions and all your thoughts will be joined together to whip you, you will know what it is like to have chains on your hands and feet and to be plunged into boiling water; all the instruments of torture you have used will torture you, all your hurtful words will reach you in your heart of hearts, every part of you will be in the pain of not being able to defend yourselves against this torture. What will be the worst for you, is knowing that all you have subjected me to will not have succeeded in destroying me nor in destroying the faith in those who love me. You have understood that everything you will be subjected to will be everything you have made me endure. Oh! how this will lead to your ruin, for an even greater rage against me will arise within you and it will turn against you, the beings given over to Satan. Do not believe that you are better than you are, Satan has deceived you and you will soon know what he has reserved for you; what I have just described to you is nothing compared to what is waiting for you in hell. 
• The Love will be in you and it is with my love in you that you will feel all these shortcomings. You alone will judge yourselves. You will not be able to flee your own judgement. You who have been given to me by my Father will live all this, as well as all of you whose names do not appear in the Book of Life. Even if we know you carry a no to The Love, you as well will live all this, but as you will have accepted to be evil in its purest state, shortly after the Great Purification, the earth will open its bowels to swallow you up so that there may never again be evil on The Love’s earth. It would have been better if you had never been born. 
• You who carry a yes to The Love, because I know all of you, my graces will sustain you, for I want you in me for eternity. When you will see me before you, you will know that I am the one who saved you from hell; I will eradicate from you all that has made you suffer, for I want to wrench all evil from you. I am your good Pastor and you, my lambs ; my lambs know me, this is why you will let yourselves be purified. You who do not want to prepare yourselves as of this moment, you will experience the Great Purification; all this will take place in enormous suffering. Why not respond to our call as of now? I, I responded to your call to save you, therefore I cannot be a Being who is negligent towards you; what you do not want me to be towards you, do not be so towards yourselves. My children, how I love you! I give myself, at every moment, on all the altars of the world to purify your offerings. Come offer me your lives so that every day I may purify everything. I am not asking you to come to mass every day, although my Heart would be glad of it, but come on Sunday. I venture to say once again that the end of this world of hatred is at hand, that this earth will be transformed by The Love; and so, come, my children, I, Jesus, I am waiting for you in the light of your interior. I love you. Amen."

He changed one word on the application

His LLC was registered as "real estate brokerage." NAICS code 531210. Chase's underwriting algorithm flags that code as high-risk lending. Automatic denial at anything over $30,000

His accountant told him to refile the LLC's business activity as "property management." NAICS code 531311. Same LLC. Same articles of organization. Same operations. Just a different 6-digit code on the Secretary of State website

Chase's system saw "property management" and approved him for $250,000 at 0% for 12 months across two Ink cards

$250,000 approved. $0 denied. Same human. Same business. One word on a state filing

High-risk NAICS codes that trigger automatic denials or reduced limits:

text:
Arab parties record number of seats in Israel's election  is often read as a simple reaction to Netanyahu, Ben-Gvir and the war in Gaza. This success was expected but the real result of success is much complex. Low turnout of the Arab communty since the fall of Camp David was mostly about the feeling of disappointment and the votes of the Arabs wouldn’t change much in the political system and according to pre-election surveys about only half of Arabs expected the elections to be free and fair. Arab community focused more on individual success and education in overall Israel, resulting with an amazingly high number of Arab doctors, lawyers and academics but lack of being kingmakers in domestic politics. So, what have changed that caused an increased turnout and overall votes of Arab Parties?

Joint List had 12 seats and Ra'am had 7. That is 19 seats in total, up from 10 in the previous Knesset. At least 730,000 people voted for the two lists, close to 16% of the Knesset. Turnout was the key to this as it has risen from %55 to %77. Much of this surge came from an accumulation of very specific, everyday problems. They rarely receive attention outside Arab communities. Houses, some built without permits, are demolished. Arab shopkeepers pay "protection" money to criminal Arab groups. Families fear stray bullets. Municipalities lose development funding. Many towns have no public bomb shelters. Violence within Arab society keeps rising. West Bank is turning into a powder keg with huge amount of smuggled guns that nobody knows why (For details: https://t.co/cuaFqjkJoC)

Add to this Ben-Gvir's policies. They brought more aggressive police operations into Arab communities. Yet many residents still feel that organised crime is tolerated. They see this as a longstanding, undeclared policy of non-intervention in Arab internal affairs. The state has also intervened more in local hamula(clan and extended-family) networks. These networks have traditionally shaped community affairs and politics. (For a detailed post on Hamula, which is extrmely important to understand the Arab society-Israeli state relations, check:  https://t.co/leuMrdCM2j)

These issues may seem unrelated but all together they help explain why people with little interest in national elections suddenly felt they had something to lose or gain by voting.

There are mainly three layers, where no single layer explains the result but all together it makes sense:
Grievancesgave people something to lose: housing, crime, policing, missing shelters and diverted funding.

Exclusion triggers in the final weeks turned grievance into urgency: the disqualification attempt, election-day rhetoric, the attack on Druze youths and pressure on students.

Mobilising capacity turned urgency into votes: a reunited Joint List, local candidates and a transformed Ra'am. Together, they do.

1. Housing demolitions and the fear of losing one's home
The housing issue in this election is not about punitive demolitions of Hezbullah, Hamas or lone wolf attackers family homes. That is a separate policy, applied mainly in the West Bank and East Jerusalem. The demolitions that mattered to Arab voters relate to planning and construction law.

Bedouin communities in the Negev have built homes and other structures without permits for many years. Enforcement is not new and previous governments also carried out demolitions. However the scale and intensity have grown considerably under the current government based on Ben-Gvir’s demands and pressure, not Netanyahu. There is an institutional reason for this. In mid-2024 the government moved the national unit that enforces planning and construction laws from the Finance Ministry to the National Security Ministry. That put it under Ben-Gvir, who later boasted of a 400% rise in demolition orders. Housing enforcement thus became a Ben-Gvir issue in a very literal sense.

The ministry's own figures show the result. In the Negev, demolitions and enforcement actions rose by 81% over three years compared with the previous three. In 2025 alone, government figures recorded 5,742 demolitions and related enforcement actions. These figures include various structures and measures, not only inhabited houses.

Roughly 300,000 Bedouins live in the Negev. Around 30% of them live in villages the state does not recognise and can anytime face with the wholesome demolition of the village.

Just 15 days before elections the vote, in Rahat and al-Dahiya villages a mosque and 80 inhabited homes destroyed, where about 400 people lived there, including 250 school-age children. Rahat’s turnout rose to %85, a record high in the recent elections and this fear caused all neighbouring villages to go to the ballot boxes.

Housing is already a serious problem in Israel, particularly in densely populated Arab communities. When a young man wants to marry he often tries to build a house next to his parents' home, if there is enough family land. Sometimes construction happens without a permit. Obtaining one is often difficult, expensive or impossible under existing planning arrangements. Even if all goes well Israeli bureaucracy is at turtle speed and while permits are being taken, someone making an official complaint can get the house demolished. This was not the case before Ben-Gvir, state was much more tolerant.

Outside the Negev, the 2017 Kaminitz Law changed the picture as well. It moved enforcement towards administrative orders and heavy fines. This affects Arab towns in the Galilee and the Triangle and Druze villages too.

For Bedouins, the situation is slightly different. A house or residential compound near family grazing areas and livestock is often tied to a traditional way of life. Such structures may lie far from established towns.

The fear is that if Ben-Gvir stays in government, enforcement will continue or intensify. The consequences are not limited to one person. A threatened house can affect an entire extended family, including children who have invested their savings in building near their parents. This is why the fear of losing a house can mobilise a whole community, regardless of broader debates about identity, nationalism or equality.

2. Umm al-Hiran and the fear of future displacement

The demolition of Umm al-Hiran in November 2024 had an impact far beyond the village itself. Umm al-Hiran was an unrecognised Bedouin village caught in a long legal dispute over land and construction. After court proceedings, the village was demolished to make way for a planned Jewish community called Dror. Residents were expected to move to the nearby Bedouin town of Hura.

One detail shows how powerless people felt. On 13 November 2024, residents began demolishing their own homes, a day before the state's demolitions were scheduled. Families facing final orders often choose this path to avoid paying the costs of a state demolition. Destroying one's own home with one's own hands is a powerful image of defeat. This can be something used against attackers homes to their relatives in Israel for Hezbollah or Hamas members but applying the same thing over ordinary people causes a mass anger.

For residents of other unrecognised villages, the lesson was clear. Even a community with a long history, established family networks and years of litigation could ultimately be removed. This creates an important psychological spillover effect. A family does not need a demolition order of its own to start worrying about its long-term security.

That is the biggest problem in Israel; there is no single applied law to all citizens, all the time. Haredim are different, West Bank settlements are different, West Bank’s illegal settlements are different, Arab towns are different, illegal Arab buildings get different treatment in Negev, West Bank or Wadi Ara, different practices in Druze area as well….This is creating an extremely complex and non-governable situation for a tiny country that makes everyone angry at the end.

3. The Tarabin al-Sana operation and Bedouin relations with the state
Tarabin al-Sana in the Negev may be the clearest example of how policing reshaped political attitudes. In late December 2025, after residents were accused of setting fire to cars in nearby Jewish communities, police encircled the village. The Border Police’s National Guard, a force founded under Ben-Gvir, sealed the entrances and checked the identity of everyone entering or leaving. During the operation, police shot dead a local father at the door of his home. Police said he endangered the officers, his family denied it, and Ben-Gvir praised the forces involved. The siege ended after twelve days, when police withdrew before a court could rule on the checkpoints.

The most revealing detail is political: the village had backed Likud in the previous election and expected its life to improve, which makes it a defection story in miniature. Bedouins have long had a complicated but often cooperative relationship with the security establishment. Many communities also enjoyed practical autonomy, because the state was largely absent and protection rackets filled the gap. That leaves them under-policed in daily life and over-policed in sudden operations. Some residents welcomed the crackdown as overdue action against criminals, while others saw it as collective punishment. Either way, it made questions of policing, autonomy and relations with the state very immediate.

4. Organised crime and the dilemma of policing Arab communities
Organised crime has soared in Arab communities under a government that puts security at the centre of its agenda. The crime rate is simply too skyrocketing among Arab communities. An Israel Democracy Institute survey from 31 August to 3 September 2026 found that 53.5% of Arab respondents named crime in Arab society as one of their two most important voting considerations. The same survey found that only 32% of Arab respondents saw 7 October as central to their vote, compared with 68% of Jewish respondents. This strongly supports the idea that domestic insecurity, not Gaza alone, drove Arab voters.

This issue is a double-edged sword. If the government intervenes more aggressively, it means more police, raids, arrests and checkpoints. It may also mean deeper involvement by security and intelligence agencies. Some residents fear their towns will become heavily policed communities.

If the government does not intervene, criminal organisations keep expanding. This reinforces the perception that the state has adopted an undeclared policy of non-intervention in Arab internal affairs.
There is also the sensitive issue of the hamula. Clan networks remain influential in many Arab communities. Aggressive policing can interfere with family relations, informal mediation and traditional authority.

An August 2026 survey for AJEEC-NISPED of 257 Arab citizens aged 18–26 found that 60% would consider voting for a non-Arab partywith convincing solutions. Only 48% said they were loyal exclusively to Arab parties. Their priorities were:
Crime and violence: 55%
Employment and income: 22%
Education: 20%
Housing: 19%

These findings suggest that many younger Arab voters are not driven mainly by ethnic or national identity. They want practical solutions, whoever offers them. Though, the actual vote complicates this picture.

5. Missing shelters: protected neither from gangs nor from missiles
Another grievance receives little attention abroad: the lack of bomb shelters. In June 2025, an Iranian missile hit a home in Tamra and killed four women. Tamra's mayor said only 40% of its 37,000 residents had a safe room or a working shelter, and the town had no public shelters at all. A later report found an almost total lack of public shelters in most Arab localities, including large cities like Umm al-Fahm and Rahat. About 100,000 Bedouins in some 35 unrecognised villages live in structures with no protected space at all. For many Arab citizens, the message is simple. The state protects them neither from gangs nor from missiles.

6. The controversial transfer of nearly half a billion shekels

In July 2026, Netanyahu’s government moved nearly half a billion shekels out of Resolution 550, the development plan for Arab society adopted under the Bennett–Lapid government, into a new campaign against organised crime. Most of the money went to the Shin Bet, with the rest going to a new police unit, and the plan also created permanent Shin Bet positions and annual funding. This was not a one-off transfer but a lasting security structure. The contradiction is obvious. Arab towns have demanded tougher action on crime for years, yet many residents fear that money meant for development, education and local government will instead strengthen the state’s ability to monitor and control them. The move was contested even inside government: the Labor Ministry objected because some funds had been earmarked for Arab employment, and rights lawyers argued the Shin Bet has no authority in criminal enforcement. Arab opinion was split too, as some local leaders called for Shin Bet involvement. Frustration with Resolution 550 predated the cut, since only a small fraction of its municipal development money had ever reached Arab towns. The real question, then, is not whether the state should fight crime, but whether Arab communities should pay for that fight with their own development funds.

7. The attempt to disqualify Arab parties may have backfired

In late September 2026, the Central Elections Committee disqualified both Ra’am and the Joint List, along with two individual candidates: Hadash’s Ofer Cassif and Balad chairman Sami Abu Shehadeh. In early October, the Supreme Court unanimously reinstated both lists and, by a majority, Cassif. Abu Shehadeh withdrew after the court signalled it would uphold his disqualification over an article he wrote the day after 7 October.

For several weeks, Arab voters faced the possibility that their main parties would not run at all. The outcome also produced two kinds of anger. The first was at a perceived double standard, since the court had let Ben-Gvir run despite his past convictions. The second was at Zionist opposition parties, including Golan’s Democrats, that supported Abu Shehadeh’s disqualification. That second grievance pushed voters towards Arab lists rather than the Jewish left.

The effort may therefore have backfired, turning a vote into an act of resisting exclusion. Its exact effect cannot be measured, but its timing, only weeks before the election, makes it hard to ignore.

8. Election-day warnings about Arab turnout
On election day, cars flying Likud flags drove through Jerusalem playing the Islamic call to prayer and urging people to vote because Arabs were voting. Netanyahu joined in. He warned of high Arab turnout, posted an AI-generated image of veiled Arab women queuing to vote, and claimed Arab voters were trying to steal the election. The groundwork had been laid earlier, with coalition parties sending activists to observe Arab polling stations and alleging fraud without evidence. After the vote, Likud claimed the Arab parties had “stolen” the election.

The aim was to mobilise right-wing Jewish voters by presenting Arab participation as a danger. Yet Arab citizens who see their vote portrayed as a threat may become more determined to cast it. Arab turnout did surge after Netanyahu’s midday messages. However, Arab localities have traditionally voted late in the day, so only a comparison with 2022’s hourly turnout can tell a backlash from an old habit.

9. The attack on Druze youths for speaking Arabic

One disturbing incident occurred just days before the election (For details: https://t.co/Qh0p7a8hPf)
Speaking Arabic in public has long been a normal part of everyday life in Israel. An argument that allegedly escalated into a stabbing because of the language spoken can therefore create a much wider sense of insecurity. It raised an uncomfortable question. If even Druze soldiers can be attacked after being mistaken for other Arabs, how safe is an ordinary Arabic-speaking citizen?

Its electoral effect should not be overstated, though. Druze voters traditionally support mainly Zionist parties. The incident's main significance was probably symbolic, not electoral. In my view, it may have resonated more widely among Arab speakers beyond the Druze community.

10. Arab voters did not want another 2022-style loss of representation
There was a straightforward electoral calculation. In 2022, Balad received 138,617 votes, or 2.91% of valid ballots. It missed the 3.25% threshold. Those votes were valid but produced no seats, roughly three to four seats' worth of wasted support. Meanwhile, Hadash–Ta'al and Ra'am each won five seats. Hadash, Ta'al and Balad agreed to run together again under the Joint List. Ra'am chose to run separately.

This changed the calculation for Balad supporters who feared wasting their vote again. A combined list reduced that risk. Voters could support their preferred political current without sacrificing representation.

11. Local candidates turned a national election into something like a municipal one

Arab parties made particularly effective use of candidates with strong local roots. In many Arab communities, municipal elections are shaped by extended families, clan networks, personal relationships and local loyalties. Turnout is usually much higher than in national elections, because people know the candidates and their families. National elections are usually less personal.

This time, local candidates brought that dimension into national politics. Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen comes from Umm al-Fahm. Ahmad Darawshe of Ta'al comes from Iksal. He is a lawyer, a former Iksal council member and the director-general of the Reineh local council. He moved up to eighth place after Abu Shehadeh's withdrawal, a realistic slot that gave his village a concrete stake in the result. Other post-election analyses have noted the same effect in Iksal and Umm al-Fahm.

The turnout figures are striking. According to a Globes analysis, Umm al-Fahm rose from 38.29% in 2022 to 79.92%. Nazareth rose from 48.29% to 73.42%, and Rahat from 60.61% to 84.79%. Sakhnin reached 86.20%. Election-night reports also gave Kafr Qasim 84.9%, Kuseife 81.2% and Hura 79.1%.

Umm al-Fahm, the city with the lowest turnout of the three in 2022, saw the largest rise. It is also the home town of the Joint List's leader and the most notorious city among Israeli Jews, where many of them stay away from the village. (For details on Umm al Fahm: https://t.co/76luyi8QtT)

A late surge of this size fits the mobilisation style of family and community networks, simply relatives checking who has not voted yet and driving them to the polls.

The obstacles make the result more impressive. In the Bedouin town of Segev Shalom, voters waited more than four hours. Some gave up and went home. The town's polling stations also served residents of unrecognised villages, some of whom travelled dozens of kilometres. Power was cut in Kuseife and Ar'arat an-Naqab.The structural cause is old. Since the mid-1980s, no polling stations have been placed in unrecognised villages.

Of course, the rise cannot be attributed entirely to local candidates. Opposition to the government and the wider political atmosphere also mattered. Nevertheless, the stronger use of local networks was a major organisational advantage. It may become a lasting feature of future national elections, if parties keep recruiting candidates who can mobilise support through family and community ties.

12. Ra'am's transformation: from Islamic Movement to civic party

Ra'am's 2026 campaign is usually reduced to one big surprise. A Jewish former police commander, Yoav Segalovitz was appointed as its number two, but Segalovitz was the second step of a deeper transformation, not the first.

Ra'am had long been the political wing of the Southern Branch of the Islamic Movement. The movement's Shura Council influenced the party's votes in the Knesset. In December 2025, Mansour Abbas announced that Ra'am would separate from it and become a "civic party". The separation was finalised in July 2026. On 5 January 2026, the party opened membership to all Israelis and declared that it wanted to recruit Jewish politicians. For the first time, party members, not religious institutions, chose the candidates.

Segalovitz is a former head of the Israel Police Investigations and Intelligence Division. He served as deputy public security minister in the Bennett–Lapid government and later sat in the Knesset for Yesh Atid. He made his move conditional on Ra'am recognising Israel as a Jewish state. According to i24NEWS, polls showed he was the only Jewish politician Arab citizens trusted.

On 31 August 2026, in Nazareth, Abbas presented him as number two on the list, the first Jewish candidate in Ra'am's history. Segalovitz joined the slate and the parliamentary faction but not the party itself. He kept the freedom to vote independently on religion and state, national security and LGBTQ rights. Abbas said Ra'am would seek responsibility for fighting crime if it returned to government, with Segalovitz at the centre of that effort.

The recruitment presented Ra'am as more than an Arab or Islamic party concerned mainly with identity. It offered a practical image: crime prevention, public security and participation in government. It may have appealed to Arab voters who do not put identity at the centre of their choice, including some who had previously voted for non-Arab parties.

The Moshe Dayan Center's May 2026 survey offers an important clue. 77.2% of Arab respondents supported an Arab party joining a governing coalition. Of these, 43.3% supported joining any government, while 33.9% preferred a centre-left government. Much of the Arab electorate wants influence over decisions, not permanent opposition

Comparing Circassians voting patterns with the latest election also will give interesting outcomes of Ra’am’s success. For the first time in my life I heard very openly from some of my Circassian friends about Abbas and Ra’am nice things. (For voting patterns of Isreali Circassians, check: https://t.co/zPIoKRxD2Z)

13. What now?

The results expose a coalition paradox. Netanyahu's bloc has about 53 seats, and the Change block 48. Add 19 Arab seats and the anti-Netanyahu camp reaches 67, above the 61 needed to govern. Yet this is a majority on paper, not a coalition.

Eisenkot promised a "Zionist government"; Liberman rejects cooperation with Ra'am or the Joint List. Yair Golan's Democrats favour it. The opposition has the numbers to replace Netanyahu, but not necessarily the willingness. Opposing Netanyahu is not the same as agreeing on a prime minister, a coalition programme or the role of Arab representatives.

The Arab parties also differ. Abbas is ready for Ra'am to join a coalition; the Joint List is willing to support one from outside, without ministries. Tibi's demands focus on fighting crime and halting Bedouin home demolitions. After a record result, their immediate priorities are the everyday grievances that brought voters to the polls, not only Gaza or Palestinian nationalism.

There are precedents. Rabin's minority government survived with external Arab-party support after Shas left in 1993, and Ra'am joined the Bennett–Lapid coalition in 2021–22. The obstacle is political, not constitutional. External support, formal coalition membership and backing on individual votes are different arrangements. They offer Arab parties different degrees of influence and impose different political costs on their partners.

That is also why Abbas recruited Yoav Segalovitz, a Jewish former police commander, as Ra'am's number two, to broaden its appeal and make coalition cooperation easier. But will Jewish-led parties treat Ra'am as a legitimate partner? Even those prepared to accept its votes may hesitate to offer cabinet positions or a formal agreement.

Eisenkot could rely on Arab parties from inside or outside government, seek another arrangement among Jewish-led parties, or fail to form a coalition and trigger another election.

The deeper issue is what this means for Arab participation. Low turnout has often reflected a belief that voting changes little. This election challenged that view. Arab voters showed up in record numbers and won unprecedented parliamentary weight. If even 19 seats cannot influence policy, frustration may return. If their representatives secure improvements in safety, housing, municipal funding and infrastructure even from outside government that could prove participation matters.

The test is no longer just how many seats Arab parties hold, but whether those seats can improve daily life. Arab voters have done their part. Now the question is whether the political system will allow their votes to count beyond election day.

text:
The suffering of others matters to me, and my faith calls me to care.

It is hard to understand why so many people who have advocated for peace have been demonized, persecuted, or even killed.
Why can’t we listen to different opinions without becoming so angry? Why do we sometimes try to silence one another, as though we wanted to bury the very truth that could save us: that PEACE is the only way we can survive together?

Across different times, faiths, and backgrounds, people have called for peace, dignity, and coexistence. Their beliefs and actions were not identical, but each offers something to reflect upon:

– Jesus Christ: Taught love of enemies, forgiveness, mercy, and peacemaking.

– Mahatma Gandhi: Advocated nonviolent resistance and peaceful coexistence between religious communities.

– Martin Luther King Jr.: Fought for racial equality through nonviolence and spoke against war, poverty, and injustice.

– Archbishop Óscar Romero: Defended the poor, condemned political violence, and pleaded with soldiers to stop killing their own people.

– Anwar Sadat: Helped negotiate peace between Egypt and Israel, taking political risks to pursue reconciliation.

– Yitzhak Rabin: Pursued negotiations with Palestinians and helped advance agreements intended to bring an end to generations of conflict.

– Sophie Scholl: Resisted Nazi tyranny through the White Rose movement, using words and nonviolent resistance to confront oppression.

– Franz Jägerstätter: Refused to serve in Hitler’s army because of his Christian conscience, accepting death rather than participating.

– The 14th Dalai Lama: Advocates nonviolence, compassion, dialogue, and a peaceful resolution to the Tibetan struggle.

– Liu Xiaobo: Advocated human rights and democratic change in China through peaceful means, enduring imprisonment for his beliefs.

– Avraham “Avrum” Burg: Advocates equal rights, dignity, and security for Palestinians and Jews, urging reconciliation and an end to cycles of revenge.

The list goes on…

Some of these people were killed; others were imprisoned, exiled, or publicly condemned. The circumstances and reasons differed, and recognizing their contributions does not require agreeing with everything they said or did.
We do not have to think alike to recognize one another’s humanity.
Perhaps peace begins there… when we choose to listen, when we refuse to dehumanize, and when another person’s suffering matters to us… even across our deepest disagreements.

We can speak firmly for love, peace, and truth while leaving room for others to disagree. A thoughtful disagreement does not have to become hatred.

May love, truth, and peace be the light that illuminates our path… here and throughout the world. 🙏🏻🕊️

text:
The narrative that China would be speaking Japanese without America is a textbook Hollywood-style simplification of WWII history. While the U.S. contribution was massive, framing America as the sole "savior" completely ignores the military and geopolitical reality of the Asian theater.

Here is the actual historical breakdown: 👇

🛡️ 1. The Quagmire: Who Really Held the Line?
Years before Pearl Harbor and the U.S. entry into the war, China had already been fighting the absolute bulk of the Imperial Japanese Army alone. Japan, a resource-poor island nation, attempted a "snake swallowing an elephant" strategy. Millions of elite Japanese troops were permanently bogged down in China's massive territorial depth. It was precisely because Japan was bleeding out its resources in this Chinese quagmire that it desperately expanded into the Pacific for oil and rubber, ultimately triggering U.S. involvement.

⏳ 2. An "Accelerator", Not a "Savior"
We deeply acknowledge the U.S. Pacific campaign. The atomic bombs drastically accelerated the end of the war and saved countless lives. However, based on the famous On Protracted War military strategy, Japan's defeat was already a strategic certainty. A resource-starved island could never permanently subjugate a massive continent of 400 million people willing to trade space for time. America's entry changed the timeline of the victory, but not the inevitable ultimate outcome.

🛑 3. The Side Effect: Japan's Psychological Excuse
Ironically, because the U.S. ended the war with the sudden "deus ex machina" of nuclear weapons—and later monopolized the post-war occupation, keeping the Emperor in power for Cold War expediency—it created a massive historical loophole. It allowed Japanese right-wingers to build a coping narrative: "We didn’t lose to China; we only lost to American industrial might and atomic tech." Because Japan was not thoroughly crushed on the ground by the nations it victimized, it has never offered a sincere, "German-style" apology to Asia.

🌍 TL;DR:
The Allied victory was built on immense, shared sacrifices. Erasing China’s 14 years of brutal resistance and tens of millions of casualties to frame the U.S. as the sole "savior" isn't just historically illiterate—it's deeply disrespectful to those who held the line for the rest of the world.

#WWII #MilitaryHistory #Geopolitics #PacificWar #HistoryFacts #ColdWar #GlobalHistory

So maybe what you really need to ask is "Why are people telling me lies? What do they or their sponsors gain from it?"
