text:
Why are there 64 Yoginis? The mystery of the number

The number 64 has a prominent place in several Indian religious and cultural systems.
One possible explanation for the Yogini grouping is the relationship between eight and sixty-four:
8X8 = 64 
The eight Mother Goddesses, or related groups of eight divine powers, offer one framework for understanding how the larger assembly may have developed.
The number also appears in Tantric classifications of deities, sacred teachings and spiritual accomplishments. Some scholars have suggested connections between the 64 Yoginis and the 64 siddhis, although this should be treated as a possible association rather than an established single origin for the entire tradition. 
Here is the crucial complication: not all Yogini temples contain exactly 64 shrines, and not all textual lists contain the same names.
The Bhedaghat temple, for example, has 81 peripheral shrines. Some other temple groups have been associated with 42 Yoginis, while the number of figures identified at certain sites remains uncertain. The name Chausath Yogini therefore cannot automatically be taken as an exact archaeological count in every case. 
This variation tells us something important about medieval religious life: the Yogini tradition was not one perfectly uniform system imposed across the entire subcontinent. It developed through multiple regions, texts, artistic traditions and ritual communities.

Why were the temples circular and open to the sky?

The surviving Yogini temples are among the most distinctive examples of medieval Indian sacred architecture.
Their principal features often include a circular or otherwise enclosed arrangement of shrines, numerous inward-facing niches and an open courtyard.
The architectural pattern is frequently discussed in relation to the mandala and chakra—sacred diagrams or arrangements that organise space and divine powers. Such interpretations are especially relevant because some Tantric texts prescribe structured arrangements of deities for ritual purposes. 
Consider what makes this architecture different.
In a conventional temple layout, a devotee may approach a principal shrine and direct attention towards one central deity. In a Yogini temple, the surrounding assembly becomes central to the experience: many figures occupy their own places within a larger sacred arrangement.
At Hirapur, the small circular structure creates an intimate relationship between the visitor, the sculptures and the open sky.
This does not prove that the temples were designed for one specific ritual or that every Yogini shrine followed the same symbolic plan. However, the combination of architectural layout and Tantric textual evidence makes the mandala interpretation a significant line of scholarly inquiry.

Were the 64 Yoginis connected to women who held power in society?

This question deserves careful treatment because it is easy to romanticise the past.
Yogini traditions provide evidence that certain medieval religious communities imagined feminine power in extraordinary forms. They also preserve evidence of female practitioners who could participate in specialised ritual traditions.
But three things must be distinguished:
1Divine authority: A goddess could possess tremendous cosmic, ritual or martial power in religious imagination.
2Ritual authority: Some women could act as initiated practitioners within particular Tantric systems.
3Social and political authority: The rights, opportunities and status of actual women varied widely by region, community, class and historical period.
These categories do not automatically correspond to one another. The presence of powerful goddesses does not by itself establish that women enjoyed social equality.
At the same time, the evidence of women receiving initiation in certain Śākta traditions complicates the idea that women were universally excluded from authoritative religious practise in medieval India.s practice in medieval India.

Dylan Stewart: First-Step Fire, First-Round Potential

South Carolina’s explosive edge flashes NFL upside, while Simmons and Clowney set the production standard.

Dylan Stewart’s first step keeps bringing me back to his first-round potential. At 6’5”, 250 pounds, South Carolina’s edge defender offers the frame and acceleration that make his development worth watching against premier SEC tackles.

My evaluation centers on translating that athleticism into repeatable wins. Against Tennessee, Stewart delivered two tackles, one sack and a forced fumble, with his late strip sack helping position South Carolina for the winning field goal. He also recorded a sack against Florida.

Through four appearances, Stewart has two sacks, three tackles for loss and three forced fumbles. His 0.50 sacks per game represents a 22.2% improvement over 2025. However, that measures finishing frequency; verified matchup pressure rates against individual SEC tackles require pressures and pass-rush snaps unavailable in my dataset.

Texas’ Colin Simmons currently owns the stronger production case: 10.5 sacks in six appearances, or 1.75 per game, 3.5 times Stewart’s pace. Different opportunities and unequal samples matter, but Stewart needs more consistent disruption to close that gap.

Jadeveon Clowney provides the school’s ultimate benchmark. Through two seasons, Stewart produced 11 sacks and 22.5 tackles for loss versus Clowney’s 21 and 35.5. The former No. 1 pick’s dominance remains a substantially higher standard.

My NFL comparison is Jacksonville’s Josh Hines-Allen: a taller, speed-oriented edge archetype. Stewart must strengthen his counters, leverage and finishing through contact. I see first-round upside, with his next step defined by sustained pressure against elite protection. His athletic tools create the opportunity; consistent execution will determine how high he climbs.

text:
Follow Up: After Winter Park, What Changed for Nevada

The incident involving three year old soccer player Nevada Pierre in Winter Park, Florida, has developed into a national story, drawing support from former professional players, sports organizations and members of the public.

Within days of the October 24 incident, former U.S. men's national team striker Eddie Johnson offered Nevada an opportunity to train at his EJE7 Soccer Academy in Orlando. According to reports citing Nevada's family, he is expected to begin training there in January. Johnson has also spoken publicly about the barriers facing children of color in youth soccer.

Roc Nation Sports has publicly expressed support for Nevada. Reports published on October 28 and 29 said the organization was planning a trip to Spain in December to explore opportunities for his development. However, the specific arrangements have not been publicly confirmed by the company.

Financial and social media support has also grown rapidly. The Economic Times reported on October 29 that a GoFundMe campaign titled Support Nevada's Soccer Journey had raised $53,909. The fundraiser is intended to cover expenses including registration, training, equipment and travel. Reports have also described a sharp increase in the family's social media following, although follower counts can change quickly.

The incident has put i9 Sports under public scrutiny. The organization said it had contacted the family and begun reviewing what happened. It maintains that police were called over a dispute involving adults. Winter Park police described the incident as a civil matter and stated that no one was arrested, trespassed or forced to leave the park.

The accounts of the dispute differ. Nevada's parents have said they believed their son was being penalized for his soccer ability, while a league official told police that the child had been pushing other players and that the adults were causing a disturbance. The available footage does not, by itself, establish every detail of the confrontation.

For now, the clearest development is that Nevada has received an offer of further training in Orlando, with a possible trip to Spain reported but not fully confirmed. His family's next steps will determine how those opportunities develop, while the broader controversy has raised questions about how recreational leagues should accommodate young children with unusually advanced skills.

Welcome to Florida's Nudist Wonderland Pasco County!

It's that time of year again! Our northern nudist friends are heading south, and here in Florida, especially Pasco County, we're ready to welcome you!

Whether you're escaping the cold for a few weeks, spending the winter with us, or visiting for the very first time, there's plenty to enjoy in one of America's best-known nudist destinations, but before you pack your bags (and leave most of your clothes behind), there are a few things worth knowing!

Pasco County is home to a variety of nudist resorts and communities, each offering its own atmosphere, activities, amenities, and experiences. From swimming pools, hot tubs, saunas, and fitness centers to pickleball, tennis, hiking trails, social events, and much more, there's no shortage of ways to enjoy life clothes-free!

However, not all nudist resorts operate the same way.
Some are clothing-optional, allowing guests to decide when and where they prefer to be nude. Others are nude only, with policies requiring nudity in designated areas or during certain activities. We also have a few clothing-optional lifestyle resorts that cater to a different atmosphere, particularly during evening hours when activities may become more adult oriented.

There's nothing wrong with understanding these differences. In fact, that's exactly why we encourage everyone, especially first-time visitors, to do a little research before choosing where to stay or visit.

Know before you go!

Check each resort's website, review its policies, explore its amenities, and make sure the environment aligns with what you're looking for, this helps everyone make informed choices.

At Kick Ass Nudists, our mission has always been to educate, encourage, and promote the freedom, body acceptance, and community that social nudism offers, and here in Pasco County, there's certainly plenty to celebrate!

So, to all our returning snowbirds, welcome back! And to those making their first trip south, welcome to the Nudist Wonderland!

We hope your stay is filled with sunshine, friendship, relaxation, and plenty of clothes-free adventures. As always, it's a great day to get your clothes off and your nude on, right here in Pasco County!

text:
🇺🇦🇷🇺 ZELENSKYY'S INTERVIEW REVEALS WHAT FIVE YEARS OF PUTIN'S WAR HAVE DONE TO HIM 💔

There is a moment in Volodymyr Zelenskyy's interview with Steven Bartlett that is difficult to forget.

Asked how he is doing, the Ukrainian president explains that he barely sleeps. His nights are spent following military communications, making decisions about air defences and trying to determine which Ukrainian cities can be protected with the limited systems available.

Nearly five years into Russia's full-scale invasion, even sleep has become something he cannot take for granted.

But the most painful moments come when he talks about the people he has lost.

He describes presenting posthumous awards to the families of fallen Ukrainian soldiers. A father approaches to receive his son's decoration, shakes the president's hand and quietly asks whether they can embrace.

Zelenskyy says these encounters leave him emotionally devastated. He knows that nothing he says, no medal he presents and no embrace he offers can bring those families back to the lives they had before.

He also recalls the horror of children killed by Russian missiles, including an attack on a playground, and the discovery of murdered civilians in Bucha after Russian forces withdrew.

These experiences help explain his frustration with demands that Ukraine simply accept a quick peace agreement.

How do you tell families who have buried their children that they must surrender more territory to the country responsible for invading their homeland? And what guarantee would prevent another invasion after the fighting stops?

At one point, Bartlett shows him photographs from his earlier life: Kryvyi Rih, comedy performances, his work voicing Paddington Bear and his television career in Servant of the People.

The contrast is extraordinary. Before becoming a wartime president, Zelenskyy was an entertainer whose work was built around making people laugh. Now his daily responsibilities involve missile interceptions, destroyed cities, military casualties and families waiting for news of missing relatives.

The interview also exposes the enormous distance between Ukraine's wartime reality and the political calculations of its allies.

While Ukrainian cities endure Russian attacks on their energy infrastructure, Zelenskyy faces American pressure over Ukrainian strikes against Russian oil facilities and their potential impact on fuel prices.

For Washington, energy costs are a political issue. For Kyiv, striking infrastructure connected to Russia's war effort is part of a struggle for survival.

Zelenskyy can be criticized, questioned and held accountable for his decisions. Wartime leadership does not place anyone beyond scrutiny.

But this interview offers something that political arguments often overlook: a glimpse of the human being carrying those responsibilities.

Watch the interview. Especially the moments when he talks about the families of fallen soldiers.

Those are the moments that stay with you.

THE EVIDENCE™
PENTAGON ANNOUNCES IT WILL BEGIN BUYING MILITARY EQUIPMENT ON DEALDASH

Defense Officials Say America's Next Aircraft Carrier Could Cost Just $37.50—Provided Nobody Outbids Them

By Kim Wojcinski | USA Best Selling Author
SATIRE | FICTIONAL NEWS REPORT

The evidence will be presented. The verdict is yours.
WASHINGTON, D.C. — In a sweeping overhaul of military procurement, the Pentagon has announced that it will abandon its traditional defense contracting procedures and begin purchasing weapons, aircraft, ships, and other military equipment through DealDash, the online penny-auction platform famous for advertising expensive merchandise at remarkably low winning prices.

The decision follows an internal review revealing that the Pentagon has been spending billions of dollars on equipment that might be available online for considerably less, assuming someone remembers to place the final bid.

"Why should American taxpayers spend $150 million on a fighter jet when somebody just bought a $900 television for $28.43?" asked the newly appointed Undersecretary of Defense for Bargain Hunting. "The mathematical implications are staggering."

According to Pentagon officials, the initiative could fundamentally change America's military readiness, defense budget, and relationship with the military-industrial complex.

It could also require several thousand generals to learn how online auctions work.

EXHIBIT ONE — THE NEW DEFENSE PROCUREMENT STRATEGY

Under the revised system, defense contractors will no longer receive multibillion-dollar contracts simply because they manufacture sophisticated weapons systems. Instead, they will be encouraged to list their equipment on DealDash, where Pentagon purchasing officers will compete against ordinary consumers for deeply discounted merchandise.

A preliminary procurement exercise reportedly identified a brand-new F-35 fighter aircraft with an opening bid of one cent.

Unfortunately, after seven hours of aggressive bidding, the Pentagon lost the aircraft to a retired substitute teacher from Des Moines who had been trying to purchase an air fryer.

The woman has declined the Pentagon's offer to buy the aircraft back, explaining that she has already promised it to her grandson for Christmas.

Military officials are reportedly exploring whether the aircraft can be classified as a household appliance for purposes of an emergency government recall.

EXHIBIT TWO — THE AIRCRAFT CARRIER AUCTION

The Navy has expressed particular enthusiasm for the new purchasing arrangement after discovering that an aircraft carrier valued at approximately $13 billion could theoretically sell for less than $50.

Admirals gathered at the Pentagon to watch the bidding, which began at one cent and continued through the night.

By 3:00 a.m., the Navy had established a commanding position with a bid of $37.49. Victory appeared certain until an unidentified bidder using the screen name GrandmaKnowsBest1942 increased the price to $37.50.

The Navy's purchasing officer attempted to respond, but his government-issued computer required a mandatory security update.

The aircraft carrier was subsequently awarded to Grandma, who has requested delivery before Thanksgiving and wants to know whether assembly is required.

EXHIBIT THREE — THE ARMY DISCOVERS THE BUY IT NOW OPTION

The Army initially celebrated the discovery that military vehicles could be purchased through online auctions without submitting 4,000 pages of procurement documentation.

However, the enthusiasm diminished when senior officers learned that every additional bid required the purchase of bidding credits.

One general reportedly spent $6.8 million in bidding fees attempting to acquire a $400,000 armored personnel carrier.

He eventually won the auction for $16.73.

The Pentagon immediately announced that the transaction represented a savings of $399,983.27, although congressional auditors have requested clarification concerning the additional $6.8 million.

Defense officials dismissed the concern, noting that government accounting has never been particularly constrained by arithmetic.

EXHIBIT FOUR — THE CHINESE MILITARY ENTERS THE BIDDING

National security analysts have raised concerns that foreign adversaries could participate in the same auctions.

During a recent demonstration, Pentagon officials attempted to purchase six attack helicopters, only to discover that an individual using the screen name DefinitelyNotChina was bidding against them.

The bidding continued for eleven hours before the Pentagon's purchasing officer fell asleep.

All six helicopters were subsequently shipped to an undisclosed address overseas.

The Defense Intelligence Agency is investigating, although officials acknowledge that the bidder's username provides few clues concerning his possible nationality.

Meanwhile, the Pentagon has proposed a new defensive strategy involving automatic bidding software capable of preventing foreign governments from obtaining American weapons systems at garage-sale prices.

Congress has already authorized $14 billion for development.

EXHIBIT FIVE — CONGRESS DEMANDS ITS SHARE OF THE SAVINGS

Congressional leaders welcomed the initiative after learning that substantial reductions in military procurement costs could free billions of dollars for other government priorities.

Within hours, lawmakers introduced legislation requiring that any savings be redirected toward a $40 billion federal study of how Americans respond psychologically to winning online auctions.

A separate committee proposed establishing the National Defense Bargain Acquisition Administration, staffed by 12,000 federal employees responsible for monitoring auctions, approving bids, and determining whether free shipping is available.

The agency's projected annual operating budget is $19 billion.

When questioned about the apparent contradiction between saving money and creating another expensive bureaucracy, a congressional spokesperson explained that the government could not responsibly save taxpayer dollars without first establishing a federal agency to supervise the savings.

EXHIBIT SIX — THE PENTAGON'S FIRST MAJOR SUCCESS

Despite several setbacks, the Pentagon announced its first successful acquisition late Wednesday evening.

After intense bidding against 47 competitors, the Department of Defense secured what officials described as a strategically important piece of military equipment.

The winning price was $3.82.

The item was a tactical flashlight.

Unfortunately, batteries were not included.

The Pentagon has requested an emergency supplemental appropriation of $7.4 million to locate compatible batteries, conduct environmental impact studies, and establish whether the flashlight complies with existing military illumination standards.

Delivery is expected sometime in 2031.

THE VERDICT

For decades, the Pentagon has struggled with cost overruns, procurement delays, expensive weapons programs, and defense contractors whose invoices occasionally resemble the national debt of a developing country.

DealDash now offers Washington an entirely new approach to military acquisition: spend millions competing for equipment, celebrate winning bids of a few dollars, and establish a government agency to explain why the savings never materialized.

The Pentagon remains optimistic.

After all, when an aircraft carrier can theoretically be purchased for $37.50, who needs a defense budget approaching a trillion dollars?

The only remaining question is whether the United States can afford to keep bidding.

The evidence has been presented. The verdict is yours.

Danielle Reiff appears repeatedly throughout the “democracy files” exposed by @DataRepublican, @SKDoubleDub33 and @iamlisalogan .

She’s a former State Department diplomat and RAD co-coordinator involved in emergency scenario planning, tabletop exercises and discussions about governors, a “Third Continental Congress” and alternative leadership during a federal legitimacy crisis.

The more I watch this September 8 meeting, the less it feels like a normal panel discussion and the more it feels like a sales pitch.

The organizers made Reiff a co-host, gave her a dedicated presentation slot and said they were “front-loading” the meeting around Washington Secretary of State Steve Hobbs’s scheduled arrival.

They then introduced her as a “key leader” in Renew to Thrive and told Hobbs she was about to present “real thought work” taking place across the country.

Reiff starts by establishing her credentials and explaining the RAD strategy.

She then walks everyone through three “democratic emergency” scenarios: an election meltdown, an Insurrection Act deployment and elected members of Congress being denied their seats.

Then she gets to the proposed response.

If the federal government became “literally illegitimate,” Reiff said they were discussing “provisional or transitional leadership.”

She floated a “cross-partisan group of governors” temporarily keeping the country running, possibly with former Presidents Bush and Obama helping lead the response.

Hobbs listened to the entire presentation.

When she finished, he told her, “Danielle, that was great. I’d love to maybe talk to you over a beer,” and said he had held similar conversations with members of the German parliament and the Japanese government.

Later, Hobbs called the federal government “kind of” an enemy of his office, offered his civic-engagement team to the organizations on the call and agreed to continued coordination.

His Civic Engagement Program manager described the office as a “nexus” for outside organizations and said they had “the seal of the secretary” behind them.

Faith leaders also presented their clergy rapid-response network, which they said was aligned with people’s organizations and labor leaders to “protect the election and protect election results.”

To be clear, Hobbs never openly endorsed the transitional-leadership proposal.

But the sequence matters.

Reiff presented the threat, introduced RAD’s framework, offered a proposed response and left with new relationships and continued access to a sitting Secretary of State’s official team.

I cut the more than two-hour recording down to eight minutes so everyone can watch the most important parts for themselves and hear the statements in context.

It looks a lot less like an academic conversation and a lot more like an effort to get public officials and outside organizations aligned with the plan.

Dr. Tom Prichard: From Portland Wrestling to Training the Legends!

@drtomprichard  JOINS RINGSIDE IN ROSE CITY!

What happens when a young wrestling fan gets his first lesson in the ring from the Iron Sheik—and refuses to quit?

He becomes Dr. Tom Prichard: champion, world traveler, mentor, and one of professional wrestling's most respected teachers.

This week, Frank Culbertson and wrestling historian Mike Rodgers welcome Dr. Tom for an unforgettable conversation spanning more than four decades of wrestling history.

From the Houston wrestling office to Don Owen's Portland territory, from Japan to WWE, Tom shares the people, places, and lessons that shaped his remarkable career.

INSIDE THIS EPISODE:

PAUL BOESCH AND THE IRON SHEIK: How a $75-a-week job in Houston opened the door to wrestling—and the punishing first workout that convinced Tom he would do whatever it took.

THE ROAD TO PORTLAND: Why his planned 1980 arrival was delayed, and what he learned wrestling in Los Angeles before reaching the Northwest in 1984.

DON OWEN'S TERRITORY: Why Portland was such a valuable place to learn, and what veterans like Rip Oliver, Buddy Rose, and the Cuban Assassin taught him about telling stories in the ring.

JIM CORNETTE—ONE OF THE GREATEST EVER? Where does Dr. Tom rank @TheJimCornette  among wrestling's legendary managers?  He also discusses Cornette's remarkable mind for the business and their years together in Smoky Mountain Wrestling.

LIFE AT THE BOMBER: The legendary wrestler hangout, wild nights, and road-trip adventures with Matt Borne and Brett Sawyer—including a terrifying drive on an icy mountain road.

RIC FLAIR: Tom recalls two NWA World Championship opportunities and the reassuring words of the Nature Boy before their matches.

JAPAN: A tour featuring the Wild Samoans, Bad News Allen, and a police-car incident you have to hear to believe.

PERSONAL ISSUES AND REAL HEAT: Why Tom believes emotional storytelling still matters—and how wrestling has changed for modern audiences.

TRAINING THE McMAHONS: What it was like working one-on-one with Vince McMahon, and why Shane was a completely different student.

THE NEXT GENERATION: Tom discusses Darby Allin, authenticity, high-risk wrestling, and his concerns about the physical toll on today's performers.

MORE THAN JUST WRESTLING STORIES

Beyond the laughs and incredible road stories, Tom offers something special: a thoughtful look at what makes a wrestler believable, why experienced performers should help younger talent succeed, and how the fundamentals survive even as the business changes.

From getting stretched by the Iron Sheik to teaching some of wrestling's biggest names, Dr. Tom Prichard has seen the business from almost every angle.

And he's sharing those experiences with us!

COMING SOON: PRETTY BOY DOUG MASTERS!

Another Portland favorite joins us to discuss his career in the Northwest and beyond, including Puerto Rico and the USWA.

Follow Ringside in Rose City on Spotify, Apple Podcasts, and YouTube. New episodes every Thursday!

Mike Rodgers' Excitement in the Air series, including his earlier interview with Dr. Tom Prichard in Volume One, is available on Amazon.

text:
She stepped to the mic like the room was her stage,
Smiling as if virtue had granted her wage.
A campus applause for the cleverest line—
Celebrating a bullet, then calling it fine.

She framed murder as verse, anniversary cheer,
A neck-shot remembered as something to hear.
No pause for the man, or the wife, or the child—
Just glee in the cadence, self-righteous and wild.

Entitled enough to demand that we nod,
To treat death as content, and silence as fraud.
She warned of the neck left uncovered and bare,
Then basked in the spotlight for daring to care—

About nothing but her own glittering spite,
A poem of blood for a late-evening light.
Houston-raised, campus-trained, fluent in sneer,
She offered the crowd what it wanted to hear:

That some lives are punchlines, some deaths are the point,
And arrogance dressed as the voice of the joint.
The verse was the tell, not the venue or name—
The pleasure she took in the killing’s acclaim.

No sorrow, no weight, just the performance of hate,
Recited with pride on the Kirkiversary date.

text:
@johnkiriakou John, I respect your right to scrutinise Netanyahu and his government. My disagreement is not with holding political leaders accountable, but with a framing that, in my view, substitutes rhetorical certainty for evidentiary precision. ⚖️

**First, electoral setbacks and the loss of power are not interchangeable.** Your post says that Netanyahu’s coalition is “poised” to fall from 68 seats to 52. Before treating that as an established outcome, we need to know whether these figures represent a poll, a projection, or certified results.

Israeli history offers a useful warning against premature conclusions: in **2009, Tzipi Livni’s Kadima won 28 seats and Netanyahu’s Likud won 27, yet Netanyahu ultimately formed the government**. Parliamentary politics is determined not merely by who finishes first, but by who can assemble a viable coalition. That precedent does not prove Netanyahu will survive; it demonstrates why “bye bye Bibi” is a question, not a conclusion. [Historical background](https://t.co/QipvLg4Jf7)

**Second, allegations of electoral fraud require evidence—not ethnic insinuations.** If Netanyahu has accused Arab Israeli voters of mass fraud, those allegations must be tested against verifiable evidence. Arab citizens’ opposition to a government is an exercise of democratic rights, not evidence of wrongdoing.

The **2020 US election** illustrates the danger of allowing political repetition to masquerade as proof: prominent statistical claims of systematic fraud did not withstand rigorous examination. I would apply the same evidentiary standard to Netanyahu as to Trump—or to any politician I happen to support. [Research published in PNAS](https://t.co/ER6ddwWAEH)

**Third, I find the phrase “a penchant for committing terrorism” analytically inadequate.** This is not because a state leader should be immune from grave accusations. On the contrary: allegations involving unlawful attacks, civilian deaths, or other violations of international law deserve precise documentation and serious investigation.

But a sweeping label does not establish which acts occurred, who ordered them, or what responsibility follows. **Demanding precision is not defending Netanyahu; it is strengthening the case for accountability.** Nor should criticism of one leader become collective blame against Israelis, Jews, Palestinians, or Arabs. 🕊️

**Finally, an alleged Saudi offer of one billion dollars to the Houthis needs context before judgment.** A payment tied to humanitarian relief, a negotiated settlement, or an unrestricted transfer to an armed organisation would raise very different questions. The screenshot’s subtitle itself says “allegedly”; that uncertainty should remain visible.

The **1998 Good Friday Agreement** shows that negotiating with parties linked to armed movements can help advance peace—but through a broader framework of political participation, power-sharing, and commitments concerning disarmament, not simply a financial transaction. Northern Ireland is not Yemen, but the distinction between a structured peace process and an unaccountable payoff matters. [BBC historical overview](https://t.co/CqSGUSJ3Kv)

**My position is therefore neither pro-Netanyahu nor anti-Kiriakou. It is pro-evidence, pro-consistency, and pro-accountability.** I can oppose a government’s conduct without accepting every accusation against it, and support diplomacy without assuming every proposed deal is wise.

🔎 **Criticism becomes more compelling—not less—when it is precise, proportionate, and historically informed.**

#EvidenceMatters #HistoricalContext #HumanRights #Accountability #ResponsibleDebate

Was the Mi‘raj Spiritual or Bodily?

Did the Prophet Muhammad (sa) ascend to the heavens with his physical body, or was the Mi‘raj merely a spiritual experience?

The Promised Messiah (as) explained that the Mi‘raj was neither an ordinary dream nor an ascent of the soul alone. Rather, the Holy Prophet (sa) ascended in a state of spiritual wakefulness with a subtle, luminous and heavenly body, while his ordinary elemental body remained upon the bed.

He distinguished between the earthly, elemental body and the spiritual body, explaining that the Mi‘raj was both bodily and spiritual, as well as spatial and temporal.

This distinction offers a deeper understanding of the nature of prophetic visions, miracles and the unseen in Islamic theology.

text:
The Twenty-Second Sunday After Pentecost: From The Liturgical Year of Dom Prosper Gueranger.
.
.
Green Semidouble.
.
According to Honorius of Autun, the Mass of today has reference to the days of Antichrist. The Church, foreseeing the reign of the man of sin, and as though she were actually undergoing the persecution, which is to surpass all others—she takes her Introit of this twenty-second Sunday from the Psalm De profundis.
.
If, unitedly with this prophetic sense, we would apply these words practically to our own personal miseries, we must remember the Gospel we had eight days ago, and which, formerly, was the one appointed for the present Sunday. Each one of us will recognize himself in the person of the insolvent debtor, who has nothing to trust to but his master’s goodness; and in our deep humiliation, we shall exclaim, If thou, O Lord, mark iniquities, who shall endure it?
.
Introit
.
Si iniquitates observaveris, Domine, Domine, quia sustinebit? quia apud te propitiato est, Deus Israel.
.
If Thou, O Lord, wilt mark iniquities, Lord! who shall endure it? For with Thee there is merciful forgiveness, O God of Israel!
.
Ps. De profundis clamavi ad te, Domine: Domine, exaudi vocem meam. Gloria Patri. Si iniquitates.
.
Ps. Out of the depths have I cried unto Thee, O Lord: Lord! hear my voice. Glory, &c. If Thou.
.
We have just been rousing our confidence, by singing, that with God, there is merciful forgiveness. It is He Himself Who gives that loving unction to the prayers of the Church, which proves that He wishes to grant them. But we shall not be thus graciously heard, as she is, unless, like her, we ask with faith, that is to say, conformably with the teachings of the Gospel. To ask with faith is to forgive our fellow creatures their trespasses against us; on that condition we may confidently beseech our common Lord and Master to forgive us.
.
Collect
.
Deus, refugium nostrum, et virtus: adeato piis Ecclesiæ tuæ precibus, auctor ipse pietatis, et præsta: ut quod fideliter petimus, efficaciter consequamur. Per Dominum.
.
O God, our refuge and strength! give ear to the holy prayers of Thy Church, O Thou, the Author of holiness; and grant that what we ask with faith, we may effectually obtain. Through, etc.
.
The other Collects, as in the Fourth Sunday After Pentecost.
.
Epistle
.
Lectio Epistolæ beati Pauli Apostoli ad Philippenses.
.
Lesson of the Epistle of St. Paul, the Apostle, to the Philippians.
.
Cap. i. Ch. i.
.
Fratres, Confidimus in Domino Jesu, quia qui coepit in vobis opus bonum, perficiet usque in diem Christi Jesu: sicut est mihi justum hoc sentire pro omnibus vobis: eo quod habeam vos in corde, et in vinculis meis, et in defensione, et confirmatione Evangelii, socios gaudii mei omnes vos esse. Testis enim mihi est Deus, quomodo cupiam omnes vos in visceribus Jesu Christi. Et hoc oro, ut caritas vestra magis ac magis abundet in scientia, et in omni sensu: ut probetis potiora, ut sitis sinceri, et sine offensa in diem Christi, repleti fructu justitiae per Jesum Christum, in gloriam et laudem Dei.
.
Brethren: We are confident of this very thing, that He, Who hath begun a good work in you, will perfect it unto the day of Christ Jesus. As it is meet for me to think this for you all, for that I have you in my heart; and that in my bands, and in the defence and confirmation of the gospel, you all are partakers of my joy. For God is my witness, how I long after you all in the bowels of Jesus Christ. And this I pray, that your charity may more and more abound in knowledge, and in all understanding: That you may approve the better things, that you may be sincere and without offence unto the day of Christ, Filled with the fruit of justice, through Jesus Christ, unto the glory and praise of God.
.
St. Paul, in the Church’s name, again invites our attention to the near approach of the Last Day. But what, on the previous Sunday, he called the evil day, he now, in the short passage taken from his Epistle to the Philippians, which has just been read to us, calls, and twice over, the day of Christ Jesus. The Epistle to the Philippians is full of loving confidence; its tone is decidedly one of joy; and yet it plainly shows us that persecution was raging against the Church, and that the old enemy was making capital of the storm, to stir up evil passions, even amidst the very flock of Christ. The Apostle is in chains; the envy and treachery of false brethren intensify his sufferings; still, joy predominates in his heart over everything else, because he is come to that perfection of love, wherein divine charity is enkindled by suffering more even than by the sweetest spiritual caresses. To him, to live is Christ, and to die is gain; he cannot make up his mind which of the two to choose—death, which would give him the bliss of being with his Jesus—or life, which will add to his merits and his labors for the salvation of men. What are all personal considerations to him? His one joy, for both the present and the future is that Christ may be known and glorified, no matter how! As to his hopes and expectations, he cannot be disappointed, for Christ is sure to be glorified in his body by its life and by its death!
.
Hence, in Paul’s soul, that sublime indifference, which is the climax of the Christian life; it is, of course, a totally different thing from that fatal apathy, to which the false Mystics of the 17th century pretended to reduce the love of man’s heart. What tender affection has not this convert of Damascus for his brethren, once he has reached this point of perfection! God, says he, is my witness, how I long after you all, in the bowels of Jesus Christ! The one ambition which rules and absorbs him is that God, Who has begun in them the work, which is good by excellence—the work of Christian perfection (such as we know had been wrought in the Apostle himself) may be continued and perfected in them all, by the day when Christ is to appear in His glory. This is what he prays for—that the wedding garment of those whom he has betrothed to the one Spouse, in other words, that charity may beautify them with all its splendor for the grand Day of the eternal nuptials.
.
Now, what is the sure means whereby charity is to be perfected in them? It must abound, more and more, in knowledge and in all understanding of salvation, that is, in Faith. It is Faith that constitutes the basis of all supernatural virtue. A restricted, a diminished, Faith could never support a large and high-minded charity. Those men, therefore, are deceiving themselves, whose love for revealed truth does not keep pace with their charity! Such Christianity as that believes as little as it may; it has a nervous dread of new definitions; and out of respect for error, it cleverly and continually narrows the supernatural horizon. Charity, they say, is the queen of virtues; it makes them take everything easily, even lies against Truth; to give the same rights to error as to Truth is, in their estimation, the highest point of Christian civilization grounded on love! They quite forget that the first object of charity being God, who is substantial Truth, he has no greater enemy than a life; they cannot understand how it is that a Christian does not do a work of love by putting on the same footing the Object beloved and His mortal enemy!
.
The Apostles had very different ideas: in order to make charity grow in the world, they gave it a rich sowing of truth. Every new ray of Light they put into their disciples’ hearts was an intensifying of their love; and these disciples, having by Baptism become themselves light, they were most determined to have nothing to do with darkness. In those days, to deny the truth was the greatest of crimes; to expose themselves, by a want of vigilance, to infringe on the rights of truth, even in the slightest degree, was the height of imprudence. When Christianity first shone upon mankind, it found error supreme mistress of the world; having, then, to deal with a universe that was rooted in death, Christianity adopted no other plan for giving it salvation than that of making the Light as bright as it could be; its only policy was to proclaim the power which truth alone has for saving man, and to assert its exclusive right to reign over this world. The triumph of the Gospel was the result; it came after three centuries of struggle; a struggle, intense and violent, on the side of darkness which declared itself to be the supreme and was resolved to keep so; but a struggle most patient and glorious on the side of the Christians, the torrents of whose blood did but add fresh joy to the brave army, for it became the strongest possible foundation of the united Kingdom of Love and Truth.
.
But now, with the connivance of those whose Baptism made them too be Children of Light—error has regained its pretended Rights; as a natural consequence, the charity of an immense number has grown cold in proportion; darkness is again thickening over the world, as though it were in the chill of its last agony. The children of light, who would live up to their dignity, must behave exactly as did the early Christians. They must not fear, nor be troubled; but, like their forefathers and the Apostles, they must be proud to suffer for Jesus’ sake, and prize the word of life as quite the dearest thing they possess; for they are convinced that, so long as truth is kept up in the world, so long is there hope for it. As their only care is to make their manner of life worthy of the Gospel of Christ, they go on, with all the simplicity of children of God, faithfully fulfilling the duties of their state of life, in the midst of a wicked and perverse generation, as stars of the firmament do in the night. “The stars shine in the night,” says St. John Chrysostom, “they glitter in the dark; so far from growing dim amidst the gloom that surrounds them, they seem all the more brilliant. So will it be with thee, if thou art virtuous amidst the wicked; thy light will shine so much the clearer.” “As the stars,” says St. Augustine, “keep on their course in the track marked out for them by God, and grow not tired of sending forth their light in the midst of darkness, neither heed they the calamities which may be happening on earth—so should do those holy ones whose conversation is truly in heaven; they should pay no more notice as to what is said or done against them than the stars do.”
The Gradual hymns the praise of the sweet and strong unity, maintained in the Church, even to the end; she has done this by the charity in which the Epistle urged us to be making fresh progress, and which the ancient Gospel of this same Sunday put before us as the one means for funding a favorable sentence passed on us at the Day of Judgment.
.
Gradual
.
Ecce quam bonum, et quam jocumdum habitare fratres in unum!
.
Behold! how good and how pleasant it is, for Brethren to dwell together in unity!
.
℣. Sicut unguentum in capite quod descendit in barbam, barban Aaron.
.
℣. It is like the precious ointment on the head, that ran down upon the beard, (yea, the whole) beard, of Aaron.
.
Alleluia, alleluia.
.
Alleluia, alleluia.
.
℣. Qui timent Dominum, sperent in eo; adjutor et protector eorum est. Alleluia.
.
℣. They that fear the Lord, hope in Him; He is their Helper and their Protector. Alleluia.
.
Gospel
.
Sequentia sancti Evangelii secundum Matthæum.
.
Sequel of the holy Gospel according to St. Matthew.
.
Cap.xxii. Ch. xxii.
.
In illo tempore: Abeuntes Pharisæi, consilium inierunt, ut caperent eum in sermone. Et mittunt ei discipulos suos cum Herodianis, dicentes: Magister, scimus quia verax es, et viam Dei in veritate doces, et non est tibi cura de aliquo: non enim respicis personam hominum: dic ergo nobis quid tibi videtur, licet censum dare Cæsari, an non? Cognita autem Jesus nequitia eorum, ait: Quid me tentatis hypocritæ? Ostendite mihi numisma census. At illi obtulerunt ei denarium. Et ait illis Jesus: Cujus est imago hæc, et superscriptio? Dicunt ei: Cæsaris. Tunc ait illis: Reddite ergo quæ sunt Cæsaris, Cæsari: et quæ sunt Dei, Deo.
.
At that time: The Pharisees going, consulted among themselves how to insnare Him in His speech. And they sent to Him their disciples with the Herodians, saying: Master, we know that Thou art a true speaker, and teachest the way of God in truth, neither carest Thou for any man: for Thou dost not regard the person of men. Tell us therefore what dost Thou think, is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar, or not? But Jesus knowing their wickedness, said: Why do you tempt me, ye hypocrites? Shew me the coin of the tribute. And they offered him a penny. And Jesus saith to them: Whose image and inscription is this? They say to him: Caesar’ s. Then he saith to them: Render therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s; and to God, the things that are God’s.
.
The getting truths to be diminished is, evidently, to be a leading peril of the latter times, for during these weeks which represent the last days of the world, the Church is continually urging us to a sound and solid understanding of truth, as though she considered that to be the great preservative for her children. Last Sunday, she gave them, as defensive armor, the shield of faith and, as an offensive weapon, the word of God. On the previous Sunday, it was circumspection of mind and intelligence that she recommended to them, with a view to their preserving, during the approaching evil days, the holiness which is founded on truth, for as she told them the previous week, their riches in all knowledge are of paramount necessity. Today, in the Epistle, she implored of them to be ever progressing in knowledge and all understanding, as being the essential means for abounding in charity, and for having the work of their sanctification perfected for the day of Christ Jesus. The Gospel comes with an appropriate finish to these instructions given us by the Apostle: it relates an event in our Lord’s life which stamps those counsels with the weightiest possible authority—the authority of the example of Him Who is our divine Model. He gives His disciples the example they should follow when, like Himself, they have snares laid by the world for their destruction.
.
It was the last day of Jesus’ public teaching; it was almost the eve of His departure from this earth. His enemies had failed in every attempt hitherto made to ensnare Him; this last plot was to be unusually deep laid. The Pharisees, who refused to recognize Cæsar’s authority, and denied his claim to tribute, joined issue with their adversaries, the partisans of Herod and Rome, to propose this insidious question to Jesus: Is it lawful to give tribute to Cæsar, or not? If our Lord’s answer was negative, he incurred the displeasure of the government; if He took the affirmative side, he would lose the estimation of the people. With His divine prudence, He disconcerted their plans. The two parties, so strangely made friends by partnership in one common intrigue, heard the magnificent answer, which was divine enough to make even Pharisees and Herodians one in the Truth; but Truth was not what they were in search of, so they both skulked back again into their old party squabbles. The league formed against our Jesus was broken; the effort made by error recoiled on its own self, as must ever be the case; and the answer it had elicited passed from the lips of our Incarnate Lord to those of His Bride, the Church, who would be ever repeating it to this world of ours, for it contains the first principle of all governments on earth.
.
Render to Cæsar the things that are Cæsar’s, and to God the things that are God’s; it was the dictum most dear to the Apostles. If they boldly asserted that we must obey God rather than men, they explained the whole truth, and added: Let every soul be subject to the higher powers: for there is no power but from God: and those that are, are ordained of God. Therefore, he that resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God; and they that resist, purchase to themselves damnation. Wherefore, be subject of necessity, not only for wrath, but also for conscience’s sake. For, therefore, also ye pay tribute; for they are the ministers of God serving unto this purpose.
.
The will of God!—there is the origin, there is the real greatness of all authority amongst men! Of himself, man has no right to command his fellow man. The number, however imposing it may be, makes no difference with this powerlessness of men over my conscience; for whether they be one, or five hundred, I, by nature, am equal to each one among them; and by adding the number of their so-called rights over me, they are only adding to the number of nothingness. But God, wishing that men should live one with the other, has thereby wished that there exist amongst them a power which should rule over the rest; that is, should direct the thousands or millions of different wills to the unity of one social end. God leaves to circumstances, though it is His providence that regulates those circumstances—He leaves to men themselves, at the beginning of any mere human society, a great latitude as to the choice of the form under which is to be exercised both the civil power itself and the mode of its transmission. But once regularly invested with the power, its depositories, its possessors, are responsible to God alone, as far, that is, as the legitimate exercise of their authority goes, because it is from God alone that that power comes to them. It does not come to them from their people, who, not having that power themselves, cannot give it to another. So long as those rulers comply with the compact, or do not turn to the ruin of their people the power they received for its well-being—so long their right to the obedience of their subjects is the right of God Himself—whether they exercise their authority in exacting the subsidies needed for government; or in passing laws which, for the general good of the people, restrain the liberty otherwise theirs by natural right; or again, by bidding their soldiers defend their country at the risk of life. In all such cases, it is God Himself that commands and insists on being obeyed: in this world, He puts the sword into the hands of representatives that they may punish the disobedient; and in the next, He Himself will eternally punish them, unless they have made amends.
.
How great, then, is not the dignity of human Law! It makes the legislator a representative of God, and at the same time, spares the subject the humiliation of feeling himself debased before a fellow man! But in order that the law oblige, that is, be truly a law, it is evident that it must be, first and foremost, conformable to the commands and the prohibitions of that God Whose will alone can give it a sacred character, by making it enter into the domain of man’s conscience. It is for this reason that there cannot be a law against God or His Christ or His Church. When God is not with him who governs, the power he exercises is nothing better than brute force. The sovereign, or the parliament, that pretends to govern a country in opposition to the laws of God has no right to aught but revolt and contempt from every upright man; to give the sacred name of law to tyrannical enactments of that kind is a profanation, unworthy not only of Christian, but of every man who is not a slave.
The Offertory-Anthem, as also the Verses which used to be joined to it, refers, like the Introit, to the period of the last persecution. The words are taken from the prayer addressed to God by Esther, when about to enter into the presence of Assuerus, that she might plead with him against Aman, who is a figure of Antichrist. Esther is a type of the Church; and we could not better show the spirit in which we ought to sing our Offertory than by quoting the inspired words which preface this sublime prayer. Queen Esther, fearing the danger that was at hand, had recourse to the Lord. And when she had laid away her royal apparel, she put on garments suitable for weeping and mourning; instead of divers previous ointments, she covered her head with ashes and filth, and she humbled her body with fasts: and all the places, in which before she was accustomed to rejoice, she filled with her torn hair! And she prayed to the Lord the God of Israel, saying: O my Lord! Who alone art our King, help me a desolate woman, and who have no other helper but Thee!
.
Offertory
.
Recordare mei, Domine, omni potentatui dominans: et da sermonem rectum in os meum, ut placeant verba mea in conspectu principis.
.
Remember me, O Lord, Who art above all power; and put a right speech in my mouth, that my words may be pleasing to the prince.
.
℣. Recordare quod steterim in conspectu tuo.
.
℣. Remember, that I have stood in Thy sight.
.
℣. Everte cor ejus in odium repugnantium nobis, et in eos qui consentiunt eis; nos autem libera in manu tua, Deus noster in æternum.
.
℣. Turn his heart into hatred of them that oppose us, and of them that consent unto them; but, deliver us by Thy hand, O our God for ever!
.
℣. Qui regis Israel, intende; qui deducis velut ovem Joseph.
.
℣. O Thou that rulest Israel, give ear; Thou that leadest Joseph like a sheep.
.
Recordare mei, Domine.
.
Remember me, O Lord.
.
The surest guarantee a Christian can have against adversity is freedom from sin. It is sin that stirs up the anger of God and cries upon him for vengeance. Let us unite in the following prayer of the Church.
.
Secret
.
Da, misericors Deus: ut hæc salutaris oblatio, et a propriis nos reatibus indesinenter expediat, et ab omnibus tueatur adversis. Per Dominum.
.
Grant, O merciful God, that this sacrifice of salvation may, constantly, both free us from our sins, and protect us from all adversity. Through, etc.
.
The other Secrets, as in the Fourth Sunday After Pentecost.
.
The Communion-Anthem shows us with what perseverance and earnestness the Church prays to her divine Lord. We must imitate her.
.
While offering the sacred mysteries in memory of our Jesus, as He commanded us to do, we must not forget that these same are also our refuge in all our miseries. It would be presumption, or folly, to neglect to pray, that they may thus protect us. The Church, here again, is our model in utilizing these most powerful of all means for help.
.
Communion
.
Ego clamavi quoniam exaudisti me, Deus: inclina aurem tuam, et exaudi verba mea.
.
I have cried out, because Thou heardest me, O God: bend down Thine ear, and graciously hearken to my words.
.
Postcommunion
.
Sumpsimus, Domine, sacri dons mysterii, humiliter deprecantes: ut quæ in tui commemorationem nos facere præcepisti, in nostræ proficiant infirmitatis auxilium. Qui vivis.
.
Having received, O Lord, the sacred mysteries, we humbly beseech Thee, that what Thou hast commanded us to do in remembrance of Thee, may be a help to us in our weakness. Who livest, etc.
.
The other Postcommunions, as in the Fourth Sunday After Pentecost.

text:
In January 2022, during the unrest in Kazakhstan, senior military and security officials were accused of abandoning their responsibilities, while Russian-led troops entered the country. Some commanders reportedly fled or deserted their posts.

Ukraine's experience offers a striking contrast.

🇺🇦 "Take me back to the front line. Return me to my brigade immediately. I'm not going anywhere. I'm staying with Ukraine."

According to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, this was General Pavlo Palisa's reaction when the possibility of becoming Ukraine's ambassador to the United States was discussed.

And it wasn't the first time he had chosen military service over opportunities in America.

In February 2022, Palisa was studying at the prestigious U.S. Army Command and General Staff College. When Russia launched its full-scale invasion, he interrupted his education and returned home to defend Ukraine.

He helped establish the 5th Separate Assault Regiment, fought in the brutal battles around Bakhmut, and later commanded the legendary 93rd Mechanized Brigade, "Kholodnyi Yar."

Known by his callsign "Hunter," Palisa received the Cross of Military Merit and the Order of Bohdan Khmelnytsky for his service.

In November 2024, he was appointed Deputy Head of Ukraine's Presidential Office. His military education in the United States, fluent English, and familiarity with American officials made him a potential candidate for the strategically important ambassadorial position in Washington.

But Palisa had a different priority.

When the possibility of a diplomatic appointment was discussed, he explained that leaving military service during wartime would contradict his moral principles and personal convictions.

In 2022, he left America to defend his homeland. Years later, after surviving some of the war's fiercest battles, receiving military decorations, and reaching a senior government position, he reportedly asked to return to his combat brigade rather than pursue a diplomatic career.

For General Pavlo Palisa, defending Ukraine is not a political slogan. His military record demonstrates a commitment that has shaped his decisions throughout the war.

Some people seek prestigious positions far from the battlefield. Others ask to return to their soldiers.

Pavlo Palisa's story is about that choice. 🇺🇦

text:
The third "Russia-Africa" Summit is taking place in Moscow on October 28-29, 2026.

The main political outcome of the summit is that Moscow maintains extensive contacts with Africa despite the harm its policies inflict on Africans. According to the organizers, 48 countries confirmed their participation, with 22 of them represented by heads of state. At the previous summit in 2023, there were 17 such leaders, and at the first one in 2019, there were 43. This is a partial recovery in the level of participation, which the Kremlin can present as evidence of international recognition. A telling example is Kenya: last time it was represented by an ambassador, but now the delegation is led by President Ruto, although the issue of recruiting Kenyans into the Russian army remains acute.

A permanent cooperation framework consolidates Russian influence but does not guarantee that African partners will see promises fulfilled. On the sidelines of the summit, Lavrov and the Chairperson of the African Union Commission signed a plan for 2027-2029 covering 19 areas - from security to energy and education. This creates channels of work between summits and expands Moscow's access to African institutions. At the same time, the Russian Foreign Ministry admitted as early as June that previous meetings had produced more declarations than practical agreements.

Russian military support helps certain regimes stay in power and increases their dependence on Moscow. According to an FDD assessment, the geography of Russian military presence has expanded since 2023 to at least nine countries. Niger illustrates how such presence turns into political leverage. At the end of August, during a mutiny by part of the military, Russian forces helped the authorities suppress the uprising. According to the Russian ambassador, the Nigerien side itself requested the assistance.

Dependence on Russian support can persist even when it fails to provide reliable security and is accompanied by violence against the population. In the spring the Africa Corps was forced to leave Kidal in northern Mali. In October, Malian forces with Russian support retook the city, yet the episode demonstrated the limits of Moscow's capabilities. Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung expert Ulf Laessing explains the preservation of the partnership by the lack of viable alternatives for the Malian authorities. Meanwhile, in October, Human Rights Watch documented new instances of torture against civilians involving Russian mercenaries from the Africa Corps.

Russia is increasing its revenues from food supplies to Africa even as its own actions contribute to food insecurity. In the first nine months of 2026 Moscow delivered more than $3.7 billion worth of agricultural products to Africa - 9% more than a year earlier. The largest increase in monetary terms came from Kenya, which is simultaneously pressing for a resolution of the problem of its citizens in the Russian army. Food supplies have value for buyers, but they must be assessed alongside the consequences of Russia's war against Ukraine. After Russia's withdrawal from the Black Sea Grain Initiative in 2023, the UN Secretary-General warned of the impact on vulnerable countries and of rising prices.

Nuclear energy risks turning the need for electricity into long-term dependence on Russia. Rosatom presented floating nuclear power plants and reported advanced negotiations with Egypt, Togo, Namibia and Tanzania. The proposed model involves the purchase of electricity while retaining Russian involvement in maintenance and fuel supply. The plants can operate for up to 60 years, making the link with the supplier long-lasting and difficult to replace. There are still no publicly confirmed contracts for these projects, agreed financing or schedules. The largest project already under way is the construction of the El Dabaa nuclear power plant in Egypt.
Opaque links between Russian payment networks create financial and sanctions risks for African partners. Putin called for expanding ties between banks, opening branches and using Russia's SPFS alongside the pan-African payment system. In this way Moscow seeks to connect its own instruments with African infrastructure.

A separate track is the A7 cryptocurrency network: in April the Financial Times wrote of limited evidence of its practical progress on the continent, but in October the Centre for Information Resilience identified numerous technical links with international payment platforms, including the Togo-linked Amani AI. Participants in the A7 network are under British sanctions.

Russian expansion in the gold-mining sector can weaken state control over national resources and channel revenues towards Russian military objectives. This mechanism is already visible in the Central African Republic: according to the US Treasury, the Wagner-linked company Midas, together with mercenaries, obstructed state inspections of the Ndassima mine, while revenues of related companies supported military operations. Against this background, new projects require particular attention. In Mali a gold-processing plant is under construction: 62% of the joint company belongs to the state, 38% to the Russian firm Yadran. Processing of raw materials from other Sahel countries is being considered, which could turn the plant into a regional hub. In Niger, Rosgeologia has so far reported only readiness to sign agreements on hydrocarbon and gold exploration. For Moscow, gold is valuable both as income and as an asset for operations outside ordinary Western banking channels.

Russia's media presence combines open agreements with covert operations that mislead African audiences. Ahead of the summit, TASS signed agreements with media partners in Burundi, Guinea, Cameroon, Mali, Niger, the Seychelles and Tanzania on news exchange, training and reciprocal visits. The network covers both close security partners of Moscow and states with other forms of cooperation. According to RT, TASS also provides its news feeds free of charge to more than 300 African media outlets. This work began long before the current summit and ensures continuous access to newsrooms. In parallel, Graphika and Code for Africa identified a network of likely fabricated journalists and experts promoting Russian interests; researchers have a high level of confidence regarding 38 such individuals.

The recruitment of Africans for the war is a direct human cost that is not offset by trade or diplomatic benefits. In August the Ukrainian Foreign Ministry reported at least 2 982 recruits from 37 African countries and around 486 known deaths. These are incomplete figures from the Ukrainian side, but independent research confirms the mechanism of abuse. Amnesty International has documented deception, coercion and the exploitation of economic hardship that in many cases amount to human trafficking. In Kenya, families are publicly demanding answers and the return of their relatives.

Russian military presence draws African states into Moscow's broader struggle for strategic positions. Russia has long sought a permanent naval presence on the continent, but this remains an unrealized ambition. The project in Port Sudan has been delayed for years. As late as the end of 2025 the Russian ambassador explained the pause by the war; Sudan Tribune, citing its own sources at the time, reported that al-Burhan had assured the Saudi side that plans for a Red Sea base had been frozen. At the same time Russia is expanding access to Libyan airfields, including Maaten al-Sarra near the borders with Chad and Sudan, supporting its operations in the Sahel. The infrastructure already exists, although guaranteed long-term access and a permanent naval base remain unresolved. The harm from previous operations in Libya is concrete: Human Rights Watch established Wagner's involvement in the mining of areas near Tripoli in 2020.

The gap between the Russian offer and the development needs of African countries risks perpetuating their economic vulnerability. The co-chair of the summit, President of Burundi Évariste Ndayishimiye, called on Russian companies to invest in local processing, jobs and skills transfer. For African governments it is important to retain a larger share of the revenues from their own resources. This is precisely where the Russian offer falls short: trade (with a surplus in Russia's favor) is more developed than large-scale productive investment.
Without the development of local production and skills, countries can remain suppliers of raw materials and buyers of finished goods. This suits Moscow but does not help its partners in Africa.

The principal danger of the Russian model is the transformation of vital needs of African societies into dependence, a significant share of whose costs is borne by the African population itself. Moscow entrenches itself through military support, food supplies and, in prospect, electricity. In the three years between summits it has expanded its presence and strengthened ties with a number of African states, gaining influence without large-scale investment in development. The social cost of this model of cooperation can already be assessed: violence against civilians, recruitment by deception, covert information operations and the restriction of state control over resources have all been documented.

African nationals captured fighting for Russia in Ukraine are appealing to participants at the Russia-Africa Summit, scheduled to take place in Moscow on October 28-29, to help secure their release.

"We have been in captivity for quite a long time, and it feels as though we've been forgotten. I hope our governments will represent us at the summit and help secure a prisoner exchange," says a citizen of Botswana.

According to the I Want to Live* project, people from 59 countries, including 18 in Africa, have been taken prisoner by Ukraine since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion.

During this time, Russia has not taken back a single African national through a prisoner exchange.

*I Want to Live is a Ukrainian project of the Coordination Headquarters on the Treatment of Prisoners of War, established with the support of the Ministry of Defense of Ukraine and Defense Intelligence of Ukraine. It is intended for servicemen of the Russian armed forces willing to voluntarily surrender into captivity.

1. A Royal Prophecy Spoken from a Deathbed

Jacob begins the gathering with an announcement that ought to control every interpretation that follows: “Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the last days” (Genesis 49:1). He is not offering parental advice for the coming month, settling an inheritance dispute, or distributing sentimental compliments before dying. He is prophesying. His sons stand physically before him, but the tribes descending from them stand prophetically before him. Genesis 49:28 confirms this by saying, “All these are the twelve tribes of Israel.” God allows Jacob to see beyond individual personalities into tribal histories, territorial conditions, royal developments, military conflicts, disciplinary judgments, and Messianic fulfillment. The old man’s natural eyes are nearly finished, but his prophetic sight extends farther than the vision of every king who will later sit in Jerusalem. Death is approaching his bed, yet history is opening before his words. That is how God enjoys humiliating human pride: He can show a dying shepherd more about the future than the combined experts of an empire know about tomorrow.

The timing makes Judah’s prophecy especially remarkable. Israel has no land, no capital, no palace, no army, no priesthood established under Moses, and no visible political existence apart from dwelling in Egypt. Judah possesses neither crown nor throne, yet Jacob sees a sceptre. David will not be born for centuries, yet Jacob announces the tribe from which the ruler will arise. Moses has not yet stood before Pharaoh, the Passover lamb has not yet been slain, the Red Sea has not yet opened, Sinai has not yet thundered, and Joshua has not yet crossed Jordan. Nevertheless, the royal promise is already fixed. God does not wait for circumstances to develop before deciding what He intends to do. He declares the end while men are still arguing about the beginning. Egypt may view Jacob’s family as dependent strangers living because Joseph secured their survival, but God sees a nation, tribes, a kingdom, and the coming King.

The phrase “in the last days” must not be jammed into a single prophetic afternoon. From Jacob’s viewpoint, the developing tribal history of Israel lay ahead. Some statements in Genesis 49 appear during the conquest and settlement of Canaan; others emerge under the judges; others mature during the monarchy; and Judah’s oracle reaches directly toward the Messiah and His kingdom. Prophecy often presents distant events like mountain peaks visible from one location while the valleys between them remain undescribed. Jacob can therefore speak of Judah’s tribal ascendancy, Davidic kingship, Shiloh’s coming, and the gathering of the people within one oracle without explaining every century separating them. The correct response is not to flatten the whole prophecy into David, nor to postpone every word until the Tribulation. The Bible reader must permit each part to reach as far as later Scripture carries it. Judah’s lion appears in tribal history, but Revelation identifies the ultimate Lion. The sceptre appears in David’s house, but Christ possesses the everlasting right to rule.

2. Judah the Man and Judah the Tribe

Judah did not begin his recorded history as a spotless candidate for royal dignity. Genesis does not airbrush the patriarchs, and God did not select Judah because a committee found no embarrassing material in his file. Judah participated in selling Joseph, deceived his father with the bloodied coat, and later became entangled in the shameful events recorded in Genesis 38. The Bible reports those matters because grace is not impressed by public relations. God does not require us to manufacture a sinless Judah in order to explain Judah’s royal future. From this article"Upon learning the news of a railway accident that occurred in Spain killing 68 people and injuring numerous others, Pope Leo XIV expresses his "deep sorrow" and offers prayers for the eternal repose of the deceased.
By Deborah Castellano Lubov

Pope Leo XIV has expressed his “deep sorrow” over the tragic railway accident that occurred in central Spain on Wednesday.

He sent a telegram of condolences signed by Cardinal Secretary of State Pietro Parolin and addressed Archbishop Francisco Cerro Chaves of Toledo.

On Wednesday, at approximately 8:54 AM local time, two high-speed trains collided in the town of Urda, Toledo.

The death toll stood at 68 but remained provisional, according to Castilla-La Mancha regional government spokesperson Esther Padilla, who added on Thursday that 53 people remained hospitalized, 15 of whom are in critical condition at various hospitals.

Search teams with sniffer dogs continued looking for victims on Thursday morning.

The Holy Father assured all those affected of his prayers for the eternal repose of the deceased and extended his heartfelt condolences to the families of those who have died, together with expressions of comfort and deep concern, and his wishes for the speedy recovery of the injured.

He likewise encouraged members of the rescue teams to persevere in their efforts to provide relief and assistance, and imparted his Apostolic Blessing.

Spain’s government declared three days of mourning. This marks Spain’s second high-speed rail disaster this year."

SpaceX uses stainless steel to build its Starship rocket.

Most rockets use expensive materials like carbon fiber or specialized aluminum alloys because they are lightweight.

But stainless steel offers several major advantages:

Much cheaper raw materials
Easier to weld, reducing manufacturing costs
Under the right conditions, strength-to-weight performance comparable to lightweight materials

By choosing affordable stainless steel, SpaceX is aiming to dramatically reduce rocket manufacturing costs. https://t.co/Uh1YPM86Li

text:
SIGNAL INTELLIGENCE BRIEF
Published: October 29, 2026 | 11:12 AM ET

Thesis:
Oil is up 8.32% in four weeks, yet bond yields, inflation expectations and credit all tell a calmer story, while the biggest technology names slide and the average stock carries the index.

WHAT MATTERS
Two gauges decide how much to trust this calm. The first is the MOVE index, which measures how much traders expect Treasury yields to swing, the way the VIX does for stocks. It is 92.59, down 15.54 points over four weeks and back under the 100 line, so rates traders are calmer than a month ago. The second is the high-yield credit spread, the extra yield that weaker companies pay over the government. It is 314bps (-10bps 4wk), which says lenders are relaxed about default risk. Prices only partly agree. The S&P 500 is up 0.76% over four weeks but down 0.46% today, and 3/6 baskets in our cross-asset check are down more than 1% today. Calm gauges and a shaky day is the combination to remember. Credit is still above its 12-month average of 288bps, so relaxed is relative.

WHAT IS HIDDEN
The 10-year at 4.98% is lower because the real return investors demand has dropped, and the flat breakeven says they are not treating the oil jump as lasting inflation.
Bond volatility is the second piece. MOVE is 5.5 times the VIX, down from about 6.6 four weeks ago, and realised stock volatility is only 10.1%. When bond volatility falls that fast, the rates market is absorbing news without panic. A reading back above 100 would show that calm is ending, and the usual next stop is credit, then funding markets.

Liquidity offers a smaller offset. The Treasury's cash balance was $1052.5bn on October 27, +115.9bn over four weeks. When the government builds that account, cash leaves the banking system, which tightens funding at the margin. The reverse repo facility, where money funds park spare cash, holds only $0.2bn, so that cushion is essentially empty, and the overnight funding rate (SOFR) is 3.94%. Nothing in today's data shows funding strain, but there is little spare buffer if it appears. The supply side of the bond market is a blind spot this morning: no new 10-year or 30-year auction since October 8, no new dealer inventory data since October 14, no new Treasury-bill share since September 30, no new foreign central bank custody figure since October 21 and no new foreign holder data since August 2026.

WHAT IS MISPRICED
Breadth. The cap-weighted S&P 500 is up 0.76% over four weeks while the equal-weight version is up 5.21% and the Russell 2000 is up 2.03%, so the average stock is 4.45 points ahead of the index. The index is held back by its largest companies: technology is down 4.47%, Communication Services -7.98% and the Nasdaq 100 3.51%. Leadership is defensive. Health Care +10.12% and utilities (+9.4%) lead, and energy (+9.98%) is the cyclical exception tied to oil, while defensive sectors as a group are up 9.6% against 4.8% for cyclicals. A headline that looks flat hides a rotation away from the market's biggest names. Gold sits on the list from the other side. Real yields fell 27bps and gold is still 3.64% lower over four weeks, so a metal that should be benefiting from cheaper real money is not doing the job.

WHAT MARKETS DISAGREE ON
Here is the witness map. Oil says inflation: Brent is up 8.32% and energy stocks are leading. Bonds say something else: real yields are lower, breakevens flat and MOVE under 100. Credit says calm, with spreads at 314bps and tighter. Gold says there is no safety bid, because it is falling. Stocks split, with the index up and technology down. No single story fits all of that cleanly. Of the stories we test, a growth scare with money moving toward safety fits best, while renewed inflation pricing and a yen carry unwind fit worst. Even the best fit is contradicted by gold falling, credit tightening and the index rising, so our regime label of stagflation and the bond and equity evidence do not line up today. The evidence favours the bond side over the oil side for now, because breakevens and term premium are the markets that price inflation directly and neither is rising.
A second disagreement runs between households and traders. The University of Michigan October survey has households expecting 4.7% inflation over the coming year and 3.5% over five to ten years, while the market breakeven is 2.38%. Traders believe prices are contained and the people buying groceries do not. If households are right, the Fed has less room to ease, and that would push real yields back up.

WHAT TO WATCH NEXT
The stress signal is MOVE climbing back through 100 from 92.59 while high-yield spreads widen from 314bps. A widening of 50bps over four weeks would put credit in warning territory, and the next place to look would be funding markets. The relief signal is technology and communication services recovering toward the equal-weight index while fund flows turn positive, which would show the narrow drag is fading. The live event risk is Iran. Reporting dated October 29 has US and Israeli officials preparing for possible renewed military action after the November 3 midterms, and Brent at $109.73 would move first. On the carry side, USD/JPY falling while Japan's 10-year yield rises would be the first sign of a yen unwind.
