The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, Nov. 10 at 4pm ET. The Colts and Titans already started selling this week, and more moves are coming.

Here's every rumor that matters for fantasy: the situation, the fantasy impact, and what to do now 👇

Jonathan Taylor
The situation: Indy wants a 2nd-round pick plus more, and the owner doesn't want to trade him
Fantasy impact: 78% of the Colts' RB carries. He's a workhorse wherever he plays. Seth McGowan has most of the rest
What to do: I’m buying JT right now. Either he continues to be the focal point of the Colts offense, or he goes to a winning team where he’ll see more red zone touches. Regardless, McGowan should be stashed in all leagues till it’s definitive. He would be colts RB1 if JT gets moved.

Saquon Barkley
The situation: His name is out there, but ESPN's Fowler says Pollard is the more likely RB to move. Philly is 2-5 with five straight losses
Fantasy impact: Left Week 7 with a back injury after 10 snaps. Philly's backfield has been a split all year due to Saquon’s struggle to stay healthy: Saquon 32% of the carries, Dameon Pierce 28%
What to do: Hold. His value is at the bottom, and a move to a contender is upside you shouldn't sell for pennies. His value can only go up from here.

Tony Pollard
The situation: Only a 15% chance per ESPN, but he's the fallback if Indy keeps Taylor
Fantasy impact: 79% of Tennessee's RB carries. A new team likely means a committee for the remaining Tennessee backs. Tyjae Spears is next up in Tennessee
What to do: Sell the 3-TD game. Stash Spears in deep leagues.

Josh Downs
The situation: Requested a trade. The Steelers are interested and the Chiefs are shopping for a WR
Fantasy impact: Leads the Colts with a 20% target share but has no TDs and 8.2 PPG. If he goes, Keenan Allen (19%) and Tyler Warren once he's healthy get the extra targets
What to do: Buy Downs cheap before he moves. Grab Keenan Allen in deep leagues

Brian Thomas Jr.
The situation: League execs think Jacksonville is moving on. 45% chance to be traded per ESPN
Fantasy impact: Just 11% of the targets and 4.2 PPG. Parker Washington owns 27% and stays the WR1 either way
What to do: Free stash in deep leagues. A new team can only help. Chiefs could potentially bring him back to his rookie season production.

Jerry Jeudy
The situation: Cleveland would only move him for a "substantial" offer
Fantasy impact: 16 catches, 11% of the targets. KC Concepcion (22%) and Denzel Boston (20%) already lead the room
What to do: Don't chase Jeudy. If he goes, Concepcion and Boston get the bump

Kirk Cousins
The situation: 16 TDs to 5 INTs and still on the block, with rookie Fernando Mendoza waiting
Fantasy impact: Brock Bowers (20% target share) and Tre Tucker (19%) would be catching passes from a rookie
What to do: Don't sell Bowers. Keep riding Tucker, but know the risk

Chiefs
The situation: Expected to add a "serviceable" WR, per Rapoport
Fantasy impact: Xavier Worthy and Travis Kelce each have 20% of the targets. A new WR eats into Worthy first
What to do: Sell Worthy now if anyone is buying

Chris Godwin
The situation: 15% chance per ESPN. His $22M in cash this year makes a deal tough
Fantasy impact: Hasn't topped 50 yards in a game this season. 7.6 PPG
What to do: Don't chase it. A trade won't fix that

Calvin Ridley
The situation: CBS says he's "completely fallen out of favor" in Tennessee
Fantasy impact: 5 catches on 10 targets. 5% of the targets
What to do: Change-of-scenery stash in deep leagues only

Jauan Jennings
The situation: ESPN has him as the most likely skill player to move (50%). Rams, Falcons and 49ers make sense
Fantasy impact: 4 catches on 8 targets. Nothing changes in Minnesota
What to do: Only matters if he lands as a starter. Watch the landing spot

text:
Before Hollywood, I was living in a van in Hawaii and waiting tables at Bubba Gump Shrimp Company. One day, the incredible Rae Dawn Chong walked into the restaurant, and naturally, I went up to her table and said, “Hey, you’re a movie star! What are you doing here?”

She asked if I could act, and I said, “Fuck yeah, put me in your movie!”

She asked for my phone number. The only problem was I didn’t have one. So I gave her my buddy Mike’s number instead. A couple days later, Mike casually mentions, “Oh, by the way, someone called you.” ARE YOU KIDDING ME, MIKE?!

I called her back, and sure enough, she was serious. I drove over to pick up the script, went back to Mike’s house, and read all 120 pages three times in a row. First script I’d ever read. My character's name was Devon, and I remember thinking, “Sweet! I could totally play a Devon!”

I showed up to the audition with every line and inflection mapped out in pencil. Rae told me I could act and offered me the part. I asked if we were shooting in Hawaii. Nope. Los Angeles.

I had about $60 to my name, a bag of clothes, and some rollerblades.

Then Rae told me they'd fly me out. And I remember thinking right then and there, my life just changed forever. I'm going to be an actor.

That little movie was Cursed Part 3, a low-budget horror comedy that opened the door to Hollywood for me.

I'll forever be grateful to Rae for taking a chance on a kid working at a shrimp restaurant. Everybody starts somewhere, and this is where it all began for me.

text:
SK Hynix $SKHY   reported quarterly revenue of 104.6 trillion won and operating profit of 83.3 trillion won, with an operating margin approaching 80%. Yet net income plunged 58%.

Despite the sharp decline in net income, the company’s U.S.-listed shares surged 13.3% on Oct. 28, while its South Korean shares rose 10.89%. The rally extended across the semiconductor sector, lifting Samsung Electronics 9.01%, Micron Technology 5.86% and SanDisk 7.66%.

The market’s reaction reflected confidence in SK Hynix’s underlying operating performance rather than its headline net income. Strong shipment guidance, rising memory prices and progress in high-bandwidth memory (HBM) reinforced the company’s position in the AI supply chain.

But the results also raise broader questions. 

How sustainable are its extraordinary margins? 
Can long-term supply agreements reduce the risks of the memory cycle? 
And as AI workloads evolve, could NAND flash become a more important part of the industry’s growth story?

1. Strong Demand Drives the Rally

Before the earnings release, investors had grown increasingly concerned about the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending. Questions about the returns on massive investments in data centers and computing capacity had begun to weigh on the semiconductor sector.

SK Hynix’s latest outlook offered a more encouraging picture.

The company expects fourth-quarter DRAM shipments to rise roughly 20% to 25% sequentially. That would indicate that the market’s strength is being driven not only by higher prices but also by growing shipment volumes—a healthier combination than price increases alone.

Production execution will be equally important. The ramp-up at the M15X facility and the transition to advanced 1c DRAM manufacturing appear to be progressing smoothly. Meanwhile, HBM4 has entered volume shipments, with yields reportedly ahead of expectations.

These developments matter because the memory industry’s profitability depends on more than demand. Manufacturers must also deliver sufficient output, improve yields and transition to new technologies without allowing production costs to erode margins.

SK Hynix’s position in HBM gives it exposure to the growing need for memory in AI accelerators, while its conventional DRAM and NAND businesses provide additional sources of revenue. Strength across these product categories could make the company less dependent on any single segment of the AI hardware market.

The company also announced a shareholder-return package worth roughly 100 trillion won, including more than 30 trillion won in dividends and over 60 trillion won in share repurchases and cancellations. 

It also ended its evaluation of a potential Solidigm IPO.

Together, these moves reinforce confidence in management’s expectations for future cash generation. The key question is whether strong demand and pricing can translate into sustained profitability as the industry invests to meet customers’ needs.

2. The 32.6 Trillion-Won Earnings Gap

Despite operating profit of 83.3 trillion won, SK Hynix reported net income of just 39.8 trillion won. The gap was largely attributed to two categories of non-operating losses.

The first was approximately 11.6 trillion won in foreign-exchange losses, reportedly associated with the Korean won’s appreciation. Currency movements can affect reported earnings when a company holds assets, liabilities or cash balances denominated in foreign currencies.

The second was around 22.9 trillion won in investment valuation losses as semiconductor-related equities declined. Together, the two items represented a substantial drag on the company’s bottom line.

The distinction between operating profit and net income is important. Operating profit provides a clearer view of the performance of the company’s core business, while net income also reflects financing costs, taxes and other items outside day-to-day operations.

Some investment valuation losses may be non-cash when recognized and could reverse if the underlying assets recover. 

However, that outcome is not guaranteed, and foreign-exchange movements can have real economic consequences depending on the company’s exposures and hedging arrangements.

The losses therefore should not simply be dismissed. Instead, they need to be assessed separately from the performance of the memory business.

If DRAM and NAND prices remain firm, shipment volumes increase and production yields improve, SK Hynix could continue generating strong operating profits even when non-operating items create volatility in net income.

For investors, the central issue is the durability of those profits. An operating margin approaching 80% is extraordinary, but the memory industry is cyclical. Whether such profitability can persist will depend on pricing power, manufacturing efficiency and the pace at which competitors add capacity.

3. Long-Term Contracts: Less Risk, Potentially Less Upside

SK Hynix is also seeking greater visibility into future demand through long-term supply agreements.

The company has reportedly signed five-year agreements with 14 core customers, including major cloud-service providers, securing commitments for more than 50% of its total capacity in 2027 and 2028. The agreements reportedly include deposits.

The strategic logic is straightforward. AI infrastructure requires substantial investment, but the pace of adoption and the commercial returns from AI applications remain uncertain. 

If customers slow their spending, memory manufacturers without firm commitments could face weaker sales and excess inventory.

Long-term agreements can reduce that uncertainty by giving manufacturers a clearer view of future demand. They may also help customers secure access to critical memory supplies in a market where advanced products can be difficult to obtain quickly.
The trade-off is pricing flexibility.

If memory prices rise sharply in 2027, SK Hynix’s ability to capture the full upside will depend on how contract prices are determined. Agreements that allow prices to adjust with market conditions may preserve some upside, while tighter pricing limits could leave the company earning less than it might in the spot market.

In effect, SK Hynix is trading some potential upside for greater demand visibility. That may be a sensible strategy in a capital-intensive industry where overestimating demand can have costly consequences.

More predictable orders could also make production planning and capacity investment easier. Rather than responding entirely to short-term price movements, the company can align part of its output with contracted customer requirements.

Still, long-term agreements cannot eliminate the memory cycle. Demand can change, technology can shift and new capacity can eventually put pressure on prices. The value of these contracts will depend not only on their volume but also on their pricing terms and flexibility.

4. Beyond HBM: NAND’s AI Opportunity

The AI memory opportunity is expanding beyond high-bandwidth memory.

DRAM shipments reportedly rose around 10% sequentially, while average selling prices increased more than 20%. NAND shipments edged lower, but average selling prices also rose by more than 20%.

The combination suggests that pricing strength is spreading across the broader memory market. For SK Hynix, this matters because conventional DRAM and NAND can contribute meaningfully to earnings alongside its HBM business.

A further opportunity may emerge from changes in AI system architecture.

AI agents and long-context models require increasingly large KV caches, which store information that models need to access during inference. As these workloads grow, keeping all relevant data in expensive, capacity-constrained HBM and DRAM becomes increasingly costly.

NAND-based storage could help address this problem. SSDs cannot replace HBM or DRAM, which offer different performance characteristics, but they could complement faster memory in a tiered architecture. 

 requiring immediate access would remain in high-speed memory, while other information could be stored on lower-cost media.

Such an approach could help AI infrastructure balance speed, capacity, and cost. If the amount of context processed by AI systems continues to expand, storage capacity may become an increasingly important part of the overall infrastructure equation.

SK Hynix is reportedly developing SALT-KV software and CMM Hybrid technology, while exploring High Bandwidth Flash (HBF) as a potential bridge between HBM and SSDs.

These technologies remain part of an evolving market, and their commercial impact will depend on performance, cost and customer adoption. Nevertheless, they illustrate why the long-term AI memory opportunity may extend beyond the fastest memory products.

The gains in SanDisk and Micron alongside SK Hynix reflect this broader market interest. Investors are increasingly looking at the entire memory supply chain rather than treating HBM as the only potential beneficiary of AI infrastructure spending.

5. The Risks Ahead

Despite the strong results, three questions will shape SK Hynix’s outlook.

First, can DRAM shipments meet guidance? Fourth-quarter growth of 20% to 25% would support the view that demand remains robust and that the M15X ramp-up and advanced 1c manufacturing are progressing as expected. A shortfall could reflect production constraints, customer timing or weaker demand.

Second, why is the profitability gap between HBM and conventional DRAM narrowing? If conventional DRAM margins are rising as prices strengthen, SK Hynix could benefit from a broader-based memory upcycle. If the narrowing instead reflects pressure on HBM profitability, investors would need to examine whether competition or customer pricing is affecting returns.

Third, will higher investment eventually trigger another supply glut? Management argues that capital spending does not immediately translate into additional output: factories can be built ahead of demand, while equipment installation and production ramps are staged over time.

Even so, the industry has repeatedly demonstrated how quickly favorable economics can encourage capacity expansion. If new supply arrives faster than demand grows, pricing power could weaken. Chinese manufacturers such as ChangXin Memory Technologies are another factor to monitor as their manufacturing capabilities develop.

If capacity expands just as AI spending slows, the market could face renewed pricing pressure by 2028. For now, supply-demand conditions remain favorable, but current margins should not be assumed to last indefinitely.

SK Hynix’s results highlight the strength of the current memory upcycle. Rising prices, growing AI demand and progress in HBM are supporting its operating performance, while the expansion of AI workloads could create opportunities across conventional DRAM and NAND.

Long-term supply agreements may provide greater visibility into future demand, although they also introduce trade-offs if market prices rise beyond contracted levels. Meanwhile, the risk of overcapacity remains a central concern for an industry accustomed to sharp swings in profitability.

The challenge is to capture the AI boom without investing too aggressively ahead of the next downturn. SK Hynix’s ability to maintain its technological edge, manage capacity, and secure sustainable demand will determine whether the current cycle develops into a more durable phase of growth—or another peak in the memory market.

ANNALS OF THE DAY 🪔

══════════════ ❧ ══════════════

A Historical Chronicle: October 29 Edition

────────────── ◈ ──────────────

EPIGRAPH

“We carry yesterday like a lantern—not to live in its light, but to see how far we’ve already come, and how much farther we need to go.” ~ Hodgepodgery, 2026

────────────── ◈ ──────────────

📑 TABLE OF CONTENTS

🪔 INTRO — Setting the Historical Stage

🧭 CALENDAR OVERVIEW — The Date at a Glance

🏛️ MAJOR HISTORICAL EVENTS — Turning Points That Shaped Our World

🔬 SCIENTIFIC, TECHNOLOGICAL, AND CULTURAL MILESTONES — Ideas and Innovations That Changed History

🎂 FAMOUS BIRTHDAYS — Celebrating Remarkable Lives

🥀 MEMORIAM — Remembering Those We Have Lost

🏟️ SPORTS HIGHLIGHTS — Triumphs, Records, and Legendary Moments

📝 HISTORY QUIZ OF THE DAY — Test Your Knowledge

⚖️ CLOSING — The Day's Historical Reckoning

🍬 CANDY — A Taste of Tomorrow

────────────── ◈ ──────────────

INTRO

History has a peculiar way of announcing its turning points: sometimes with the arrival of a king, sometimes with the declaration of a republic, and sometimes with a stock market discovering that confidence is not the same thing as security. October 29 gathers moments when empires changed hands, humanitarian principles took shape, technological revolutions began with decidedly unimpressive first attempts, and the machinery of modern life revealed both its promise and its capacity for catastrophe. From an ancient capital opening its gates to a message that stopped after two letters, this date reminds us that history's most consequential beginnings rarely arrive with guarantees about how the story will end.

────────────────────────────────

🧭 CALENDAR OVERVIEW

October 29 is the 302nd day of the year in the Gregorian calendar (≈82.74% of the year completed). There are 63 days remaining after this date, representing ≈17.26% of the year. The year 2026 is a common year of 365 days. Today is Thursday, falling in ISO week 44. Observances associated with this date include World Stroke Day, National Cat Day in the United States, and Republic Day in Turkey. In 2026, October 29 also coincides with Karva Chauth, a Hindu observance whose date varies according to the lunar calendar.

────────────────────────────────

🏛️ MAJOR HISTORICAL EVENTS

Across centuries of political evolution, humanitarian progress, financial upheaval, and global conflict, these monumental events reshaped nations and altered human destiny.

539 BCE — Cyrus the Great Enters Babylon 👑

On the third day of Arahsamnu, traditionally converted to October 29, 539 BCE, Cyrus the Great entered Babylon after Persian forces under Gobryas had taken the city without a major battle earlier in the month. The Nabonidus Chronicle distinguishes the entry of the Persian army from the subsequent arrival of Cyrus himself. The Persian king presented his rule as a restoration of order and established a new imperial administration over the former Babylonian Empire. His conquest became a defining moment in the rise of the Achaemenid Persian Empire, while biblical accounts associated Persian rule with the return of Judean exiles.

🧩 TRIVIA: The Nabonidus Chronicle records that Cyrus's arrival was accompanied by green branches being spread before him, a gesture associated in the text with the establishment of peace.

🌀 OBSCURE: The city had already been entered by Persian forces before Cyrus arrived. The distinction matters because the celebrated royal entrance was not necessarily the moment when Babylon's defenses first fell.

1618 — Sir Walter Raleigh Is Executed ⚔️

Sir Walter Raleigh, the English courtier, explorer, poet, and former favorite of Elizabeth I, was beheaded in Old Palace Yard, Westminster. His execution followed the revival of a treason sentence originally imposed in 1603. James I had authorized Raleigh's release for an expedition to Guiana, but the venture ended in disaster after clashes with Spanish forces. With Raleigh's political position irretrievably damaged, the king ordered the old sentence carried out. His death illustrated the precarious fate of a royal favorite who had survived imprisonment but failed to recover the confidence of the Crown.

🧩 TRIVIA: Raleigh had spent much of the period between his original conviction and execution imprisoned in the Tower of London.

1863 — Geneva Conference Establishes Red Cross Principles 📜

Delegates representing sixteen states and several humanitarian organizations met in Geneva to consider how wounded soldiers might receive assistance during wartime. The conference adopted resolutions supporting voluntary national relief societies, protections for medical personnel, and a distinctive red cross on a white background. These principles laid the groundwork for the First Geneva Convention of 1864 and helped establish the foundations of modern international humanitarian law.

🧩 TRIVIA: The organizing Committee of Five that initiated the conference developed into the International Committee of the Red Cross.

🏆 FIRST: The conference established an international framework for national voluntary relief societies and a common protective emblem, laying essential groundwork for the first Geneva Convention the following year.

1923 — The Republic of Turkey Is Proclaimed 🇹🇷

Turkey's Grand National Assembly formally declared the country a republic by amending the constitution. Mustafa Kemal, later known as Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, was elected the first president. The proclamation consolidated a political transformation already underway following the nationalist victory in the Turkish War of Independence and the abolition of the Ottoman sultanate. Ankara became the center of the new republican government, marking a decisive departure from the imperial order that had governed the region for centuries.

🧩 TRIVIA: The republic's founding president, Mustafa Kemal, later received the surname Atatürk, meaning “Father of the Turks,” through legislation adopted in 1934.

1929 — Black Tuesday Shakes Wall Street 📉

The New York Stock Exchange experienced another wave of panic selling as investors attempted to escape a collapsing market. A record 16,410,030 shares changed hands, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell approximately 12% in a single session. The crash followed severe losses on October 28 and came after years of speculative buying, extensive borrowing, and increasingly fragile confidence in stock prices. The market collapse did not single-handedly cause the Great Depression, but it accelerated the financial crisis and deepened the economic contraction that followed.

🧩 TRIVIA: The exchange's ticker machines fell hours behind as the unprecedented volume of transactions overwhelmed the equipment.

⚠️ IRONY: The speculative boom had encouraged investors to treat rising prices as evidence of prosperity, only for the scramble to sell to expose how little security those paper gains had provided.

1956 — Israel Invades Sinai; the Suez Crisis Escalates ⚓

Israeli forces launched Operation Kadesh, advancing into Egypt's Sinai Peninsula toward the Suez Canal. The invasion formed part of a secret arrangement involving Britain and France, which followed Egypt's nationalization of the Suez Canal Company in July. British and French ultimatums and military intervention followed days later. International pressure, particularly from the United States and the Soviet Union, ultimately forced the invading powers to withdraw. The crisis exposed the declining ability of Britain and France to impose their will independently in the postwar international order and strengthened Egyptian President Gamal Abdel Nasser's political standing.

🧩 TRIVIA: The United Nations Emergency Force, established during the crisis, became the first armed UN peacekeeping force.

🤫 SPOILER: The military intervention failed to reverse Egypt's nationalization of the canal. The episode instead accelerated the decline of British and French imperial influence in the region.

1998 — John Glenn Returns to Space at 77 🚀

Space Shuttle Discovery launched on mission STS-95 with John Glenn aboard as a payload specialist. Glenn had become the first American to orbit Earth in 1962. His return to space at age 77 made him the oldest person to travel into orbit at that time. The mission conducted biomedical research alongside solar and technology experiments, renewing scientific attention to the effects of spaceflight on the aging human body.

🧩 TRIVIA: Glenn's first spaceflight aboard Friendship 7 lasted approximately five hours and included three orbits of Earth.

2012 — Superstorm Sandy Makes Landfall 🌊

On the evening of October 29, post-tropical cyclone Sandy came ashore near Brigantine, New Jersey, bringing destructive winds and catastrophic storm surge to the northeastern United States. Coastal communities were inundated, lower Manhattan experienced extensive flooding, and transportation and electrical infrastructure suffered widespread disruption. Sandy caused approximately 147 direct deaths across the United States and Caribbean, according to the National Hurricane Center's commonly cited count, and inflicted tens of billions of dollars in damage.

🧩 TRIVIA: At Sandy Hook, New Jersey, water levels reached approximately 8.9 feet above ground level, while the tidal gauge failed during the storm, suggesting the actual surge may have been higher.

🕵️ MYSTERY: Sandy's unusual transition from a tropical cyclone into a powerful post-tropical storm complicates comparisons with ordinary hurricanes. Its size, interaction with other weather systems, and timing near high tide all contributed to the exceptional coastal flooding.

2015 — China Announces the End of the One-Child Policy 📜

China's Communist Party leadership announced that all married couples would be permitted to have two children, ending the one-child restriction as the country's central population-control policy. Officials cited population aging, a shrinking workforce, and a skewed sex ratio. The change followed earlier exceptions for selected rural families and couples who met specified eligibility rules. The announcement represented a major reversal of a policy that had shaped Chinese family life for decades.

🧩 TRIVIA: The two-child policy was implemented through subsequent legislative changes rather than taking effect solely through the October announcement.

These pivotal events continue to shape the course of history. 🌍

────────────────────────────────

🔬 SCIENTIFIC, TECHNOLOGICAL, AND CULTURAL MILESTONES

From the operatic stage to the birth of networked computing and the evolution of everyday technology, these achievements showcase human ingenuity.

1787 — Mozart's Don Giovanni Premieres 🎭

Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart's opera, with a libretto by Lorenzo Da Ponte, received its first performance at the Estates Theatre in Prague. Blending comedy, seduction, supernatural drama, and moral reckoning, the work presented a daring portrait of a libertine whose confidence ultimately brings him face to face with consequences he cannot charm away. Its musical sophistication and dramatic range secured its place among the defining works of the operatic repertoire.

🧩 TRIVIA: The opera is classified as a dramma giocoso, a genre that combines comic and serious dramatic elements.

1945 — Reynolds Rocket Ballpoint Pen Goes on Sale ✒️

The Reynolds Rocket went on sale at Gimbels department store in New York City for $12.50. The launch produced extraordinary public demand for a pen marketed as a convenient alternative to traditional fountain pens. Although earlier ballpoint designs and patents existed, the Reynolds Rocket became the first modern ballpoint pen sold commercially in the United States. Its debut helped introduce a technology that would eventually transform everyday writing.

🧩 TRIVIA: Gimbels sold approximately 30,000 Reynolds pens during the first week, despite having initially ordered 50,000 for its stock.

🏆 FIRST: The Reynolds Rocket was the first modern ballpoint pen sold in the United States, not the first ballpoint pen ever invented.

1969 — The First ARPANET Message Is Transmitted 💻

Researchers at the University of California, Los Angeles, attempted to send the command “LOGIN” from their computer to a host at Stanford Research Institute. The experiment was part of ARPANET, an early computer network funded by the U.S. Department of Defense's Advanced Research Projects Agency. The receiving system crashed after accepting only the first two letters, leaving the historic transmission incomplete. Within approximately an hour, the connection was restored and the full command was successfully transmitted.

🧩 TRIVIA: The first message sent between the two host computers was “LO,” unintentionally creating one of the most memorable beginnings in computing history.

🌀 OBSCURE: The first transmission was not a polished demonstration of a mature network. It was a practical engineering test, and the system's crash became inseparable from the story of its success.

Human creativity and scientific inquiry continue to expand our horizons. ✨

────────────────────────────────

🎂 FAMOUS BIRTHDAYS

Today we celebrate the lives and enduring contributions of remarkable individuals born on this date.

1891 — Fanny Brice (1891–1951) — American comedian, singer, and actress who became a star of the Ziegfeld Follies and later created the radio character Baby Snooks.

🧩 TRIVIA: Barbra Streisand portrayed Brice in the Broadway musical Funny Girl and its 1968 film adaptation.

🌀 OBSCURE: Brice’s Baby Snooks character was a mischievous little girl whose childlike questions and outrageous behavior made her a radio sensation.

1897 — Joseph Goebbels (1897–1945) — Adolf Hitler’s propaganda minister, who used mass communication, censorship, and deception to promote Nazi ideology.

🧩 TRIVIA: Goebbels earned a doctorate in German literature from the University of Heidelberg in 1921.

⚠️ IRONY: The propaganda chief of a regime that promised a thousand-year empire died in 1945 as that regime collapsed.

1921 — Bill Mauldin (1921–2003) — American editorial cartoonist whose irreverent World War II cartoons portrayed the exhaustion and humanity of ordinary soldiers.

🧩 TRIVIA: Mauldin won the Pulitzer Prize for Editorial Cartooning in 1945 and again in 1959.

🌀 OBSCURE: His recurring infantrymen, Willie and Joe, exposed the gap between frontline realities and the polished image favored by military authority.

1938 — Ellen Johnson Sirleaf (age 88) — Liberian economist and politician who served as Liberia’s president from 2006 to 2018.

🧩 TRIVIA: Johnson Sirleaf shared the 2011 Nobel Peace Prize with Leymah Gbowee and Tawakkol Karman.

🏆 FIRST: She became Africa’s first elected female head of state when she took office in 2006.

1942 — Bob Ross (1942–1995) — American painter and television host whose gentle manner and landscape demonstrations made The Joy of Painting a beloved instructional program.

🧩 TRIVIA: Ross’s television series ran from 1983 to 1994 and introduced viewers to his distinctive wet-on-wet painting technique.

🌀 OBSCURE: Before becoming a painting instructor, Ross served in the U.S. Air Force and was stationed in Alaska, where the landscape influenced some of his paintings.

1944 — Denny Laine (1944–2023) — English singer, guitarist, and songwriter who helped found the Moody Blues before becoming a key member of Wings.

🧩 TRIVIA: Laine sang lead vocals on the Moody Blues’ 1964 hit recording of “Go Now.”

🔦 SPOTLIGHT: He performed on Wings’ Band on the Run, one of the group’s defining albums.

1945 — Melba Moore (age 81) — American singer and actress celebrated for her work across Broadway, soul, R&B, and dance music.

🧩 TRIVIA: Moore won the 1970 Tony Award for Best Featured Actress in a Musical for her performance in Purlie.

🏆 FIRST: Her Tony win recognized a breakthrough Broadway performance that helped establish her career as a leading stage performer.

1947 — Richard Dreyfuss (age 79) — American actor known for American Graffiti, Jaws, Close Encounters of the Third Kind, and The Goodbye Girl.

🧩 TRIVIA: Dreyfuss won the Academy Award for Best Actor for The Goodbye Girl (1977).

🏆 FIRST: At age 30, he became one of the youngest winners of the Academy Award for Best Actor.

1971 — Winona Ryder (age 55) — American actress whose roles in Beetlejuice, Heathers, and Edward Scissorhands helped define her early career.

🧩 TRIVIA: Ryder received an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actress for Little Women (1994).

🧬 HUMAN: Her later role as Joyce Byers in Stranger Things introduced her to a new generation of viewers.

1972 — Tracee Ellis Ross (age 54) — American actress, producer, and television host known for Girlfriends and Black-ish.

🧩 TRIVIA: Ross won a Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Television Series—Musical or Comedy in 2017 for Black-ish.

🧬 HUMAN: She is the daughter of singer Diana Ross and music executive Robert Ellis Silberstein.

Happy birthday to them all! 🎉

────────────────────────────────

🥀 MEMORIAM

We pause to honor the memory of notable figures who left an indelible mark on our world before their passing.

1618 — Sir Walter Raleigh (aged about 64)

English courtier, explorer, and poet whose career flourished under Elizabeth I. Raleigh helped promote English overseas exploration and was associated with the Roanoke colonization efforts. His execution under James I followed the revival of a treason sentence imposed years earlier.

🧩 TRIVIA: Raleigh's final hours became the subject of numerous later accounts, including the traditional story that he requested time to finish smoking his pipe. The anecdote should be treated as a reported tradition rather than an indisputable detail.

1911 — Joseph Pulitzer (aged 64)

Hungarian-born American newspaper publisher who transformed mass-circulation journalism through the New York World and other publishing ventures. His legacy includes the prizes established through his bequest to recognize excellence in journalism, literature, music, and other fields.

🧩 TRIVIA: Pulitzer's will provided funding for the Columbia University Graduate School of Journalism, which opened in 1912.

1924 — Frances Hodgson Burnett (aged 74)

British-American novelist remembered for Little Lord Fauntleroy, A Little Princess, and The Secret Garden. Her fiction explored childhood, imagination, hardship, and personal transformation, becoming a lasting part of children's literature.

🧩 TRIVIA: The Secret Garden was published in book form in 1911 after first appearing in serial form.

1971 — Duane Allman (aged 24)

American guitarist and co-founder of the Allman Brothers Band. His expressive slide-guitar playing helped define Southern rock, combining blues traditions with improvisational musicianship. He died in a motorcycle accident in Macon, Georgia.

🧩 TRIVIA: The Allman Brothers Band's album Eat a Peach was completed and released after Allman's death.

2024 — Teri Garr (aged 79)

American actress and comedian celebrated for Young Frankenstein, Close Encounters of the Third Kind, and her Academy Award-nominated performance in Tootsie. Her comic timing and distinctive screen presence made her a memorable figure in American film and television.

🧩 TRIVIA: Garr received an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actress for Tootsie in 1983.

In fond remembrance of them all. 🕯️

────────────────────────────────

🏟️ SPORTS HIGHLIGHTS

Moments of athletic triumph, dramatic competition, and legendary achievements that captivated sports fans worldwide.

1960 — Cassius Clay Makes His Professional Debut 🥊

Cassius Clay, who would later become Muhammad Ali, defeated Tunney Hunsaker by decision in a six-round professional boxing match in Louisville, Kentucky. The bout began a career that would transform boxing through extraordinary athletic ability, theatrical confidence, and an outspoken public presence.

🧩 TRIVIA: Clay had won the light-heavyweight gold medal at the 1960 Summer Olympics in Rome just months before his professional debut.

2014 — San Francisco Giants Win the World Series ⚾

The San Francisco Giants defeated the Kansas City Royals 3–2 in Game 7 of the World Series. Madison Bumgarner, pitching in relief on two days' rest, delivered five scoreless innings to preserve the lead and secure the championship. His performance became one of the defining postseason pitching efforts of the modern era.

🧩 TRIVIA: Bumgarner was named World Series Most Valuable Player after allowing just one earned run across 21 innings during the series.

2017 — Lewis Hamilton Clinches His Fourth Formula One Title 🏎️

Lewis Hamilton secured the 2017 Formula One World Drivers' Championship at the Mexican Grand Prix. Although a first-lap collision damaged his race and he finished ninth, his accumulated points were sufficient to clinch the championship with two rounds remaining.

🧩 TRIVIA: The title made Hamilton the fifth driver to win at least four Formula One World Drivers' Championships.

2018 — Klay Thompson Sets an NBA Three-Point Record 🏀

Klay Thompson scored 52 points and made 14 three-pointers in the Golden State Warriors' 149–124 victory over the Chicago Bulls. His performance established a new NBA single-game record for three-pointers made, surpassing the previous mark held by teammate Stephen Curry.

🧩 TRIVIA: Thompson set the record in just 27 minutes of playing time.

These athletic triumphs remind us of the power of passion and perseverance. 🏆

────────────────────────────────

📝 HISTORY QUIZ OF THE DAY

October 29, 2026

❓ Question: On October 29, 1969, what two-letter message became the first transmission between host computers on ARPANET, the precursor to today's Internet?

[A] OK
[B] LO
[C] GO
[D] HI

✅ Answer: [B] — LO. Researchers at UCLA attempted to send the command “LOGIN” to a computer at Stanford Research Institute. The receiving system crashed after the first two letters, leaving “LO” as the first message successfully transmitted between the two hosts.

────────────────────────────────

CLOSING

October 29 is a date of entrances and exits. Cyrus entered Babylon after his army had already secured the city. Turkey declared a republic as an imperial order gave way to a new political identity. Wall Street discovered that speculation could turn confidence into panic, while the Suez Crisis demonstrated that old imperial powers could no longer dictate outcomes simply because they had done so before. And in a California computer laboratory, an ambitious message intended to say “LOGIN” stopped at “LO”—an accidental beginning whose importance would grow far beyond the intentions of the people who sent it.

History rarely offers its participants a view of the finished picture. They act with incomplete information, uncertain outcomes, and the stubborn belief that the next step will make sense of the last. Sometimes it does. Sometimes the system crashes after two letters. Either way, the consequences keep moving.

Happy 26th birthday to the gorgeous, hugely talented Rapper, Singer, Songwriter, Composer, Musician, TV Host, Dancer, Superstar and Fashion & Global Icon, the One & Only #GISELLE,  who rings in her 26th, trending in the Top 10 of X Worldwide with ENCHANTED GISELLE DAY! 👏🎂🎉🌟💥🔝🔟✖️🌎🐐👑 🩷
Giselle became famous as the Main Rapper and Vocalist of the hugely popular Girl Group aespa, one of the Best-selling K-Pop Groups of the Era! Giselle stands out for her powerful Rap, her cool charismatic “girl crush” presence onstage and her stylish, globally adaptable force in fourth-generation K-pop! Her trilingual abilities enhance aespa's global appeal, often incorporating English rap verses that resonate internationally. She has greatly contributed to aespa's global success, multiple million-seller albums, and strong Billboard charting! Her rapid rise from a brief training period to worldwide recognition highlights both her exceptional talent and remarkable ability to adapt. aespa’s boundary-pushing concepts remain at the forefront of K-pop innovation, with Giselle’s distinctive rap style serving as a crucial driving force.

Giselle was born in the Gangnam District of Seoul to a South Korean mother and a Japanese father, and grew up in Tokyo, studying at the Tokyo International School and International School of the Sacred Heart. Giselle was an alto in her school choir during her high school years in Japan, and was known for her rich, low-toned vocal texture even as a teenager! She was also part of a girls’ a cappella team, where her deep, resonant voice stood out in harmonies. Her excellent pitch control and vocal stability later translated into her precise rap delivery and live vocal performance as a member of aespa. She was introduced to K-pop in the 2nd year of high school, and returned to Korea after graduation, to audition for SM Entertainment! Giselle was unveiled as the 3rd member of Aespa on November 6, 2020, and officially debuted with the group's debut single "Black Mamba" on November 17! In December, 2021, Giselle sang on the song "Zoo" for the 2021 Winter SM Town: SMCU Express and in June, 2022, she featured in BOL4's single "Lips" which reached #102 on the Circle Digital chart! On October 9, 2024, Giselle released her own solo song "Dopamine' with aespa's Singles album 'SYNK : PARALLEL LINE', which topped iTunes Charts in 14+ countries and reached #3 on US iTunes! "Dopamine" scored the 8th Highest New entry on the Worldwide iTunes song chart, reaching #94 with just a few hours tracking! Since 'Dopamine', Giselle has continued releasing individual material through aespa’s tour-related SYNK projects, including the 2025 solo “Tornado” from SYNK: aeXIS LINE which she co-wrote and composed, the 2026 unit track “Lollipop” with Ningning from the same series, also co-written and composed by her, and the September 2026 solo “BYEB4HELLO” from SYNK: COMPLaeXITY again with her writing and composition credits.

Giselle is also a very talented host, and in 2024, she hosted the 2024 Visit Seoul Z-Line series (a multi-episode web campaign on VisitSeoul TV) for the Seoul Tourism Organization. It featured her as the guest host leading solo travel content around Seoul, covering spots in Hannam-dong and other areas, with episodes released throughout June 2024.
                                                                                                     
Giselle has won 145 of awards out of 315 nominations as a member of aespa. aespa swept the 2024 Melon Music Awards (MMA), becoming the first female Act to win 3 Daesangs including Album of the Year for their debut full album! The group won the Rookie of the Year Award at all major music awards in South Korea including the MelOn Music Awards (MMA), the MAMA Awards (MAMA), the Golden Disc Awards (GDA), the Seoul Music Awards (SMA), the Circle Chart Music Awards (GCMA), and the Korean Music Awards (KMA). In March 2022, aespa won Song of the Year for "Next Level" at the 19th Korean Music Awards, becoming the 2nd girl group to have won the award! The Group has won 18 MelOn Music Awards, 11 Asia Pop Music Awards, 12 MAMA Awards, 9 Golden Disc Awards, 8 FACT Music Awards, 8 Hanteo Music Awards, 6 Seoul Music Awards, 6 Korean Music Awards, 5 TME live International Awards, 4 Circle chart Music Awards, 4 Asia Artist Awards, 4 MTV Video Music Awards Japan, 4 Tencent Music Entertainment Awards, 3 Asian Star Entertainer Awards, 3 D awards, 2 Japan Gold Disc Awards, 1 MTV Europe Music Award, 1 Mubeat Award, 1 Music Award Japan, 1 Philippine K-Pop Award, 1 Tik Tok Award Korea and a Visionary Award at Billboard Women In Music! In 2022 aespa received a Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism Commendation!

Giselle is one of 4th-generation K-pop’s most influential fashion figures, known for her sharp, versatile style that blends Tokyo street edge, Seoul minimalism, and high-fashion edge. In 2023, She became a Global Ambassador for Givenchy, and was the first K-pop idol to open a Givenchy show  at Paris Fashion week! In 2024, she sat in the front row at PFW rocking a Celine leather aviator jacket + pleated mini, and sparked the global “Giselle jacket” dupe trend! Since 2024 she has served as a global brand ambassador for Loewe, causing a media blitz at the Fall Winter 2024 women's runway show in Paris! On September 9, 2024, she was appointed as the muse of the Korean cosmetics brand Either& and in 2025, she starred on the cover of Vogue Korea “Icons” wearing custom Chanel, becoming the 1st idol to fuse a traditional Korean jacket with haute couture. She has also been appointed muse or ambassador for other brands including SENKA, Maison Kitsuné, while her bold event looks consistently set trends and earn praise!

Giselle is also a philanthropist and contributes to causes she cares about. In June 2022, she made an anonymous donation of KR₩10 million to Yuhengsa, an organization focused on helping abandoned animals. During aespa's 'Synk: Parallel Line tour' stop in LA, in February 2025, the group announced a donation of concert proceeds to fire relief efforts. Giselle performed, contributing to the group's impact on disaster aid. In October 2025, Giselle attended W Korea’s 20th “Love Your W” Breast Cancer Awareness Campaign charity gala in Seoul alongside the other aespa members. The event, held at the Four Seasons Hotel, aimed to raise funds and awareness for breast cancer research, free screenings, and support for patients, and her presence as part of the high-profile group helped bring further attention to the cause. In late October 2025 Giselle offered during a livestream to help pay for a fan's tuition. In November 2025, aespa as a group donated 500,000 Hong Kong dollars ($64,000) to the Hong Kong Red Cross for relief efforts following the deadly Tai Po apartment fire. 

Giselle’s combination of skill and down-to-earth humility has made her a clear fan favorite. With aespa continuing to top the charts, her contributions highlight just how essential she is to the group’s chemistry and overall success.

text:
What makes a college a good fit for rural students?

For Dr. Trey Jarboe, it was finding an affordable, quality education close to home, professors and staff who saw his potential, and opportunities that changed what he believed was possible for his life.

Jarboe came to University of the Cumberlands as a first-generation student from Whitley County, Kentucky. He went on to earn three degrees and now serves as Cumberlands' executive vice president for student experience.

His experience offers some valuable advice for rural students choosing a college: Look for a place that expands your possibilities, supports you along the way, makes earning a degree financially realistic, and prepares you for the life you actually want.

Because success doesn't have to mean leaving home. Sometimes education gives you new ways to build a life there.

Fraud Scandal Drags Flanagan as Minnesota's Senate Seat Slides   Toward the GOP

Bloomberg Government flagged the dynamic   Monday: Minnesota’s sprawling welfare-fraud scandals — federal prosecutors describe alleged fraud across Medicaid, housing aid, and pandemic-era programs that could reach as much as $9 billion, roughly 15% of the state budget, under Gov. Tim Walz’s administration — are overshadowing what was supposed to be a safe Democratic seat. The Center Square: With less than two weeks until Election Day, the Minnesota U.S. Senate race has shifted in favor of Republican and former sports broadcaster Michele Tafoya. 
The Cook Political Report shifted its rating from “Likely Democrat” to “Lean Democrat.” The shift comes as fraud, crime, and the economy take center stage in the race between Tafoya and Democratic Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan.   “Peggy Flanagan will be a rubber stamp for the far-left socialist agenda,” Tafoya said Wednesday. “Our campaign has the support of law enforcement,   farmers, and business owners who are tired of failed policies. Minnesotans are ready to end single-party control. Peggy offers excuses. I’ll deliver   accountability.” 
Flanagan has continued to tie Tafoya to President Donald   Trump, saying she is “lockstep with Trump’s MAGA agenda.” (The Center Square). Flanagan still leads,   but barely: about 47% to 42.6% in the recent poll average, and 46–45 in one late-September survey. A Tafoya win would be the first Republican statewide victory in Minnesota since 2006.

text:
FBI offers 7million Naira reward for Nigerian fra¥dster who disappeared at Atlanta airport before she was to start her 8-year sentence 

The United States Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has announced a $5,000 reward for information leading to the arrest of Emuobosan Emmanuella Hall, a 46-year-old Nigerian citizen and U.S. permanent resident accused of fleeing before beginning an eight-year prison sentence. 

Hall, who was convicted for her role in a romance-fraud scheme, was sentenced to 96 months in prison by U.S. District Judge Jane Milazzo in January 2026 and ordered to surrender to the Bureau of Prisons by March 25. 

However, she failed to report as directed. Investigators said GPS data from her monitoring device showed her last known location was Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport on March 24, 2026, where the device stopped transmitting. 

Hall had reportedly informed her probation officer that she was scheduled to fly to Minnesota, where she was to serve her sentence, but airline records showed she never boarded the flight. 

A federal grand jury subsequently indicted her on October 23, 2026, for failing to surrender to the Bureau of Prisons, and a warrant has been issued for her arrest. 

Hall had earlier pleaded guilty to conspiring to defraud mostly older women through romance scams. Court documents said members of the syndicate posed online as generals, philanthropists and entrepreneurs, built romantic relationships with victims and later persuaded them to send money under false pretences. 

Hall and her co-defendant, Kenneth Akpieyi, allegedly used Le Beau Monde LLC to process victims’ funds. Hall admitted responsibility for $851,207 in losses, while Akpieyi was held responsible for more than $3.5 million and sentenced to 25 years in prison. 

If convicted of the new charge, Hall could receive up to 10 additional years behind bars, consecutive to her existing sentence.

text:
Dialect coach Erik Singer @AccentVoiceGuy has a new book coming out early next year! “The Accent Code: Unlocking the mysteries of how we talk and what it says about who we are”. Here’s the blurb:

Why do so many movie villains have British accents? Why do some New Englanders say “carr” and others “cahh”? Why does Alaskan Sarah Palin sound like she’s from Minnesota?

Where do accents come from, and why do people speak with different accents in the first place? Dialect coach Erik Singer has spent decades training Hollywood actors in the nuances of accents. How we pronounce our words isn’t just a matter of how we move our mouths. Accents come with a host of associations—geography, class, intelligence, attitude—that influence how we express our identities and how we perceive those of others. In The Accent Code, Singer offers an irresistible guide to how accents work and what they mean, revealing the hidden ways accents shape our lives.

Language never stops changing: it reflects the churn of human striving and conflict, from sweeping developments like migration and war to the more quotidian intrigue of the high school cafeteria. With wit, erudition, and inexhaustible curiosity, Singer leaps across time and geography to bring a symphony of past and present accents to life. Along the way, he examines what accents might have to do with political polarization, deconstructs the dangerous biases we apply to the ways people speak, and spotlights the ingenuity of the linguists who documented language change in real time. Armed with a dialect coach’s grasp of language from the inside out, we come to understand that an accent says so much more about us than where we’re from.

Drawing on history, linguistics, and pop culture, The Accent Code is an exhilarating tour of the rich variety of human communication and identity.

text:
Everybody is talking about $GOOGL, $AMZN, $NOW and $MSFT earnings. But there are other companies reporting some very interesting developments, and I think we should pay attention to them too.

I understand why the megacaps dominate the conversation. Their earnings influence entire sectors, indexes and market expectations.

But this week I spent some time going through the Q3 earnings releases, management calls and business updates of six other companies.

$GEV, $STRL, $PI, $BLKB, $AUR and $NEXT.

They operate in very different industries, but each has something worth investigating.

And I want to make an important distinction before going further. These are not six automatic buying opportunities. Some are already generating substantial profits, while others are still trying to prove that their business models can work at scale.

1. $GEV | GE Vernova. The electricity infrastructure opportunity is becoming very real.
GE Vernova reported Q3 revenue of $12.64B, growing 27%, with organic growth of 18%.

Orders reached approximately $29.3B, while the total backlog climbed to $197B. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 15.4%.

Those are strong results, but what interests me most is what happens after the initial equipment sale.

GE Vernova manufactures gas turbines, power generation equipment, transformers and other critical electrical infrastructure.

When a customer orders a gas turbine, the company doesn't simply deliver the machine and forget about it.

That equipment needs maintenance, inspections, replacement parts and service over decades.

Management estimates approximately $500M in lifetime services revenue for every gigawatt of its HA turbine fleet over 20 years.

That gives the business a potentially valuable recurring revenue component.

There is also evidence of pricing power. Management expects 2026 gas equipment orders to carry prices per kilowatt approximately 50% higher than orders placed in 2025.

But here is what I would watch carefully.

GE Vernova generated $5.41B in free cash flow during Q3, largely supported by customer advance payments.

That is useful financing, but advance payments are not the same as sustainable operating profits.

And the Wind business continues facing challenges.

My read: Strong operating momentum, significant demand visibility and improving pricing power. The next question is how much of that backlog converts into sustainable margins and normalized cash flow.

2. $STRL | Sterling Infrastructure. Data centers need much more than GPUs.

This company delivered one of the most impressive growth reports in the group.
Q3 revenue reached $1.56B, increasing 127% year over year.

But there is an important detail.

Part of that increase came from acquisitions. Organic revenue growth was approximately 70%, which is still remarkable.

Adjusted EBITDA reached $337.8M, while adjusted diluted EPS increased to $7.58.

What does Sterling actually do?

Think about everything required before a data center can begin operating.

Land preparation, foundations, roads, utility infrastructure and electrical installation.

Sterling operates in those parts of the construction process.

It also works on semiconductor facilities and advanced industrial projects.

The company reported $4.14B in signed backlog and another $2B in unsigned awards.

Management also described a broader opportunity pipeline approaching $8B.

That is encouraging, but I would never treat the entire $8B as guaranteed revenue.

Signed contracts, unsigned awards and potential future project phases carry very different levels of certainty.

The company is also expanding its electrical installation business, which may have lower margins than certain site development activities but potentially better capital efficiency.

My read: One of the strongest operating growth stories in this group. I want to monitor new contract conversion, project margins, labor availability and cash generation.

The demand is impressive. Execution at this pace becomes the next challenge.

3. $PI | Impinj. A semiconductor company that helps businesses understand where their products actually are.

This business deserves attention for a completely different reason.

Impinj reported record Q3 revenue of $112.1M, with adjusted EBITDA of $24.5M and non-GAAP EPS of $0.69.
Its endpoint IC business generated $97.3M.

Impinj develops RFID technology that allows companies to identify and track individual items.

Imagine a large retailer with millions of products moving between suppliers, warehouses and stores.

Traditional inventory systems often depend on manual scanning and incomplete information.

Impinj provides chips that are embedded into RFID tags, along with readers and other technology that allow businesses to identify those items automatically.

That can improve inventory accuracy, reduce losses and make supply chains more efficient.

And here is the interesting business mechanism.

As customers deploy more RFID systems, the number of tagged products can continue increasing.

That creates ongoing demand for endpoint chips.

Impinj is also developing enterprise software intended to help customers use the collected information more effectively.

But software monetization is still in its early stages.

Management expects Q4 revenue of $104M to $107M, below Q3, partly because some enterprise deployments have shifted into 2027 and customers are consuming previously purchased equipment.

My read: A commercially established semiconductor business with an interesting expansion opportunity.

But I want to see whether delayed deployments return, production bottlenecks improve and the software business begins generating meaningful revenue.

4. $BLKB | Blackbaud. Not every software investment needs explosive revenue growth.

This is a different kind of software business.

Blackbaud provides software used by nonprofits, educational institutions and other organizations to manage fundraising, donors, finances and operations.

Q3 revenue reached $292.6M, growing 4.1%.
That is not spectacular growth.

But recurring revenue represented approximately 98% of total revenue.

Adjusted EBITDA reached $111.1M, with a 38% margin, while non-GAAP free cash flow reached $126M.

Non-GAAP EPS increased approximately 24% to $1.36.

But that doesn't mean the business itself grew 24%.

A meaningful part of the EPS improvement came from share repurchases reducing the number of shares outstanding.

That can create shareholder value when management buys shares at reasonable valuations.

But I don't want to confuse improving earnings per share with accelerating business demand.

Blackbaud is also introducing new AI products, but management acknowledged that these products are not yet contributing meaningful revenue.

Customer retention is another issue worth monitoring.

My read: An established, cash generating software business with moderate growth and improving per-share economics.

The important questions are whether retention improves, organic growth accelerates and capital allocation creates lasting value.

5. $AUR | Aurora Innovation. The technology works. Now the business has to scale.

Aurora is one of the most interesting companies in this group, but also one of the riskiest.

The company has moved beyond simply demonstrating autonomous trucking technology.

It is operating commercial freight routes without a driver behind the wheel.

Management reported approximately 500,000 commercial driverless miles and is expanding its operational network.
Aurora also announced a memorandum of understanding with Charger Logistics involving up to 500 autonomous trucks.

But that agreement is nonbinding, and this distinction matters.

The company wants to transition toward a Driver as a Service model.

Instead of Aurora owning every truck, fleet operators would own the vehicles and pay for the autonomous driving technology.

That could eventually create a more capital efficient business.

But the financial numbers show how early this opportunity remains.

Q3 revenue was only $3M, compared with an operating loss of $257M.

The company used approximately $170M in operating cash and ended the quarter with roughly $1.03B in cash and short term investments.

Management is targeting a production rate of 20 trucks per week by early December, but the manufacturing ramp is approximately six weeks behind its original plan.

Its ambition remains to exit 2027 with more than 1,000 driverless trucks operating.

My read: Real commercial progress, but the economic model is not proven.

I want to see reliable production, paid utilization, customer contracts, operating costs per truck and eventually positive unit economics.

This is not yet an earnings growth story. It is a commercial scaling and capital efficiency thesis.

6. $NEXT | NextDecade. A completely different infrastructure opportunity.

NextDecade is developing the Rio Grande LNG export facility in Texas.

Unlike the previous companies, this is primarily a construction and future cash generation story rather than a conventional operating earnings report.

The latest Q3 update shows meaningful progress.

Trains 1 and 2 reached approximately 79.7% overall completion.

Management expects first gas before the end of 2026, with first LNG production from Train 1 during Q2 2027.
That is encouraging because the project is progressing toward actual operations.

But there is an important distinction between construction completion and commercial readiness.

For Trains 1 and 2, commissioning was only 4.9% complete at the September reporting date.

Complex industrial facilities still need to demonstrate that their systems can operate safely and reliably.

And the financial structure is just as important.

NextDecade does not own all the economic benefits of every LNG train.

Its Phase 1 joint venture interest entitles it to receive up to 20.8% of available cash distributions during operations.

Other trains have different ownership and distribution arrangements.

That means the value of the business cannot be calculated by assuming that every dollar of project cash flow belongs to NextDecade shareholders.

Debt service, operating expenses, contractual allocations and partner distributions all matter.

My read: Real physical progress toward LNG production, but substantial commissioning, financing and cash distribution questions remain.

I want the first operating milestones to be achieved before treating projected project economics as established cash generation.

Now, what do these six companies tell me?

I wouldn't put them in the same category.

$GEV and $STRL have the strongest evidence of operating expansion.

Both are benefiting from substantial infrastructure demand and already generating meaningful profits.

$PI and $BLKB have established operating businesses, but very different growth profiles.

Impinj has a growing hardware platform and an emerging software opportunity.

Blackbaud has an established recurring revenue base and strong cash generation, but slower growth and retention challenges.

$AUR and $NEXT are earlier in their economic development.

Both have real operational progress, but neither has fully demonstrated the profitable scale economics that would justify treating future projections as proven results.

And this is why I enjoy researching companies outside the main earnings conversation.

There are important developments happening in power generation, electrical infrastructure, semiconductor manufacturing, industrial automation, software, autonomous transportation and LNG.

Some of these companies are directly exposed to AI infrastructure spending. Others have completely different business drivers.

But good earnings, a promising business and an attractive stock price are three separate questions.

I can appreciate the growth of $STRL without automatically assuming the current valuation is attractive.

I can recognize the opportunity at $AUR without ignoring its cash consumption.

And I can like the business model of $PI or $BLKB while still questioning their current growth assumptions.

My next step is valuation and manual chart analysis.

I want to know what investors are already paying for these future results, where each stock sits on its weekly chart and whether the current price offers a reasonable risk and reward relationship.

For now, these are companies worth investigating, not a buy list.

The megacaps deserve attention. But they are not the entire market.

Sometimes the most useful research starts by looking at the businesses that are building, operating and supporting the infrastructure behind the headlines.

And sometimes it starts with companies that have nothing to do with the headline theme at all.

Don't just follow the loudest earnings conversation. Follow the evidence.

My investing journal, not financial advice.

text:
Why did Samsung SELLOFF despite record earnings?

Samsung just reported its third quarter earnings and I think the biggest takeaway here is that 2027 could be an even bigger year for the memory industry than 2026. The company generated approximately $146 billion in revenue and $80 billion in operating profit in just three months. Revenue increased 14% quarter over quarter, while operating profit jumped 20%, bringing operating margins to an incredible 55%. To put that into perspective, Samsung generated just 12.2 trillion won in operating profit during the same quarter last year, compared with 107.4 trillion won today. And almost all of that came from semiconductors. Samsung's semiconductor division generated approximately 147.1 trillion won in revenue and 106.5 trillion won in operating profit, largely driven by higher memory prices and demand for AI infrastructure. However, despite these record numbers, Samsung actually missed expectations. Revenue came in 3% below consensus and 7% below UBS estimates, while operating profit missed UBS estimates by approximately 9%. Net income also came in 14% below consensus, partly because of 9.5 trillion won in net finance expenses.

But I think investors had VERY high expectations going into this and are focusing too much on the earnings miss and not enough on what Samsung said about 2027. One of the biggest takeaways was just how much memory prices are increasing. Samsung disclosed that DRAM average selling prices increased approximately 20% quarter over quarter, while NAND prices increased by a high teens percentage. Meanwhile, shipment volumes increased by only single digit percentages. So most of the growth wasn't coming from Samsung selling significantly more memory but rather coming from charging significantly higher prices. And this is happening across several different memory categories simultaneously. We've been talking a lot about HBM lately, especially following SK Hynix's earnings yesterday, but conventional DRAM and NAND are becoming increasingly important parts of the AI infrastructure buildout. AI data centers need HBM for accelerators, conventional DRAM for CPUs and servers, and NAND for storage. Samsung is benefiting from all three.

Now, here's where things get REALLY interesting. Samsung reported that HBM4 sales increased more than threefold quarter over quarter and HBM4 now accounts for approximately 60% of its total HBM sales. But the most important comment came from Jaejune Kim, Samsung's memory business executive, who confirmed that the company's entire planned HBM supply for 2027 is already SOLD OUT, with pricing negotiations concluded at its target levels. And despite that, customers are still requesting additional supply. Also, earlier Korean media reports suggested Samsung was quoting HBM4 prices in the mid to high $4 range per gigabit, compared with approximately $1.50 per gigabit for HBM3E. That's potentially more than THREE TIMES the pricing of the previous generation.

Now, Samsung hasn't confirmed the exact final contract prices, but management saying negotiations concluded at its target levels suggests the company has secured favorable pricing for next year. And remember, there were earlier rumors that Nvidia was pushing back against Samsung's proposed HBM4 pricing. So there's speculation that Nvidia may have ultimately accepted Samsung's asking price, although that hasn't been officially confirmed. If those reported prices are accurate, Samsung could generate substantially more revenue from its HBM4 business in 2027, even without a proportional increase in production volumes. There's also speculation that Nvidia could offer separate Rubin configurations using Samsung's HBM4 at a premium compared with configurations using SK Hynix or Micron memory. That's not confirmed, but it's something worth following. Samsung is also preparing to begin mass production of HBM4E in 2027. And I think this is particularly important because Samsung doesn't necessarily need to take significant market share away from SK Hynix to benefit. If demand continues growing faster than supply, both companies can increase sales and maintain stronger pricing.

Another part of the earnings call that I found interesting was Samsung's discussion of AI agents and how they're creating additional demand for NAND storage. We've already seen how AI training created enormous demand for HBM but AI inference and agentic workloads are creating entirely different memory requirements. Samsung specifically mentioned KV cache, which is essentially information an AI model stores from previous tokens so it doesn't have to repeatedly process the same information. As AI agents become more advanced, handle longer conversations, and perform tasks over extended periods, the amount of information that needs to be stored and retrieved increases significantly. Samsung believes this is creating additional demand for high performance TLC SSDs. But the company also mentioned that cloud based personal AI agent services are increasingly moving toward allocating dedicated virtual machines to individual users. Essentially, individual AI agents could have their own dedicated computing environments and storage rather than sharing the same resources. And that creates demand for high density QLC SSDs, which provide larger amounts of storage at a lower cost per bit. Samsung is already preparing a 256TB enterprise SSD for commercial launch in early 2027. And all of this is happening while supply remains extremely constrained. Samsung expects the memory shortage to continue through 2028, even as manufacturers significantly increase capital spending.

Samsung has also signed multiyear memory supply agreements with 10 major customers and is negotiating similar agreements with another 10. These agreements aren't limited to hyperscalers either. Samsung is seeing demand from automotive, mobile, and networking customers. The company ultimately wants approximately 60% to 70% of its production capacity covered by multiyear agreements by 2030. That would give Samsung much better visibility into future demand and make it easier to plan production and capital expenditures. Speaking of capital expenditures, Samsung expects to spend approximately 84.4 trillion won in 2026, an increase of 31.7 trillion won from last year. Of that amount, approximately 76.8 trillion won will go toward semiconductors, representing roughly a 62% increase from 2025. And management expects semiconductor capital spending to increase again in 2027.

This is also important for companies like Lam Research, KLA , ASML, which supply the equipment needed to expand semiconductor manufacturing. Samsung also provided some updates on its foundry business. The company expects its 2nm project wins to more than double in 2026 compared with last year, with some of those projects coming from major cloud providers and AI customers. Its Taylor, Texas facility is also expected to begin production in 2027. But I wouldn't focus too much on foundry just yet. The business remains loss making, and competing with TSMC isn't going to be easy. Memory is still the main reason Samsung's earnings are growing so quickly.

Now, another important announcement was Samsung's shareholder return program. The company expects to return approximately 90 trillion to 110 trillion won to shareholders for 2026 through dividends and share repurchases. Samsung announced a 30 trillion won cash dividend for the third quarter, equivalent to 4,601 won per common and preferred share. And with approximately 35 trillion won already planned or completed, the company expects another 55 trillion to 75 trillion won to be returned to shareholders. More importantly, management confirmed that a significant portion of those remaining funds will go toward share repurchases and cancellations. The cancellation part is important because Samsung will permanently retire those shares, reducing the total number of shares outstanding. Samsung also acknowledged the valuation gap between common and preferred shares and said it would consider adjusting the proportion of preferred shares included in its buyback program. However, the company won't finalize the exact amounts and execution plans until its board meeting in late January 2027.

And that brings us to why Samsung's stock actually sold off following the earnings announcement. Part of the reaction was the earnings miss, but investors were also disappointed that Samsung didn't immediately announce more specific buyback detail. I actually viewed the shareholder return guidance positively because the additional 55 trillion to 75 trillion won was above investor expectations, which ranged from no additional returns to approximately 50 trillion won in the fourth quarter. So the problem wasn't necessarily the size of the shareholder returns. It was the lack of clarity around when and how the remaining funds would be distributed. The other issue was Samsung's outlook compared with SK Hynix. SK Hynix said yesterday that its DRAM and HBM supply was already sold out through 2029 and that memory shortages could potentially continue into 2030. Samsung, meanwhile, expects supply to remain constrained through 2028. That's still extremely bullish, but investors had just heard SK Hynix provide an even more aggressive outlook. And with expectations already so high, even slightly more conservative commentary can disappoint.  There's also an interesting theory going around that Samsung might be holding back some positive announcements because of its controlling family. Long story short, Samsung's chairman is set to receive approximately $1.9 billion worth of shares from his mother, and the gift tax bill is calculated using the average share price over a four month period ending in January 2027. The lower the stock price during that period, the lower the potential tax bill. And what's interesting is that Samsung has delayed announcing the full details of its massive share buyback program until late January, right after that valuation period ends. This makes a lot of sense to me.

Now, there are still some risks worth monitoring. Samsung's semiconductor business is benefiting from higher memory prices, but those same prices are putting pressure on its smartphone and consumer electronics businesses. The company's Device eXperience division reported an operating loss of 0.8 trillion won during the quarter, partly reflecting higher component costs. And eventually, higher memory prices could begin affecting demand for smartphones, PCs, and other electronics. But when I look at Samsung's earnings alongside SK Hynix's results yesterday, I think the broader takeaway is pretty clear, this is a 2027 story, not a 2026 story. Samsung is already generating extraordinary profits, but its HBM4 ramp is accelerating, its planned 2027 HBM supply is already sold out at negotiated target prices, and the company expects memory demand to exceed available supply by an even greater margin next year. And that's before considering additional demand from AI agents, inference, and enterprise storage. I am happy as a shareholder, if you are a long term investor, ignore the noise and you will very happy over the next 2 years.

text:
A cow on his family's ranch did not survive calving season, so he took the calf and bottle fed it himself.

He was also the starting quarterback of his high school football team at 14 years old.

Byrd Ficklin is a quarterback at Utah now, and he grew up on a cattle ranch in Oktaha, Oklahoma, about 20 minutes outside Muskogee.

His mother Brandy and his stepfather Mark run it. Cows, goats, chickens and donkeys. He has a horse out there named Clutch.

His parents both went to Bacone College, a small school in Muskogee. His mother played soccer. His father Justin played football. Ficklin spent the first years of his life running around that campus.

Then he got to Muskogee High and became the varsity starter as a freshman. Muskogee calls its teams the Roughers.

That first team went 2 and 8.

The next year they went 10 and 3.

The year after that they went 12 and 2 and won the Oklahoma 6A-II state championship, which Muskogee had not won in more than 30 years.

Here is what his former coach Travis Hill says about what that did to the town.

He says Ficklin "brought the community all together."

Now here is the part that does not make sense.

Not one Power Four program offered him a scholarship.

His family believes there were two reasons. He was in the wrong corner of Oklahoma, too far from where the big schools do their looking. And he throws left handed, which a lot of coaches quietly do not want.

He could have transferred to a Texas school and fixed the exposure problem in one move. He stayed in Muskogee.

Brent Venables and Oklahoma came around late. Then on November 20 of 2024, Kyle Whittingham called from Utah, and Ficklin committed.

Then Whittingham left for Michigan and took the offensive coordinator with him.

The new head coach, Morgan Scalley, called and made the case for staying.

Ficklin stayed anyway.

"Utah feels like home."

Be straight about it. He is a backup. Devon Dampier is the starter in that Big 12 offense and Ficklin is in a gadget role, and Dampier is headed for the NFL, which means this probably is not Ficklin's team until 2027. Winning a state title in Oklahoma does not make anybody a college starter.

Here is what his mother says about how they raised him.

"We've always been really big on letting Byrd go and be a kid."

And here is his father, on where he is right now.

"I think he now knows he's ready, but he's still the next guy."

On a ranch you feed the thing that cannot feed itself yet, and then you wait on it.

Here is what Byrd Ficklin says about waiting.

"I live every day like my time will come."
