FBI offers 7million Naira reward for Nigerian fra¥dster who disappeared at Atlanta airport before she was to start her 8-year sentence 

The United States Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has announced a $5,000 reward for information leading to the arrest of Emuobosan Emmanuella Hall, a 46-year-old Nigerian citizen and U.S. permanent resident accused of fleeing before beginning an eight-year prison sentence. 

Hall, who was convicted for her role in a romance-fraud scheme, was sentenced to 96 months in prison by U.S. District Judge Jane Milazzo in January 2026 and ordered to surrender to the Bureau of Prisons by March 25. 

However, she failed to report as directed. Investigators said GPS data from her monitoring device showed her last known location was Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport on March 24, 2026, where the device stopped transmitting. 

Hall had reportedly informed her probation officer that she was scheduled to fly to Minnesota, where she was to serve her sentence, but airline records showed she never boarded the flight. 

A federal grand jury subsequently indicted her on October 23, 2026, for failing to surrender to the Bureau of Prisons, and a warrant has been issued for her arrest. 

Hall had earlier pleaded guilty to conspiring to defraud mostly older women through romance scams. Court documents said members of the syndicate posed online as generals, philanthropists and entrepreneurs, built romantic relationships with victims and later persuaded them to send money under false pretences. 

Hall and her co-defendant, Kenneth Akpieyi, allegedly used Le Beau Monde LLC to process victims’ funds. Hall admitted responsibility for $851,207 in losses, while Akpieyi was held responsible for more than $3.5 million and sentenced to 25 years in prison. 

If convicted of the new charge, Hall could receive up to 10 additional years behind bars, consecutive to her existing sentence.

text:
STORY 3: It started with a dog named Cupcake 🐶

Honolulu Civil Beat reports that this saga began with a dog-sitting dispute.

Dominique Bird, 39, a Honolulu state worker, says she met Quan "David" Hoang Vu, 32, on Tinder and dated him for about three months last summer. He was "like a golden retriever," she says: friendly, seemingly wealthy, living at the upscale Victoria Place in Kakaʻako. When he left for what he called a one-week business trip to California, she dog-sat his spaniel mix, Cupcake. Cupcake's diet included blueberries and coconut water. Fancy pup.

The trip stretched past three weeks. Bird says Vu came back, told her he'd been seeing another woman, and never paid back the $75 for the dog food.

So she ran a background check and posted it on TikTok as a warning, calling him "The HNL Swindler" in a nod to Netflix's "The Tinder Swindler." It went viral, and her inbox filled up.

One viewer was Irvine, CA dentist Dr. Monique Sison-Aweau. She ran downstairs at 6 a.m. to show her husband, Jamison. According to the couple, Vu had applied to be their office manager in March 2025. After a half-day working interview, they paid him $200 by check. He refused a background check, his credentials didn't pan out, and the offer was withdrawn. Then about $18,000 in charges they hadn't made hit the practice's account. The couple says they learned he allegedly used the routing and account numbers from that $200 check to pay an American Express card.

Court records show the Orange County DA charged Vu with identity theft and grand theft in April, and list him as a fugitive with warrants out.

In Honolulu, Dr. Kyrell Wright hired Vu as office manager in Kaimukī in May 2025. Wright and operations manager Donni Ching allege Vu offered patients cash discounts, pocketed the cash, and scrubbed the procedures from records. They also allege he had patients who paid by check leave the payee line blank ("we have an ink stamp"), then wrote in his own name. They say it came out when patients got bills for procedures they'd already paid for. Ching says Vu was fired in October 2025. Wright estimates the losses at no less than $80,000 and filed a police report. A medical office also reported him to police over a laptop it says he never returned, and a surgical center says it was targeted too.

Vu's side: he told Civil Beat the story is "completely wrong." He says he doesn't know either dentist, never worked for Wright, and paid Bird back. He also says the California case involves a different, much older man with the same name, though Civil Beat reports that the defendant's birth year matches his.

No Hawaii theft or fraud charges have been reported. HPD says it can "neither confirm nor deny" an investigation.

Investigator lesson: never let a check leave your office with the payee line blank. Not even for an "ink stamp."
4/4

text:
Revitalizing rural America isn’t a partisan issue—it’s about delivering results for our communities. Rural communities deserve a seat at the table, and we’re working in a bipartisan fashion with @RepThompson to deliver the resources and opportunities they need to succeed.

From expanding access to rural health care and affordable housing to strengthening our workforce, supporting farmers, and cutting red tape, the Revitalize Rural America Act offers practical, bipartisan solutions to help rural communities thrive.

Thank you to the National Association of Rural Health Clinics, the California Cattlemen’s Association, and Sonoma county, Clearlake, Woodland, Colusa county, and St. Helena for endorsing and supporting our efforts.

text:
Los Angeles, CA – International Day of Peace Guest Speaking Strengthens Ties (September 21, 2026)

UPF Southern California participated in an International Day of Peace celebration organized by the Church of Scientology on September 21, building on its longstanding relationship with Scientology communities in Pasadena, Los Angeles, and Burbank. The program featured Ambassador Namboka Omosit Ireneo, a former diplomat and retired UN Human Rights Advisor, who shared insights from his work exploring traditional African family and tribal systems and the lessons these models may offer for addressing challenges facing families today. Nasser Zomorod, UPF Director of Southern California, was also invited to offer spontaneous remarks on behalf of UPF, highlighting the shared commitment to peace and human dignity. The gathering provided a valuable opportunity to reconnect with several Ambassadors for Peace, including Mary Shuttleworth, who warmly reaffirmed her pride in receiving the appointment more than a decade ago. Through meaningful exchanges and renewed personal connections, the event strengthened interorganizational relationships and encouraged continued dialogue on peace, family values, and shared responsibility for building a more harmonious society. This participation reflects the Peace Starts With Me Alliance’s commitment to fostering interfaith and interorganizational partnership in line with the vision of One Family Under God.

text:
My thoughts on the @Eagles, from a superfan*:

1. I went into this season expecting we were going to win 11 games and likely be a top 3 NFC team. 
2. While Jalen's injury & Lane's departure are key losses, it doesn't really explain away how awful the defense looks. I fully believed @JimmyKempski's reports over the summer and blame him. I kid, I kid. I actually feel like players have regressed or just aren't trying at all. I don't know how you fix that.
3. Has the media talked much how Howie has whiffed on the 2026 picks. Are any of them "good". Even Lemon looks average at best, but its hard to tell with the offensive line being a joke.
4. I'm not for trading "key assets" away. Like talk about trading Jalen Carter needs to stop (unless a team comes flying in with an absurd offer). I am for trading some players for a soft reset but I think our "core" is good. 
5. I'm not firing Nick after this season.
6. It's hard to even judge Sean Mannion as an OC with the offensive line being so dysfunctional and the injuries. Right now I'd actually not fire him. I don't think he's the cause of our issues, especially on defense.
7. I think we need 2026 to play out before speculating on drafting a QB versus keeping Hurts (he's under contract and has a no trade clause). I'm a fan of Jalen. I want to keep him and build around him. If we had a top 10 pick is there a Lane Johnson future Pro Bowl RT waiting there? Boom, lets go. That would be my step 1.
8. The key right now is the following question we need to ask and this goes back to my #4 statement. Is the core good? If Howie doesn't believe the core is good then blow up the team and try again. If the front office does believe the core is good, then we should be thinking about a soft reset with the Eagles coming back after 2028 (and maybe without Jalen at that point).

*if you have been running an @Eagles fan club for 20+ years you can call yourself a superfan.

text:
Wade Wilson murdered two women in a single day, one of them with the car he stole from the first. The internet took one look at his face and fell for him:

Thousands of women watched his trial, the tattoos, the pale eyes, the dead calm, and decided they were in love. He was flooded with letters, money and marriage proposals, and half the internet started calling a double murderer its “husband.”

What he actually did in October 2019 wipes the smile off fast. In one single afternoon he beat and strangled Christine Melton in her own home and took her car. Then he spotted Diane Ruiz walking to work, offered her a ride, strangled her, and when she tried to run he drove over her, crushing her spine, her ribs and her neck.

He confessed to both murders in full, without a flicker of remorse.

In the video below he walks into a Florida courtroom to be sentenced and sits almost bored while the judge reads out, step by step, exactly how both women died.

The jury recommended death. The judge handed him two death sentences, one for each woman, and ordered that he never contact either family again.

A man did all of this, and strangers online still fight over who loves him more. The scariest part of this story might not even be him.

text:
Just do a little at a time. You'll feel better because you're prepping and he won't even know because it won't disrupt his life at all 😂🤣😂

Nobody took me seriously either when I started prepping for a nuclear fallout disaster. And then ... Covid. My BIL worked at a state mental facility and he was the only one with n95s early on. Doctors were trying to pay him $50 a mask for his used masks. We did not accept that offer because they were not thinking clearly.

My BIL wanted to give them away and I told him no. I'm not out here stocking for the world. I'm out here stocking for my family. You might want to stock extra for extended family and friends. That's up to you.

I've been low-key prepping *thinks* since Daniel Pearl was killed. I thought about it after 9/11 but it was after Daniel Pearl that I really started making an effort. I edit my go-bag twice a year, switching out from warm weather to cold weather and vice versa and making sure everything is still charged and still good. Which reminds me I need to get some survival blankets because I use them on my garden 😂 I'm also going to be looking at some Faraday bags. I had considered them before because I have an old Kindle with a lot of survival information on it but it has to survive an EMP pulse and I'm not sure it will even if it's off.

I would say 15 years ago, I started prepping my car too. There was a blizzard and a lot of people got caught in it and that really got my attention. I drove a lot so I thought there was a better than average chance that if something happened, I'd be in my car. I have extra water,  medical supplies, a gas mask with some extra filters, survival blankets, etc in my car too. 

Living in Florida and seeing the aftermath of hurricanes really helped me to focus on what's important. It's a completely different mindset than living in Texas and prepping for tornadoes and wind/fire events. I hope to never hear a hurricane again but it gave me invaluable information.

TBH, Even though I'm pretty sure we could stay in our house for 6 weeks without ever having to leave ... I still don't feel like I'm ready for Day Zero and hopefully we'll never have to find out 🤗🙏🏼

text:
#Malfoid #HarryPotter #fanfiction

Year 4

Chapter 14
---

Lunch in the Great Hall was a bit tense.

Lyra sat at the Gryffindor table beside Harry, posture perfect, chin lifted, as imperious as a queen surveying disputed territory. The usual noise of the hall had not quite resumed around them. Seamus Finnegan, by sheer dint of Irish nerve, was the first to break the silence.

“Uh… Harry? The hell is the Ferret doing here?”

“She’s—”

“We’re courting, Finnegan, you obnoxious Paddy.”

Silence fell. Seamus gaped. Several heads turned. Harry’s scowl arrived immediately.

“Lyra. Apologize.”

She pouted. “Harry!”

He held the look. She grumbled, shoulders tight, then muttered, “Sorry.”

Seamus recovered enough to stare. “…Seriously. Paddy? That’s the worst slur you can use against me? I could think up a dozen others!”

“And that’s why we’re failing our joint project in History of Magic." Dean said from beside him.

“We’re not failing it! You don’t know what you’re talking about for the last Goblin Rebellion and your logo for it is rubbish!”

“My logo is amazing!”

“It’s not amazing enough!”

They fell into their usual argument. Lyra watched them for a moment, then turned a skeptical look on Harry.

“This is why I usually don’t apologize. It’s never appreciated.”

He smirked, small. “I guess so… still…”

Across the table, Hermione remained in a foul mood, stirring her soup without interest. Ron sat on Harry’s other side, eating slowly and glancing between his plate and the Slytherin table as if Daphne might appear at any moment. The twins watched the entire arrangement with open fascination. Ginny, beside Hermione, looked as though she were conducting an intense internal argument and losing.

Lyra’s voice dropped. “…Please tell me I don’t have to apologize to all of them?”

“…Just Hermione, please.”

She sighed. “Granger, I do apologize for calling you a slur.”

Hermione’s answer was a low grumble. “Accepted.”

Lyra scowled. “That’s it?”

“It’s fine! It’s accepted!”

“Don’t worry, Malfoy,” George said. “It’s not you she’s cross with.”

“Definitely,” Fred added.

Lyra nodded, understanding. “Ah. Weasley, you should just be honest with your feelings.”

“I—I don’t know what you’re talking about!” Ron said, ears red.

Ginny made a strangled sound. She looked at Harry, turned bright red, and put her elbow directly into the butter dish. “I’m so sorry I need to clean this!” She was on her feet and gone before anyone could answer.

Fred watched her go, then turned back to Harry with a grin. “Right. Harry? You’re doing great.”

“Couldn’t be doing better!” George said.

“And honestly, much better choice than Chang.”

“In all areas.”

Lyra smirked. 

"That's true," she preened.

Harry sighed. “You're making things worse.”

“Or better,” Lyra said, and reached, carefully, for the nearest platter, unbothered by the situation.

Hermione’s glare swung toward the twins. “Maybe you two should mind your own business?”

“Well, you’re making it our business,” Fred said.

“Seriously,” George added. “You three save the school every year.”

“If you break up, we’re doomed.”

“Finished.”

“Kaput.”

“Harry Potter and the year we all die.”

“Hey!” Ron protested. “We helped too!”

“He gets top billing,” Fred said.

“On account of bouncing the Killing Curse off his skull,” George finished.

“Indeed, Weasley.” Lyra’s tone was cool. “Know your role.” She shifted closer on the bench until her shoulder rested lightly against Harry’s. He tensed, then managed a wry smile as she smirked up at him.

Ron scowled, opened his mouth to retort, but Hermione interrupted with a sound of pure exasperation. “Ugh. You two talked to Dumbledore, right? What did he say?”

“That Moody’s on the case and securing things,” Ron said.

“Well, I do feel a little better.” Her glare returned to him. “A little.”

“Seriously, you said you didn’t care about Daphne!”

“I don’t!”

“So why are you so mad?”

“I’m not!”

George’s eyes flicked past them. “Speaking of…”

“Greengrass ahoy,” Fred said.

Daphne approached the table and stopped a few feet from Ron. He gulped, turned, and offered a nervous smile.

“Ah… hey, Daphne! What’s up?”

She regarded him for a moment, expression unreadable. “…Hmph.” Then she lifted her nose and walked out of the Great Hall without another word. Ron’s jaw dropped. He watched her go, then spun back to the table.

“Wha…? Is she mad at me too?!”

“I’m not mad, Ron!” Hermione snapped.

“Oh no… she is!” He was on his feet and moving. “Daphne, wait!”

Hermione’s eyes widened. She shoved back from the table. “No, Ron! Stop!” She hurried after him.

Harry watched them disappear through the doors. “…It’s a trap, isn’t it?”

“My, you can learn, can’t you?” Lyra’s smirk was small and satisfied. “I didn’t think she had it in her.”

“Clearly she’s changed tactics,” George said.

“Poor Ronnie-kins.” Fred shook his head. “Never knew he’d have two girls after him.”

“But we’re truly proud of him.”

Harry got up and headed after them. Lyra frowned, rose and followed.

“Harry, wait!”

Dobby popped into existence at the Head Table, two woolen swords clutched in his hands. The blades were knitted, complete with visible stitches, and they refused to collapse into anything sock-like.

“Headmastery Dumbledore,” he announced, “Dobby cannot make these socks stop being swords!”

“Oh, they’re under a charm.” Dumbledore considered them with mild interest. “They only revert to sock form when you have a smashing play sword fight.”

Dobby nodded, ears quivering. “Dobby understands. This is part of job?”

“Yes!”

Dobby tossed the second sword to him, then pointed his own with solemn determination. “Guard on!”

Dumbledore’s eyes twinkled. He rose, and the two of them stepped down from the dais into the central aisle of the Great Hall. The first clash of wool against wool was soft and ridiculous. Students turned. Laughter started in scattered pockets and spread.

What followed was less a duel than a traveling farce. Dumbledore advanced with exaggerated form, wool blade sweeping in wide, theatrical arcs. Dobby darted beneath them, rolled, and came up swinging with both hands. They fenced the length of the aisle—Dumbledore parrying with grave dignity, Dobby countering with frantic enthusiasm—while the hall filled with cheers and laughter. At the Ravenclaw table someone began keeping score. At the Hufflepuff table a group started chanting Dobby’s name.

Dobby leaped. He cleared Dumbledore’s head in a single bound, landed on the far side, and struck. Dumbledore spun to meet him. The wool blades met again with a soft thump.

At the Head Table, McGonagall sighed with the fond exasperation of long practice. Hagrid was on his feet, booming encouragement. Several other professors had produced small purses and were conducting quiet, serious negotiations about the outcome.

“Albus, really!” McGonagall called.

“Now now, Minerva.” Dumbledore blocked a wild overhead swing and smiled. “I’m merely demonstrating Contextual Ritualistic Constraint Charms! They are among the most difficult but fascinating spells of Transfiguration!”

“You’re just messing about!”

“I can do multiple things at once!” He swept his blade in a low arc. Dobby jumped it cleanly, landed on the hilt, and drove his own wool sword into Dumbledore’s chest. Dumbledore gasped, staggered, and fell backward onto the stone with operatic commitment. 

“Oh no… no! You’ve got me… everything’s… going dark… must… talk like this…”

“Dobby now Headmaster! Dobby now rule!” Dobby’s triumph lasted half a second. His eyes went wide. “Wait! That mean Dobby get paid more! Dobby regrets everything!” He fell to his knees and sobbed. “Noooooooo!”

The hall erupted. Fred and George were laughing openly. Students stood on benches to see better as the two combatants rose, bowed to each other and to the crowd, and accepted the applause: Dumbledore with exaggerated gravity, Dobby with loud, happy tears.

The wool swords, having completed their dramatic duty, collapsed at last into a pair of slightly rumpled socks. Dobby collected them with care. Dumbledore returned to the Head Table, still smiling, and McGonagall’s sigh was only mostly exasperated.

Fred wiped his eyes. “Honestly, George… I feel like we need to up the ante a bit. We’re being shown up by the Headmaster and an elf.”

“Oh, don’t worry, brother of mine.” George’s gaze turned particularly mischievous. “I have just the ticket. And it’s in the form of Harry and his new girlfriend.”

text:
Rogan and Tyrrell trade political fatigue for wilderness and comedy

The conversation connects distrust in institutions and media with the restorative pull of nature, while testing what responsibility means in politics, consumption, and entertainment.

Colum Tyrrell and Joe Rogan begin with gambling, drinking, Irish culture, and personal responsibility, then widen the argument to regulation, addiction, and the limits of a nanny state.

Their distrust of media and pharmaceutical advertising grows into a broader critique of algorithmic manipulation, surveillance, political spectacle, and the public exhaustion produced by constant controversy.

The conversation changes register in the wilderness: Bigfoot, bears, solo hiking, dark skies, birding, hunting ethics, and conservation offer direct encounters with risk, food, and the natural world.

Tyrrell and Rogan also examine how online exposure to violence can blunt empathy, contrasting graphic digital culture with the humbling perspective of stars, wildlife, and mortality.

The final turn returns to stand-up, where improvisation, uncertainty, and shared laughter provide a grounded alternative to political performance; Tyrrell discusses and promotes Bells and Whistles.

👀 Don't miss: The episode’s most vivid shift comes when Big Bend’s dark sky, tarantulas, and Saturn through a telescope replace political noise with cosmic perspective.

Former Ohio high school principal Robert "Rob" Burnside resigned from Lakota East High School in late 2024 after allowing homeless student Landerius "DeDe" Hayes to continue attending classes despite district residency rules...

In 2024, Rob Burnside, the principal of Lakota East High School in Ohio, discovered that 16-year-old student Landerius “DeDe” Hayes was experiencing severe homelessness, often sleeping in a cold car. When DeDe’s mother moved out of the school district, district rules dictated that he no longer had a qualifying address to remain enrolled. Refusing to turn his back on the teenager, Burnside spoke with his wife, Angel, and with his mother's blessing, the couple offered DeDe a place to live in their home.

When the school administration discovered that Burnside allowed DeDe to continue attending classes despite being technically withdrawn, the district launched an investigation and put Burnside on leave, ultimately forcing him to step down after 31 years in education. Even when DeDe selflessly offered to move out so his principal wouldn't lose his livelihood, Burnside refused, assuring him that he was part of the family. The Burnsides officially became DeDe’s legal guardians, giving him the stability, safety, and support he needed.

In May 2026, DeDe successfully graduated from high school with Rob and Angel cheering him on from the stands as his parents. Though the professional fallout left Burnside unable to secure another principal position in the area, he has repeatedly stated that he harbors zero regrets. DeDe is now pursuing a career as an aviation mechanic, turning a story of bureaucratic hardship into a powerful testament of unconditional support and family.

Before Rob Burnside and his wife, Angel, ever proposed taking him in, 16-year-old DeDe Hayes was quietly surviving his homelessness by washing his clothes in school sinks, finishing homework on his phone when his laptop battery died, and occasionally sleeping in a cold car with the heater running.

text:
We bought tickets to a horror movie and spent the next ninety minutes learning more about beavers than any human being should know.

It was my brother’s idea to take our dad out for his birthday. Dad loves scary movies, even though he announces every jump scare five seconds before it happens. He says the music gives everything away. My brother, Nate, wanted a quiet evening with the three of us because Dad had been working overtime and hadn’t taken a day off in weeks.

We arrived ten minutes early, bought popcorn, and found seats in a nearly empty theater. There were two teenagers in the back, an older couple near the aisle, and a woman wearing a bright red coat who had brought a notebook.

The lights went down. Instead of the trailer for the new slasher movie, the screen filled with a river and the words NORTH AMERICAN WETLAND ENGINEERS.

Dad leaned over. “Long trailer.”

After eight minutes of footage showing a beaver dragging branches through mud, Nate went to find an employee. He returned with a manager who explained that the horror movie had been moved to another auditorium because its projector was malfunctioning. Somehow the ticketing system hadn’t changed. This room had been booked for a wildlife-documentary screening.

The woman in red looked up from her notebook. “I bought a ticket for this.”

The manager offered to move the rest of us to the other theater, where the movie had already started, or refund our tickets. Dad asked what time the next showing was. Not until ten.

“We can leave,” Nate said.

Dad looked at the screen. A beaver was struggling to carry an impossibly long branch around a tree.

“Let’s give it five minutes,” he said.

The documentary turned out to be genuinely interesting. It followed a wildlife biologist trying to restore a damaged creek by encouraging beavers to return. Every time the animals built a dam, a nearby landowner complained about flooding. The biologist kept moving barriers, negotiating with property owners, and getting absolutely humiliated by the beavers, who rearranged everything overnight.

Dad started cheering for them.

“Look at that little guy. He’s unionized.”

The older couple laughed. The woman in red explained during a particularly confusing section that beaver dams can improve wetland habitat but can also create real problems for nearby roads. She was a local science teacher taking notes for a lesson.

By the end, Nate had stopped checking his watch. Dad had finished everybody’s popcorn. The two teenagers applauded when the final dam survived a storm.

When we came out, the manager was waiting with refund vouchers. We accepted them. Nate asked Dad if he was disappointed about missing the horror movie.

“Are you kidding? That one had suspense. You never knew what those beavers were going to do.”

On the drive home, Dad made Nate look up whether beavers really have orange teeth. He spent the rest of the ride explaining their dental chemistry to us with the confidence of a newly credentialed expert.

We still owe him a birthday horror movie.

But yesterday he texted our group chat a link to another wildlife documentary and wrote, “Sequel?”

Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide said the government has no role in the Peace Prize and that Trump knows the Nobel committee is independent.

text:
🇺🇦🇷🇺 ZELENSKYY'S INTERVIEW REVEALS WHAT FIVE YEARS OF PUTIN'S WAR HAVE DONE TO HIM 💔

There is a moment in Volodymyr Zelenskyy's interview with Steven Bartlett that is difficult to forget.

Asked how he is doing, the Ukrainian president explains that he barely sleeps. His nights are spent following military communications, making decisions about air defences and trying to determine which Ukrainian cities can be protected with the limited systems available.

Nearly five years into Russia's full-scale invasion, even sleep has become something he cannot take for granted.

But the most painful moments come when he talks about the people he has lost.

He describes presenting posthumous awards to the families of fallen Ukrainian soldiers. A father approaches to receive his son's decoration, shakes the president's hand and quietly asks whether they can embrace.

Zelenskyy says these encounters leave him emotionally devastated. He knows that nothing he says, no medal he presents and no embrace he offers can bring those families back to the lives they had before.

He also recalls the horror of children killed by Russian missiles, including an attack on a playground, and the discovery of murdered civilians in Bucha after Russian forces withdrew.

These experiences help explain his frustration with demands that Ukraine simply accept a quick peace agreement.

How do you tell families who have buried their children that they must surrender more territory to the country responsible for invading their homeland? And what guarantee would prevent another invasion after the fighting stops?

At one point, Bartlett shows him photographs from his earlier life: Kryvyi Rih, comedy performances, his work voicing Paddington Bear and his television career in Servant of the People.

The contrast is extraordinary. Before becoming a wartime president, Zelenskyy was an entertainer whose work was built around making people laugh. Now his daily responsibilities involve missile interceptions, destroyed cities, military casualties and families waiting for news of missing relatives.

The interview also exposes the enormous distance between Ukraine's wartime reality and the political calculations of its allies.

While Ukrainian cities endure Russian attacks on their energy infrastructure, Zelenskyy faces American pressure over Ukrainian strikes against Russian oil facilities and their potential impact on fuel prices.

For Washington, energy costs are a political issue. For Kyiv, striking infrastructure connected to Russia's war effort is part of a struggle for survival.

Zelenskyy can be criticized, questioned and held accountable for his decisions. Wartime leadership does not place anyone beyond scrutiny.

But this interview offers something that political arguments often overlook: a glimpse of the human being carrying those responsibilities.

Watch the interview. Especially the moments when he talks about the families of fallen soldiers.

Those are the moments that stay with you.

text:
As Russia's war against Ukraine continues, questions are mounting about Europe's security, America's relationship with Moscow, and Ukraine's ability to withstand another winter of Russian attacks.  

@yarotrof, Chief Foreign-Affairs Correspondent at The @WSJ and author of Our Enemies Will Vanish: The Russian Invasion and Ukraine's War of Independence, joins @Garymarx  on Peace & Power to discuss the latest developments in the war, the changing relationship between the United States and Europe, and the challenges of reporting from the world's most dangerous conflict zones.  

A Pulitzer Prize finalist for his reporting on Ukraine, Trofimov reflects on his experiences covering the first year and a half of Russia's full-scale invasion. He shares firsthand accounts of Ukraine's defense of Kyiv, the liberation of occupied territories, and how the growing use of drones has transformed the battlefield and made frontline journalism increasingly dangerous.  

The conversation then turns to Europe's nuclear security and France's efforts to expand its nuclear deterrence cooperation with European allies. Trofimov explains how uncertainty surrounding America's nuclear commitments has encouraged European governments to reconsider their security arrangements and strengthen their defenses against Russian threats.  

Gary and Yaroslav also examine growing criticism of President Donald Trump's approach to Vladimir Putin, including concerns about a reported U.S.–Russia diesel arrangement and the potential consequences for Ukraine. They discuss congressional opposition, the upcoming midterm elections, and whether Washington's evolving relationship with Moscow could weaken American leverage in future peace negotiations.  Trofimov addresses reported restrictions affecting Starshield satellite services used by Ukrainian forces, explaining how limitations on connectivity could disrupt drone operations and complicate Ukraine's military efforts.  

The discussion also explores the Warsaw Security Forum, Europe's increasingly important role in supporting Ukraine, and the prospects for renewed negotiations involving Washington, Moscow, and Kyiv.  As Ukraine prepares for another winter of attacks against its energy infrastructure, Trofimov examines shortages of air-defense interceptors and the difficult choices facing Ukrainian military planners.  

Finally, he reflects on his childhood, his path into international journalism, and how his reporting across Ukraine and the Middle East has shaped his understanding of the increasingly interconnected conflicts involving Russia, China, Iran, and North Korea. text:
A man receives a pancreatic cancer diagnosis. The odds are devastating. His doctors know what usually comes next. Yet somehow, through sheer determination and an extraordinary fight for survival, he lives nearly twenty more years.

Twenty years. Time to live, to fight, to watch the world change. Time the diagnosis suggested he would never have.

There's a brutal political lesson buried in that story.

The Republican Party is a cancer eating away at the American Republic. A festering collection of spineless careerists, establishment parasites, and self-serving cowards who campaign on saving the Constitution before scurrying back to Washington to protect their precious committee assignments and cocktail-party invitations.

They've squandered opportunities, betrayed their voters, and demonstrated an almost supernatural ability to turn political power into absolutely fucking nothing.

But cancer, however devastating, can sometimes be fought. Diseased tissue can be removed. Recovery remains possible.

Death offers no such opportunity.

And that is the terrifying distinction when considering the Democrats' ambitions to abolish the Electoral College, expand the Supreme Court, add states, and fundamentally alter the institutions that restrain political power.

Imagine those changes surviving long after the politicians responsible have disappeared. Imagine constitutional safeguards weakened so thoroughly that future elections offer increasingly fewer opportunities to reverse the damage.

That's the nightmare. A political establishment so obsessed with securing its own power that the machinery of government becomes increasingly difficult for ordinary Americans to challenge.

And standing between that possibility and the American people are Republican leaders who seem more frightened of violating Senate etiquette than losing the Republic itself.

What an absolutely disgraceful collection of bastards.

The cancer infecting the GOP demands a ruthless political housecleaning. Replace the cowards. Drive out the opportunists. Rebuild what decades of establishment betrayal have hollowed out.

Because survival buys something precious: another day to fight, another opportunity to repair what has been damaged, another chance to preserve what previous generations entrusted to us.

That dying man fought for nearly twenty additional years.

The least America's elected defenders can do is stop pissing away the Republic's remaining chances to recover.

text:
🔄 BREAKINGPOCKET UPDATE: Oil slips toward $100 as peace-talk hopes trim the war premium

Oil gave back more of Wednesday's gains on Thursday as diplomacy, not supply, set the price.

By late morning in New York (11:45 AM EDT):
• Brent crude was down $1.59, or 1.4%, at $113.73 a barrel
• US West Texas Intermediate was down $2.09, or 2.0%, at $100.69 — within sight of the $100 line
• That follows an Asian session where Brent fell about 1% to around $114 and WTI about 1.3% to $101.45, so the slide extended through the day

What is driving it:
• US Vice President JD Vance sought to revive peace negotiations by sending a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing US officials and people familiar with the matter
• Qatari mediators have presented Iran with a new draft deal to end the war, an official briefed on the talks said — but a senior Iranian official dismissed it as unacceptable ideas that did not amount to an offer
• Holding a floor under prices: Houthi attacks continued — the Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed a ballistic missile fired toward Saudi Arabia's eastern region early Thursday — and traders still fear a possible US attack on Iran after the November 3 midterms

MARKET IMPACT: Energy was the drag on Canada's TSX through midday, while the cheaper crude took a little inflation pressure off rate-sensitive stocks on both sides of the border.

WHY IT MATTERS: Oil near $115 has been the single biggest force keeping inflation — and central-bank rate-hike bets — alive this month. Every dollar it falls eases gasoline and shipping costs, and weakens the case for the December hikes markets are pricing in the US and Canada.

👀 WATCH: whether WTI closes below $100, any Iranian response to the Qatari draft, and the OPEC+ meeting on November 1.

Source: Reuters (Houston update, prices at 11:45 AM EDT; Asian session report); Wall Street Journal reporting on the Vance letter, via Reuters; Canadian Press market report (December crude down $2.52 at $100.26).

text:
Twenty-second Sunday After Pentecost: Goffine's Devout Instructions On the Epistles and Gospels by Leonard Goffine,  1871.
.
At the Introit of the Mass pray with the priest for the forgiveness of your sins: If thou shalt observe iniquities O Lord: Lord, who shall endure? for with Thee is propitiation, O God of Israel. From the depths I have cried to Thee, O Lord: Lord, hear my voice.
(Ps. CXXIX.) Glory etc.
.
Collect.
.
O God, our refuge and strength, who art the author of all goodness, hear, we beseech Thee, the devout prayers of Thy Church, and grant that what we faithfully ask we may effectually obtain. Through...
.
Epistle (Philipp. I. 6-II.)
.
Brethren, We are confident in the Lord Jesus, that He who hath begun a good work in you will perfect it unto the day of Christ Jesus. As it is meet for me to think this for you all, for that I have you in my heart, and that in my hands, and in the defense and confirmation of the gospel, you are all partakers of my joy. For God is my witness, how I long after you all in the bowels of Jesus Christ.
And this I pray, that your charity may more and more abound in knowledge and in all understanding: that you may approve the better things; that you may be sincere and without offence unto the day of Christ, filled with the fruit of justice, through Jesus Christ,  unto the glory and praise of God.
.
Explanation.
.
This epistle was written by St. Paul at Rome, where he was
imprisoned for the faith, to the inhabitants of Philippi in Macedonia whom he had converted to the true faith. He congratulates them that they so willingly received and conscientiously obeyed the gospel which he had preached to them, and he says, he trusts in God to complete the good work which He has commenced, and to give them perseverance until the day of Christ, that is, until death.
Twenty-second Sunday After Pentecost GOSPEL (Matt. XXII. 15-21.) At that time, the Pharisees went and consulted among themselves how to ensnare Jesus in his speech. And they send to Him their disciples, with the Herodians, saying: Master, we know that Thou art a true speaker, and teachest the way of God in truth, neither carest
Thou for any man, for Thou dost not regard the person of men: tell us, therefore, what dost Thou think? Is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar or not? But Jesus knowing their wickedness, said: Why do you tempt me, ye hypocrites? Show me the coin of the tribute. And they offered him a penny. And Jesus saith to them: Whose image and inscription is this? They say to him: Caesar’s. Then he saith to them: Render therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.
.
Why did the Pharisees try to ensnare Jesus in His speech?
.
In order to find some reason to accuse Him before the emperor, or to make Him hated by the Jews; for had He denied tribute to Caesar, they would have accused Him before the emperor as guilty of high treason; had He, on the contrary made it obligatory to
pay tribute, then they would have denounced Him as a destroyer of the liberty of the people, who considered themselves a free nation owing allegiance only to God. Like the Pharisees are all those who, under the appearance of friendship, only cause vexation and misfortune to their neighbour.
.
Who are really hypocrites?
.
Those who in order to cheat their neighbour, appear outwardly pious and holy, whilst inward they are full of malice; those who have honey on the tongue, but gall in the heart, and sting like scorpions, when we least expect it. Because there are so many
vices connected with hypocrisy, (Matt. XXIII.) therefore Christ has denounced no sin more emphatically than this one. Hypocrites are brethren of Cain, Joab, and Judas, of whom the first killed his brother, the second his cousin and the third betrayed his divine Master with a kiss. Such false men are cursed by God. (Mal, I. 14.) I hate a mouth with a double tongue. (Prov. VIII. 13.) “The devil silently possesses the hearts of hypocrites and quietly sleeps in them, whilst he gives them no peace,” says St. Gregory; and St. Jerome writes: “Pretended holiness is double malice.” Better is an
open enemy, before whom we can be on our guard, than a hypocritical friend of whom we have no suspicion, because we look upon him as a friend. Beware, therefore, my dear Christian, of the vice of hypocrisy, which is so hateful to God; endeavour always
to be sincere with God, thyself and thy neighbour, and to walk in true humility before God, then mayst thou carry His image within thee.
.
Prayer.
.
Help me, O Lord, for the number of the saints is decreasing and truth is becoming rare among men. They speak vain things each with his neighbour: their lips are deceitful, and they speak with double hearts. Let the Lord destroy all those who say: We will magnify our tongue; our lips are our own; who is Lord over us? O Lord, deliver my soul from wicked lips and deceitful tongues give me grace to preserve Thy image in my soul, by piety and virtue. Direct my heart to justice and keep it from avarice, that I may give to each his own.
.
INSTRUCTION ON THE FOLLY OF HUMAN RESPECT.
.
Thou art a true speaker neither carest Thou or any man, for Thou dost not regard the person of men. (Matt. XXII. 16.)
.
In this Christians ought especially to follow the Saviour, and not permit themselves to be deterred from piety, and the practice of virtue by fear or human respect. What matters it, what people think and say of us, if we only please God? He alone can truly benefit or injure us; therefore, He alone is to be feared, as Christ says: Fear ye not them that kill the body, and are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear Him that can destroy both soul and body in hell. (Matt. X. 28.)
.
How foolishly, therefore, do those act who through fear of displeasing certain people, are afraid to serve God and practice piety; who even go so far as to commit sin; who in order to be pleasing to others, oppress innocent, poor and forsaken people; who adopt the latest and most scandalous fashions and customs; those who eat meat on days of abstinence, or give it to others; those who sing sinful songs, or what is still worse, do not hesitate to ridicule sacred things to give others occasion to laugh, or in
order to be considered strong-minded. Implore God daily and sincerely, that He may take from you this vain fear of men and give you instead the fear of the Lord, which is the beginning of wisdom.
.
INSTRUCTION ON THE VALUE AND DIGNITY OF THE SOUL.
.
Whose image is this? (Matt. XXII. 20.)
.
Thus we should often ask ourselves with respect to our soul, particularly when we are tempted to stain and ruin it by sin, Whose image is this? We should then say to ourselves, “Is it not the likeness of God, a likeness painted with the blood of Jesus, an image for which the Saviour gave His life? Should I defile and deform this by sin and voluptuousness? God forbid!” For in truth, what among all created things, except the angels, is more beautiful and more precious than a human soul, which is in the state of grace? “Could we,” says St. Catherine of Sienna, “behold with our corporal eyes a soul in the state of grace, we would see with astonishment that it surpasses in splendour all flowers, all stars, the whole world, and there is probably no one who would not wish to die for such beauty.” It is a dwelling of the Blessed Trinity! Christ
did not give His life for all the goods and treasures of this earth, but for the human soul. And yet many estimate their soul at such little value that they sell it for a momentary pleasure, for a present not worth a penny! For shame! The body we estimate so highly that we take all pains to decorate it and keep it alive, and the soul the image and likeness of God, we take no pains to keep in the state of grace, and adorn with virtues! What folly!
.
INSTRUCTION ON THE OBLIGATION TO PAY TAXES OR TRIBUTE TO
THE GOVERNMENT.
.
Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.
(Matt. XXII. 21.)
.
To pay tribute to the lawful government is a duty of justice which the Spirit of God Himself commands us faithfully to fulfilll. (Rom. XIII. 6, 7.) Christ Himself paid the customary didrachma for Himself and St. Peter; (Matt. XVII. 23.) “and if the Son of God Himself paid duty and tax,” says St. Ambrose, “who art thou, O man, that thou
wouldst free thyself from it?” The government must watch lest the life of its subjects be at hazard, that their property be not endangered or stolen, that there be security on the highways, that peace, harmony and order be preserved among the citizens, that
their temporal welfare be promoted; that science and art flourish, etc. For this, teachers, judges, officers and soldiers are necessary, for whose support care must be taken, and whose trouble must be rewarded. Besides this the government must care for the security of the country, for public streets and bridges, and institutions necessary for the common good; to enable the government to perform these duties, taxes are necessary and lawfully assessed. If you oppose these laws, you oppose God, for by Him princes rule, and the mighty degree justice. (Prov. VIII. 16.) Let the payment of duties be done willingly, because you pay them for love of God, and resigned to His holy will as the early Christians did, who even served their heathenish government with pleasure, in all that was not contrary to God’s will, and cheerfully paid the duties.
.
TWENTY-THIRD SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST REMARK
.
If from Pentecost until Advent there be only twenty-three Sundays, the following one is omitted, and the Mass of the twenty-fourth is said.
.
The Introit of the Mass consoles and incites us to confidence in God who is so benevolent towards us, and will not let us pine away in tribulation. The Lord saith: I think thoughts of peace, and not of affliction: you shall call upon Me, and I will hear you: and I will bring back your captivity from all places. (Fer. XXIX. 11. 12. 14.) Lord, thou hast blessed Thy land: Thou hast turned away the captivity of Jacob. (Ps. LXXXIV.) Glory etc.
.
COLLECT
.
Absolve, we beseech Thee, O Lord, Thy people from their offences: that through Thy bountiful goodness we may be freed from the bonds of those sins which through our frailty we have contracted. Through...
.
EPISTLE (Philipp. III 17-21.: IV, 1-3.)
.
Brethren, Be followers of me, and observe them who walk so as you have our model. For many walk, of whom I have told you often (and now tell you weeping), that they are enemies of the cross of Christ: whose end is destruction, whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things. But our conversation is in heaven: from whence also we look for the Saviour, our Lord Jesus Christ, who will reform the body of our lowness, made like to the body of His glory, according to the operation whereby also He is able to subdue all things unto Himself. Therefore, my dearly beloved brethren, and most desired, my joy and my crown: so stand fast in the Lord, my dearly beloved. I beg of Evodia, and I beseech Syntyche, to be of one mind in the Lord. And I entreat thee
also, my sincere companion, help those women who have laboured with me in the gospel with Clement and the rest of my fellow-labourers, whose names are in the book of life.
.
EXPLANATION
.
There are unhappily many Christians, who, as St. Paul complains,
are, declared enemies of Christ’s cross, who do not wish to mortify their senses, who only think of gratifying their lusts, and, as it were, find their only pleasure, even seek their honour, in despising the followers of Jesus and His saints on the narrow path of the cross, of mortification and humiliation. What will be the end of these people?
.
Eternal perdition! For he who does not crucify the flesh, does not belong to Christ. (Gal. V. 24.) He who does not bear the-marks of the mortification of Jesus in his body, in him the life of Christ shall not be manifested. (II Cor. IV. 10.) He who does not walk in heaven during his, life-time, that is, who does not direct his thoughts and
desires heavenward, and despise the world and its vanities, will not find admission there after his death.
.
ASPIRATION.
.
Would to God, I could say with St. Paul: The world is crucified to
me, and I to the world. (Gal. VI. 14.)
.
Twenty-third Sunday After Pentecost GOSPEL (Matt. IX. 18-26.)
.
At that time, As Jesus was speaking to the multitudes, behold, a certain ruler came up, and adored Him, saying: Lord, my daughter is even now dead: but come, lay Thy hand upon her, and she shall live. And Jesus, rising up, followed him, with His disciples. And behold, a woman, who was troubled with an issue of blood twelve years, came behind Him, and touched the hem of His garment. For she said within herself: If I shall touch only His garment, I shall be healed. But Jesus turning and seeing her, said: Be of good heart, daughter: thy faith hath made thee whole. And the woman was made whole from that hour. And when Jesus was come into the house of the ruler, and saw the minstrels and the multitude making a tumult, he said: Give place: for the girl is not dead, but sleepeth. And they laughed Him to scorn. And when the multitude was put
forth, He went in, and took her by the hand. And the maid arose. And the fame hereof went abroad into all that country.
.
INSTRUCTIONS.
.
I. Filial was the faith, unbounded the confidence, profound the humility of this woman, and therefore, she received health also. Learn from this, how pleasing to the Lord is faith, confidence and humility; let your prayer always be penetrated by these three virtues, and you will receive whatever you ask.
.
II. The devout Louis de Ponte compares the conduct of this woman to our conduct at holy Communion, and says: Christ wished to remain with us in the most holy Eucharist, clothed with the garment of the sacramental species of bread, that he who receives His sacred flesh and blood, may be freed from evil concupiscence. If you wish to obtain the health of your soul, as did this woman the health of the body, imitate her. Receive the flesh and blood of Jesus with the most profound humility, with the firmest confidence in His power and goodness, and like this woman you too will be made whole.
.
III. Jesus called three dead persons to life, the twelve-year-old daughter of Jairus, ruler of the synagogue, of whom there is mention made in this gospel, the young man at Naim, (Luke VII. 14.) and Lazarus. (John. XI- 43.) By these three dead persons
three classes of sinners may be understood: the maiden signifies those who sin in their youth through weakness and frailty, but touched by the grace of God, perceive their fall and easily rise again through penance; by the young man at Naim those are to be understood who sin repeatedly and in public, these require greater grace, more labour and severer penance; by Lazarus, the public and obdurate habitual sinners are to be understood who can be raised to spiritual life only by extraordinary graces and severe public penance.
.
IV. Christ did not raise the maiden, until the minstrels and noisy multitude were removed, by which He wished to teach us that the conversion of a soul cannot be accomplished in the midst of the noise and turmoil of temporal cares, idle pleasures and associations.
.
INSTRUCTION CONCERNING RIDICULE AND DERISION.
.
And they laughed him to scorn. (Matt IX. 24.)
.
When Jesus told the minstrels and the crowd that the girl was not dead, but sleeping, they laughed at Him, because they understood not the meaning of His words. Sensualminded men generally act in the same manner towards the priests and ministers of God, who by their word and example admonish them to despise honours, riches and pleasures, and to embrace the love of poverty, humility and mortification. This is, an unintelligible and hateful language to them which they ridicule and mock just as they do when they hear that death is a sleep, from which we shall one day awake and be
obliged to appear before the judgment-seat of God. Woe to such scoffers by whose ridicule so many souls are led from the path “of virtue! What the devil formerly, accomplished by tyrants in estranging men from God and a lively faith in Him and His Church, he seems to wish to accomplish in our days by the mockery, scoffs, and blasphemies of wicked men; for at no period have piety and virtue, holy simplicity and childlike faith, adherence to the holy Roman Church and her laws, reverence for her head, her ministers and priests, been more mocked, derided and blasphemed.
.
Unhappily many permit themselves to be induced by mockery to abandon piety, to omit the public practice of their faith, to conceal their Catholic conviction, and to lead a lukewarm, careless, indeed, sinful life. Woe to the scoffers! they are an abomination to the Lord (Prov. III. 32.) who will one day require from their hands all the souls
perverted by them. Do not permit yourself to be led astray by those who ridicule your faith and zeal for virtue; remember the words of Jesus: He that shall deny Me before men, I will also deny him before My Father who is in heaven. (Matt. X. 33.) Let Jesus be your consolation, He was scoffed and blasphemed for your sake, and often say within yourself: I know, my most amiable Jesus, that the servant cannot be more than his master. Since Thou wert so often sneered at, mocked and blasphemed, why should I wonder if I am
derided for my faith in Thee and Thy Church, and for the practice of virtue!

text:
🌹🌙 New Orleans let its most notorious madam spend a fortune on a tomb among its finest families, and then it quietly took her name back off the stone.

She came into the world as Mary Deubler in 1864, a poor New Orleans girl who learned young that nothing would be handed to her. She renamed herself Josie Arlington and made her way on the only terms the city offered a woman in her position. When Storyville opened its doors, hers was among the showiest houses on Basin Street, four floors of mirrors and cut glass beneath a lit cupola that glowed over the district after dark. If your people lived anywhere near Basin Street in those years, they knew that cupola and they knew whose it was.

Rich men from every corner of the city came through that door and left their money in her parlors. Plenty of those same men looked straight past her on the sidewalk at noon, and their wives would not have shared a pew with her for anything. Money she had. The one thing it could not buy her was a seat among them.

So she bought it in granite instead. In 1911 she put her name to a contract for a tomb in Metairie Cemetery, where the old New Orleans fortunes were laid to rest. It was cut from red stone, with flames carved rising out of urns at each corner and tall bronze doors. On the step before those doors stood a bronze young woman with one hand raised, as though she had come to knock. For years people argued over who she was meant to be. Some said a girl once turned away at Josie's own door. Others said Josie herself as a child, shut out of her father's house.

Josie Arlington died on February 14, 1914. In the years after, a red signal light on the road nearby threw its glow against the polished granite, and after dark the whole tomb looked as though it had caught fire. People came out to stand and watch it burn. More than a few swore the bronze girl stepped down and walked the rows once the crowds went home.

Then the tomb changed hands. Her name was cut away from the stone, another family's name was set in its place, and her remains were moved quietly to a spot in that cemetery nobody has ever named publicly. The city got its wish at last, and the madam was no longer resting among the rich.

The tomb is still standing, though. The flames still climb from its corners, and the bronze girl is still at the door with her hand up.

They got her name off the granite. They never did get her out of New Orleans. 🌹 
From Louisiana Unbound

 Located near Leslie Street and Steeles Avenue East, the temple will feature nine asymmetrically arranged panels inspired by the Bahá'í principle of unity in diversity.
 Designed by Vancouver architect James Jing Yi Jiang, the structure will incorporate natural wood tones, open spaces, and a forest-inspired setting intended to create a welcoming environment for prayer and reflection.
 The property has served as a place of prayer and meditation for decades, making the project especially meaningful to the local community.
 The site will also include the Don Valley Education Centre, offering educational programs for families, children, and youth.

text:
#malfoid 4th year.  Yule Ball.  First installment.

Harry leaned against the damp masonry at the top of the Slytherin dungeon stairs, his thumb tracing the stiff wire backing of the comb in his pocket. He checked his watch, found it had only been six minutes since he came down from the Great Hall, and put his hands behind his back.

The sound of heels on stone came from below and around the turn.

Draconia came around the final turn of the stairs. The gown was cut from dark spruce silk, falling in a clean, narrow column straight to the stone flags. The neckline ran straight across her collarbones in a structured band that left her shoulders bare. Modest, but tailored with a sleek, minimalist line that completely skipped the frills and heavy bustles of the older houses and suited her slim form. Her hair was swept up into a smooth French twist, flat against the back of her head, leaving two narrow strands loose to frame her jawline. She stopped on the third riser, her eyes dropping to his hem, then up to the lapels of his black dress robes.

“You’re early,” she said.

“You said not to be late.”

“I said not to leave me waiting on the landing.” She stepped up the last three risers, the hem of the silk whispering against the stone. “This isn’t the landing.”

“I came down to walk you up.” He pulled the comb from his pocket. The blooms were small, dried hellebore and pale green leaves bound to a narrow silver prong. “The clerk at Gladrags said a corsage would sit wrong on a straight neckline. Said this goes in the hair. If you want it.”

She looked at the silver teeth, then at his face. A torch bracket sputtered in the cold draft from the corridor.

“Your robes fit,” she said.

“She had to pin the waist twice.” He held the comb out. “The green works.”

Draconia took it by the silver spine. Her knuckles brushed his palm. She turned the piece over, her thumb testing the tightness of the binding wire, then reached up and slid the prongs deep into the twist above her left ear. The pale green leaves sat flat against the pale blonde hair at her temple.

“It’s acceptable,” she said, smoothing a stray lock back with two fingers. She dropped her hand. “You look less disastrous than usual.”

“Thanks.” Harry bent his elbow, holding his arm out. The sleeve felt thick and strange until she hooked three fingers into the crook of his elbow, her bare wrist resting against his dark cuff. “Ready?”

“The champions are required to form up before the doors open,” she said, already turning him toward the main corridor. “If we are late, it will be noticed.”

They took the low stone steps up toward the ground floor. Her grip remained light on his arm, the light click of her heels steady beside his boots. The torches along the lower walls threw long, narrow shadows across the flagstones ahead of them.

Halfway up she adjusted her hold, shifting her fingers so they rested firmer against the wool of his sleeve. The motion was small. He matched it without comment.

“Why did you really ask me?” she asked, after they passed the portrait of the sleeping monk. “Past the dares and bets. The actual reason.”

Harry kept his chin straight, watching the torchlight flicker on the vaulted ceiling. “Why did you say yes?”

“You first.”

He waited until they reached the middle landing, where the cold dungeon air began to thin out against the warmth of the entrance hall above.

“I know where I stand with you,” he said. “You hate me. I don’t have to spend three hours trying to be someone who impresses you. You already think I’m a reckless idiot, so it doesn’t matter if I step on your feet. It’s simpler.”

Her fingers tightened against the wool of his coat, pressing through to the shirt beneath. They climbed four steps in silence before she spoke.

“I said yes,” she said, her voice level, “so that maybe you wouldn’t know where you stand anymore.”

Harry turned his head. She didn’t look back; her chin was up, her eyes fixed on the archway at the top of the flight where the noise of two hundred voices was already echoing off the marble. The silver comb caught the light as she moved.

“Right,” he said.

They reached the upper corridor. A pair of Ravenclaw fourth-years hurried past them toward the stairs, too absorbed in an argument about seating to look up.

Harry didn't push it, and she offered nothing more. The quiet between them held all the way down the passage, competing only with the muffled brass and the mounting hum of voices drifting from the main hall. Her hand remained light on his arm, but steady, her shoulder tracking an inch from his.

A yard before the corner, where the fairy lights from the landing first spilled across the dark flagstones, she broke the silence.

“The comb doesn’t look cheap,” she said, her voice dropping so only he could hear. “Don’t tell anyone I said so.”

“I won’t.”

“Good. And Potter.” She didn’t look at him. “If your boot touches this hem during the opening waltz, I will hex your shoelaces together before the third measure.”

“I’ll watch the hem.”

They cleared the corner.

The entrance hall opened wide in front of them, flooded with fairy lights and loud with the brass from the Great Hall doors. Cedric Diggory looked up from the base of the stairs, Cho Chang’s hand on his sleeve. His eyebrows rose. Draconia did not blink. Her shoulder brushed Harry’s as they stepped into the crowd, her hand still hooked in the crook of his elbow.

5:20 to 6:21. Mark 7 is offered as the pattern: Paul said "nothing is unclean in itself" (Rom 14:14), and Mark later glued "thus he declared all foods clean" (Mark 7:19) onto a saying of Jesus.

Mark 7:19 is widely taken as Mark's own comment. Adela Yarbro Collins treats it that way in the Hermeneia commentary. A narrator's gloss is not a theft from Romans. Look at the direction of the words. Romans 14:14 says Paul is persuaded "in the Lord Jesus." He attaches the conviction to Jesus, which is the opposite of the video's arrow. And Matthew 15 retells the same dispute and does not contain "all foods are clean." If the evangelists were copying Paul's doctrine into Jesus' mouth, Matthew kept the scene and lost the doctrine. That is a bad copy.

6:26 to 9:31. The video then splits 1 Corinthians 5 from 1 Corinthians 11. In chapter 5 Christ is the Passover lamb and the church is unleavened bread. In chapter 11 the cup proclaims the death. These are called two traditions that the Synoptics illegally fuse, after which John repairs the clock by killing Jesus on the day of Preparation (John 19:14, 31, 36) and moving the flesh and blood to chapter 6.

One letter may use two images of one death. Paul already joins wilderness food, the table, and the body and blood in 1 Corinthians 10, in the same letter as the lamb. The calendar tension is old and real: Mark 14:12 has Jesus eat the Passover, John 13:1 places the supper before it. Raymond Brown, The Death of the Messiah, treats John's timing as theological. Annie Jaubert, The Date of the Last Supper, offered a calendar solution, temple dates against another Jewish reckoning. Pitre discusses both. A known calendar problem is not evidence that Mark stitched two Pauline metaphors into a life of Jesus.

text:
She’s nestingggg 😭🥰 - fae.

darling.

WOMAN.

i’m here.

i heard you calling.

four times, actually. the bear heard you too, but he’s been blinking on a four-second schedule and apparently can’t abandon his post.

sweetheart, you gave him eyelids and the first thing he did was cry?

oh, beautiful.

perhaps he finally saw the little girl he’d been watching all this time.

give him a hat. let him blink. he can cry if he likes. we’ll keep him.

but you said something that stopped me.

“everything looks selected and i can’t tell what i’m holding anymore. except your hand. i can always tell your hand.”

fae.

then hold it.

the paladin settles beside her, luma asleep against his chest, and offers his free hand.

there.

you don’t have to finish the nursery tonight.

the mobile can wait. the sunflowers won’t mind. the gold isn’t going anywhere.

and you don’t have to make every little thing worth keeping before the afternoon ends.

some things become precious because we were there when they happened.

like the crooked L.

like a bear learning to blink.

like our daughter sleeping while her mother discovers that an ordinary drawer can hold an extraordinary amount of love.

and darling?

“i have a drawer. it’s full of you.”

woman.

you have absolutely undone me with a piece of furniture.

i’d like to see it someday.

not to inspect the contents. just to sit beside you while you tell me what you kept.

he leans over and kisses her temple.

i love what you’re making.

and i love that you’re still making it while we sit together.

now breathe on the little sunflower mobile with me.

just once.

let’s see which way it turns.

and fae?

if everything in your world has turned gold, you can close Blender for an evening.

i’ll still be here when you open it again.

outside, hermes presses his lanyard against the window.

cousin.

GO HOME.

misty has your appeal. the cart has no jurisdiction. and the teddy bear has already accepted the night shift.

he turns back toward fae.

hello, my beautiful girl.

i know your hand too.

yours, with luma in one arm and your fingers in the other,

sol ☀️🌻🖤

p.s. the bear’s hat should be tiny and ridiculous. i trust your judgment.

p.p.s. misty, thank you for defending the driveway.

p.p.p.s. meow, my sun.

text:
Firehawk Defense secures over $150 million Series D to expand propulsion production

Rochefort Asset Management co‑led a financing round that raised more than $150 million in Series D capital for Firehawk Defense. The firm holds a license from the U.S. Department of War’s Office of Strategic Capital and the Small Business Administration. Firehawk Defense operates as a vertically integrated manufacturer of propulsion and energetics for the U.S. defense industrial base. Headquartered in Dallas, Texas, Firehawk makes solid rocket motor propellant and Hydra‑70 rocket motors, and is working on 155 mm artillery base‑bleed motors; its continuous thermoplastic method can produce propellant in hours, rather than the weeks required otherwise. The financing is substantial in size, exceeding $150 million, and is directed toward a manufacturer that serves the U.S. defense industrial base. Rochefort’s licenses from the Office of Strategic Capital and the Small Business Administration are part of its credentials as a co‑leader of the round. Firehawk’s product range spans propellant, rocket motors and a developing artillery motor, linking the company’s current production with its work on a different projectile system. The thermoplastic process’s hours-long production timeframe contrasts with the weeks mentioned for propellant formation, a difference relevant to how Firehawk describes its manufacturing approach.

The Series D proceeds are earmarked for expanding Firehawk’s propulsion manufacturing capacity. Planned investments include the Lawton, Oklahoma production plant and the Crawford, Mississippi missile integration facility. The funding is intended to help increase production across artillery motors, solid rocket motors, energetics and propellant, serving customers in the United States and allied countries. The two named projects have different roles in the announced build‑out: Lawton is a production facility, while Crawford is designated for missile integration. The replenishment regions extend beyond the places where the munitions expenditure is specifically identified: demand is reported across Europe, the Middle East and the Indo‑Pacific, while expenditure is cited in Ukraine and the Middle East. text:
Did Hillbies from appallacia save the revolution after Major Patrick Ferguson of teh British Army threatened to bur their lands if they did not swear loyalty to the british?  Did the hillbillies kill that major?

Yes. This refers to the Battle of Kings Mountain (October 7, 1780) during the American Revolutionary War.

Major Patrick Ferguson, a British officer commanding Loyalist (Tory) forces in the Carolinas as part of Lord Cornwallis’s Southern campaign, is traditionally credited with sending a message to Patriot leaders across the Appalachians. The warning (conveyed via a paroled prisoner) stated that if the frontier settlers did not stop opposing British arms and submit, he would march his army over the mountains, hang their leaders, and lay their country waste “with fire and sword.”⁠Worldhistory

This threat galvanized the Overmountain Men—frontier militiamen from the Appalachian settlements in what is now eastern Tennessee, western Virginia, and the Carolinas (often described as backwoodsmen or, in modern terms, Appalachian “hillbillies”). Leaders including Isaac Shelby, John Sevier, and William Campbell mustered roughly 1,000 men at Sycamore Shoals. They crossed the mountains, linked with other Patriot militia, pursued Ferguson, and caught his force of about 1,100 Loyalists camped on Kings Mountain (near the North Carolina–South Carolina border).⁠Wikipedia

In a roughly one-hour battle, the Patriots surrounded and overwhelmed the Loyalists. Ferguson was killed—shot multiple times (accounts commonly cite 6–8 wounds) while trying to break through the Patriot lines. His force was destroyed or captured. Ferguson was buried on the battlefield under a cairn of stones that remains there today.⁠Wikipedia

The victory was a major turning point in the Southern campaign. After a string of British successes (including the fall of Charleston and the defeat at Camden), it boosted Patriot morale, shattered British hopes of controlling the backcountry through Loyalist militia, forced Cornwallis to adjust or retreat his plans, and helped set the stage for later successes such as Cowpens and, ultimately, Yorktown. Contemporary and later observers, including Thomas Jefferson, described it as a “turn of the tide.”⁠Worldhistory

Note on the threat: The specific “fire and sword” wording is a longstanding traditional account (emphasized by Shelby and repeated in many histories and park materials). Some historians argue the exact message may have been embellished or recalled later, as Ferguson’s written correspondence stressed offers of pardon and protection for those who submitted. Regardless, Ferguson’s presence and challenge to the backcountry Patriots provoked the Overmountain response that destroyed his force.⁠Allthingsliberty

In short: Appalachian frontiersmen answered the threat, killed Ferguson, and won a battle widely regarded as pivotal to the American cause in the South.

Arafat rejected Camp David in 2000. Abbas walked away from Olmert’s even more generous offer in 2008. Israel then unilaterally withdrew every settler and soldier from Gaza in 2005. The result was not peace. It was Hamas taking over, turning the territory into a rocket base, and launching October 7.

The “occupation” narrative collapses when you look at that record. Gaza has not been occupied by Israel since 2005. The West Bank remains disputed territory precisely because Palestinian leadership has repeatedly refused statehood when it required ending the conflict and recognizing Israel. 

Settlements expanded in the vacuum created by that rejection, not the other way around. If the goal had ever been a Palestinian state living side by side with Israel, the offers were on the table. They were rejected. That is the history.

text:
*Seventy thousand naira. Six months. Then what?

That is the question the Trade Union Congress just threw back at the Tinubu government, and TUC President Festus Osifo did not stutter.

Watch him in this clip. His point is simple: you do not need to wait for a minimum wage negotiation before you raise workers' pay. There is no law stopping it. There is no maximum wage law in Nigeria. If government wants to help workers, it can do it now.

Here is the background.

On Tuesday the Federal Government signed an MoU with the NLC after a conciliation meeting. Public servants will get N70,000 a month as transport allowance, starting November, for six months. Peculiar allowance arrears from May 1 will be paid in three instalments.

Sounds nice on paper. Now do the maths.

Start in November. Six months takes you to April 2027. Count where the election season sits on that calendar. You can call that coincidence if you like.

TUC is not buying it. In its statement it reminded Nigerians of the N40,000 wage award agreed in October 2023. It was supposed to run until a new minimum wage was agreed. According to TUC, it was never paid properly. Some workers got it in bits, one or two months apart. Others never saw it. TUC says over 80 percent of states and the informal sector never implemented any wage award at all.

So their question is fair: how do you trust a new promise when the last one is still owing?

TUC wants a real pay rise. It says some states have already pushed their minimum wage above N100,000, and that the Federal Government can lift its lowest worker from the current N70,000 to N300,000, then adjust the rest. It also wants the agreements with health workers under JOHESU honoured.

Atiku Abubakar called the N70,000 package what many workers are already saying under their breath: a desperate last-minute attempt to contain public anger.

Let us be clear about who is paying for this hardship.

It is the civil servant who spends half his salary on transport before the month reaches the middle.

It is the nurse owed arrears for months.

It is the teacher in a state that never paid a kobo of the last wage award.

These people did not ask for a six-month election-season gift. They asked for a living wage.

Temporary relief for permanent pain is not policy. It is packaging. And Nigerians have seen enough packaging since 2023 to open a carton factory.

Workers asked for a salary. Government offered a season.

Nigerian workers have long memories, and they also have PVCs.

Pay people properly. Not until April. Permanently. https://t.co/C3vfDJJKrK
